### Current behavior:

We've had huge performance problems with cypress since 3.4.1. After 3.4.1 cypress went unusably slow. Then in 4.2.0 suddenly it was fast again.. but after 4.4.1 it went a little slower, on the latest release its double the time and on v5 it just times out. In all cases the performance problems could not be reproduced locally, only on our azure windows builds.

I've been trying to identify the problem and trying different solutions ;- it seems that windows, low hardware build servers aggrevate the performance. e.g.

v4.4.1 - 2 v cpu's, 8gb ram - 24min
v4.4.1 - 4 v cpu's, 8gb ram - 19min
v5 - 2 v cpu's 8gb ram - times out after 50mins
v5 - 4 v cpu's, 8gb ram - 23min

Note that 2 virtual cpu's, 8gb ram is the normal build machine for public azure devops.

So on a faster machine its only 20% slower. On a slow machine we just get lots of problems.

The cpu logs indicate that the "cypress" process is using by far the most amount of cpu and it seems from the logs like network requests are the main cause of slowness.

I tried a few hacks:
* I tried disabling the cache clear - but I couldn't get it to work, even commenting out the cache clear in the electron file and disabling the profile cleaner util
* I had an idea to disable the proxy only for certain requests by specifying a pac script instead of a proxy in electron.js - then sending the main page and __ cypress request to the proxy and everything else direct - If something like this could be made to work I think it would offer a significant performance boost. However I couldn't get electron to use the pac script correctly, either encoded as a data uri or a web request.

My theory is that the proxy uses request and pipe and that something about it isn;t optimal on slower machines. I read a bit about setting highWatermark settings etc. to optimize piping a request to a response - but I'm a bit out of my debt. I see a number of other issues about network performance and there might be improvements here.

btw modifyObstructiveCode is false.

I'll upload two debug logs of the same spec and the same version of cypress on 2cpu's and 4 cpu's showing it being very slow.

### Desired behavior:

No performance degradation.

### Test code to reproduce

I think I should be able to put together a repo of our project - will this be valuable? I guess I can see if I can reproduce problems on app vejor? If all I can reproduce on public servers is a 20% degradation is that expected? Its going to be alot of effort to put it together so I'd like to hear if its helpful first.

title: Cypress installs critical security vulnerabilities, preventing it from running in CI pipeline
body:
Hey folks,

I've been trying hard to integrate Cypress into our our CI pipeline. We deploy our services in docker containers and  then analyze the resulting image against a list of know vulnerabilities. Critical vulnerabilities fail the build, well before we ever get to run the end-to-end tests. I suspect this applies to a lot of folks out there who would want to use Cypress in their CI pipeline Unfortunately, Cypress is installing a module with a critical vulnerability (in the `server` package) that has been known since 2015: the `tar@0.1.20` module. See https://www.npmjs.com/advisories/57. As a result, we can't currently use Cypress in our CI pipeline

I dug a little into this and realized that the dependency is brought in by `node-webkit-updater`, a defunct project that you have forked. Here's the offending line: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/9a32d226bbd2fabf27266a8d143b1a71e6eb2826/packages/server/package.json#L92

I should note that Cypress is also bringing in a number of other vulnerabilities. Currently, those aren't an issue for us because we are only failing on critical vulnerabilities, but they may be for other people with stricter security requirements. Here's the list:
High 
* `qs@5.1.0`: also introduced by `node-webkit-updater` ([advisory](https://www.npmjs.com/advisories/1469))
* `minimatch@2.0.10`: introduced by `babel-core` [(advisory)](https://www.npmjs.com/advisories/118)
* `http-proxy@1.18.0`: ([advisory](https://www.npmjs.com/advisories/1486))

Moderate:
* `tunnel-agent@0.4.3`: also introduced by `node-webkit-updater` ([advisory](https://www.npmjs.com/advisories/598))
* `hoek@2.16.3`: also introduced by `node-webkit-updater` ([advisory](https://www.npmjs.com/advisories/566))

### Current behavior:
Installing Cypress installs a version of `tar` below `2.0.0`

### Desired behavior:
Installing Cypress should not install a version of `tar` below `2.0.0`

### Test code to reproduce
Pull this repo, install dependencies with `yarn`, and then run `yarn why tar`. Result should indicate that `tar@0.1.20` was installed:
```
...
=> Found "tar.gz#tar@0.1.20"
info This module exists because "_project_#@packages#server#node-webkit-updater#tar.gz" depends on it.
info Disk size without dependencies: "220KB"
info Disk size with unique dependencies: "468KB"
info Disk size with transitive dependencies: "956KB"
info Number of shared dependencies: 17
...
``` 

### Versions
At least `14.7.1`

title: Custom timeouts are ignored on retry attempts.
body:
### Current behaviour:

Given the following sample spec:
```js
it('does very little', function () {
  cy.get('#notInTheDOM', {timeout: 15000}).should('exist')
})
```
When you first launch this spec file from the runner, the 15s timeout elapses before the test fails. If you then click retry (or edit the spec file, triggering an automatic retry) the test fails after just 3-4s

### Desired behaviour:

The specified custom timeout should be respected on retry.

### Test code to reproduce

Please see above.

### Versions

Cypress 4.10-4.12, CentOS8, and Chrome 83

title: Can't access alias via 'this.value' syntax
body:
### Current behavior:

I am trying to count founded 'button' elements on a page and get the result via two syntax constructions: '@value' and 'this.value':

```js
describe('page', () => {
  it('two aliases', function() {
    cy.visit('https://example.cypress.io')
    cy.get('h2')
        .its('length')
        .as('num');
    cy.get('@num').then(num => cy.log(`num via '@num' is: ${num}`))
    cy.log(`num via 'this' is: ${this.num}`)
  })
})
```
An output is a little unclear for me:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61494460/90665224-6ce07100-e254-11ea-915f-4b192d3a53aa.png)

### Desired behavior:

I expect that I can access the value both ways:  via '@value' and via 'this.value'. Just like in documentation:
https://docs.cypress.io/guides/core-concepts/variables-and-aliases.html#Sharing-Context
```js
beforeEach(() => {
  // alias the $btn.text() as 'text'
  cy.get('button').invoke('text').as('text')
})

it('has access to text', function () {
  this.text // is now available
})
```

### Test code to reproduce

https://github.com/denis-domanskii/cypress-test-tiny-8349

### Versions
OS: Mac 10.15.5
Browser: Chrome 84
Cypress: 4.1.0, 5.0.0

title: Nesting hooks within other hooks causes the test to never finish (runs forever)
fix: remove offscreen mode from headless Electron windows
body:
* Closes #7930

### User facing changelog
Switch off offscreen rendering which can cause a 8x performance slowdown for headless electron runs on slow computers. Problem last introduced in cypress 4.5.0.

### Additional details
Offscreen rendering:
https://www.electronjs.org/docs/tutorial/offscreen-rendering

passes every frame to a 'paint' event, which cypress does not listen too.

In electron 8.2.1 it was fixed and switched back on, so when cypress upgraded from 8.2.0 to 8.2.3, it caused a performance regression.

The performance regression on slow computers is about 8x slower. On fast computers you don't see a difference - I expect the multi-process nature of electron and cypress means that more cores mitigate the extra cpu needed.

The option was introduced here, 3 years ago:
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/commit/5bde862d9122697dbab48156770950d4b58096f1

title: Remove .then wrap from return value of Cypress.Blob.base64StringToBlob
body:
<!-- Is this a question? Questions WILL BE CLOSED. Ask in our chat https://on.cypress.io/chat  -->

### Current behavior:
We added a `.then` method to the return value of `Cypress.Blob.base64StringToBlob` so we could improve the error message when a user attempts to use its old promise-returning API (see [this comment](https://github.com/abramenal/cypress-file-upload/pull/215#issuecomment-677520674)). This causes methods like `Promise.resolve` and `Promise.try` to think the return value is a `thenable`, invoking the `.then` and throwing our error. This makes it [difficult to add backwards compatibility](https://github.com/abramenal/cypress-file-upload/pull/215) without an ugly hack.

### Desired behavior:
We shouldn't add on the `.then` method so that the return value is not mistaken for a promise-returning value. This may just result in a `.then is not a function` error when using the old API, but that might not be so bad.

### Test code to reproduce
```javascript
it('uses Cypress.Blob.base64StringToBlob', () => {
  return Cypress.Promise.resolve(Cypress.Blob.base64StringToBlob(btoa('foo')))
})
```

title: fix: Remove error message wrapping of Cypress.Blob return values
body:
<!-- 
Thanks for contributing!
Read our contribution guidelines here: 
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
-->

<!-- Example: "Closes #1234" -->

- Closes #8365 

### User facing changelog

- Cypress no longer adds a `.then` method to the return value of `Cypress.Blob` methods for the sake of a custom error message. Fixes an issue where those return values were mistaken for promises and unintentionally trigger the custom error.

### Additional details

There is no longer a custom error message for using the old promise-returning API of Blob methods, but it makes it easier to wrap those methods for backwards compatibility. I think this an okay compromise.

### How has the user experience changed?

Before, this would incorrectly error:

```javascript
Cypress.Promise.resolve(Cypress.Blob.base64StringToBlob(btoa('foo'))
// => throws error 'base64StringToBlob() no longer returns a Promise. Update the use of base64StringToBlob() to expect a returned Blob'
```

Now it does not error:

```javascript
Cypress.Promise.resolve(Cypress.Blob.base64StringToBlob(btoa('foo'))
// => returns promise with base64 value
```

The error experience of using `.then` has degraded a bit:

Before:

```javascript
Cypress.Blob.base64StringToBlob(btoa('foo').then(() => {})
// => throws error 'base64StringToBlob() no longer returns a Promise. Update the use of base64StringToBlob() to expect a returned Blob'
```

After:

```javascript
Cypress.Blob.base64StringToBlob(btoa('foo').then(() => {})
// => throws error '.then is not a function'
```

title: fix: Resolve tsconfig.json for plugins file from the plugins directory
body:
<!-- 
Thanks for contributing!
Read our contribution guidelines here: 
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
-->

<!-- Example: "Closes #1234" -->

- Closes #8359

### User facing changelog

- Cypress now resolves and loads `tsconfig.json` for TypeScript projects starting from the `plugins` directory

### Additional details

`ts-node` resolves the `tsconfig.json` starting from the current working directory (`cwd`) by default. This means using `cypress/tsconfig.json` won't work to specify TypeScript config for Cypress.

In reality, this only affected a couple options in `tsconfig.json` because only a couple options (e.g. "esModuleInterop", "downlevelIteration") affect the runtime. Any non-runtime options would take affect in a user's IDE because it would resolve the `tsconfig.json` starting from the directory of the opened file.

This PR changes it so `ts-node` will now start looking for the `tsconfig.json` from the plugins directory. That is `cypress/plugins` by default or the `dirname` of the plugins file path if a custom one is provided. For example, if the "pluginsFile" is set to `<project root>/some/other/path/to/plugins.js`, it will start looking in `<project root>/some/other/path/to`.

### How has the user experience changed?

Users will now see runtime options in `cypress/tsconfig.json` take effect, whereas before they were ignored.

title: cy.type sometimes fails to type without causing test failure
body:
In some cases when interacting with an element which has recently become interactable, `cy.type()` will fail to type into an element, or only partially type, even after the element has been found. No error is shown in the cypress log. 

This behavior was observed specifically on a form modal which was hidden and revealed with a fade-in effect. If `cy.wait()` is called to give the modal longer to fade in or `{force:true}` is added to the `cy.type` options, this error does not occur. 

Looking at the logs and the console output cypress provides, it appears that the target of the keydown events is changing to the previously targeted element for some reason:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/55517627/90945826-303f8180-e3dc-11ea-8755-760570fb7a1c.png)

Unfortunately this does not occur with every page load (I tried but wasn't able to isolate the specific event that is causing the element to lose focus), but I was able to observe it fairly frequently when the test is rerun enough times (it seemed to occur more often when the window fully reloaded so the cache was emptied as well).

Test code:
```js
cy.visit('https://www.previewsite.adpearance.com/inventory/437')

cy.get('[aria-controls="RequestQuoteForm"]')
    .first()
    .click()
	   
cy.get('#RequestQuoteForm')
    .should('be.visible') 
    .within(($contactModal) => {
         cy.get('input[name="person.firstName"]').type('Test') 
         cy.get('input[name="person.lastName"]').type('Test') 
    }
```

Desired behavior: If this is an issue with the type command, it should be updated so it does not lose focus. If the type command is working as intended and something in the site code is causing the type command to lose focus, ideally this should result in some kind of error from the type command.

### Versions

Cypress 5.0.0
Windows 10
Chrome 84.0.4147.135 (bundled)

Modal is powered by Foundation 6 Reveal : https://get.foundation/sites/docs/reveal.html`

title: Experimental fetch polyfill has different prototype than webpage
body:
### Current behavior:

Results from fetch calls when using `experimentalFetchPolyfill` have a different prototype than `Object.prototype` in the browser context. This breaks the `isPlainObject` check in Mobx: https://github.com/mobxjs/mobx/blob/6ec6499fb8b55a17fe65f42b14d1188fd7fa1ba1/src/utils/utils.ts#L85

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47303296/91098257-28c3e680-e62f-11ea-8beb-8256a23c54da.png)

### Desired behavior:

When running in the browser without Cypress, we can see that the fetch response behaves correctly:

```js
fetch('/test')
  .then(response => response.json())
  .then(data => Object.getPrototypeOf(data) === Object.prototype); // this evaluates to true in the browser, false in cypress
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47303296/91098370-56a92b00-e62f-11ea-85ef-d423f4a01e72.png)

### Test code to reproduce

https://github.com/bhgsbatista/cypress_fetch_prototype

feat: support beforeinput event.
body:
* Closes #7088
* Dependent on #8255. Firefox tests will fail until it's done.

### User facing changelog
* Support `beforeinput` event to solve slate.js issue.

### Additional details
#### Why was this change necessary?
Cypress cannot be used to test some applications that use `beforeinput` events like slate.js

#### What is affected by this change?
N/A

#### Any implementation details to explain?
* slatejs uses `inputType` to decide what to do. So, I had to decide it based on the key combo and [the spec](https://rawgit.com/w3c/input-events/v1/index.html#interface-InputEvent-Attributes).
* `noUpdate` option had to be introduced to `cy.type()`. Because slatejs handles its own state and the text updated by Cypress causes errors. 
* I had to use [the plaintext example.](https://www.slatejs.org/examples/plaintext) Because slatejs uses React and creating a webpack bundle is big.
* Firefox test will fail. Because this PR needs the dispatching event fix code in #8255.

### How has the user experience changed?
You can test slatejs with Cypress.

title: Video and screenshot recording consumes way too much CPU, causing Cypress to freeze.
body: I ran into a problem recently where Cypress began freezing towards the end of my tests. The problem was even worse when I upgraded to Cypress@5.0. Also, others seemed to run into the same exact problem on the gitter chat. ![Screen Shot 2020-08-26 at 3 17 05 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26511068/91362459-62bbf680-e7af-11ea-9a00-437f7bf6fb6d.png) Obviously that is not enough information on its own, so with the help of my team, we did a little digging and discovered that the process responsible for video and screenshot upload would shoot up to over 500% of CPU usage. There is absolutely no reason for it to be consuming that much CPU. That feature specifically caused cypress to freeze. When I turned off video and screenshot recording, my tests passed with flying colors, Cypress didn't freeze, and not a single process shot up to 500% CPU usage. Keep in mind, I have over 20 specs in my tests. This is a fairly large application I'm working with. So for small apps, you probably won't have Cypress freezing on you. With that said, process to record videos and screenshots should still not be consuming that much CPU, and I believe it's something you guys should look into.

Cypress can't locate Chrome 85 exe in Windows
body:
### Current behavior:
```cypress open``` does not show Chrome as a browser option. This occured after update to Chrome 85, released 2020-08-25.

I'm pretty sure this comes down to how Cypress is checking for the browser. While debugging, I came across a claim that cypress uses the following line to detect Chrome:

```
wmic datafile where name="C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" get Version /value
```

Feature: Add global config option for including shadow DOM in commands
body:
<!-- Is this a question? Questions WILL BE CLOSED. Ask in our chat https://on.cypress.io/chat  -->

### Current behavior:

Currently, to enable shadow dom support, it's necessary to pass `includeShadowDom` into a command that supports it every time it's used.

```javascript
cy.get('.in-shadow-dom', { includeShadowDom: true })
cy.get('.shadow-root').find('.in-shadow-dom', { includeShadowDom: true })
```

### Desired behavior:

Enable configuring shadow dom inclusion globally, per-suite, per-test, or programmatically. Still need to decide on a name for it.

_cypress.json_

Turns on inclusion behavior for all tests

```json
{
  "includeShadowDom": true
}
```

_Per Suite_

Turns on inclusion behavior for all tests and commands within the suite

```javascript
describe('shadow dom tests', { includeShadowDom: true }, () => {
  it(...)
  it(...)
})
```

_Per Test_

Turns on inclusion behavior for all commands within the test

```javascript
it('shadow dom tests', { includeShadowDom: true }, () => {
  cy.get(...)
  cy.get(...).find(...)
})
```

_Programmatically_

Turns on inclusion behavior conditionally based on where it's used (before, beforeEach, etc)

```javascript
before(() => {
  Cypress.config('includeShadowDom', true)
})
```

title: Allow the user env variable of `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=''` (an empty string) to take precedence over npm config
body:
<!-- Is this a question? Questions WILL BE CLOSED. Ask in our chat https://on.cypress.io/chat  -->

### Current behavior:

<!-- A description including screenshots, stack traces, DEBUG logs, etc -->
A user env variable of `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=''` (an empty string) cannot override the npm config.

We want to run cypress only in CI, so we put a `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=0` in `PROJECT/.npmrc` to avoid all our developers to download the cypress binary, which is a big cost considering our poor network. And then add a user env variable in CI to let it do download. Since cypress releases frequently, a fixed version like `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=5.1.0` is not a good approach. But `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=''` is not working too.

### Desired behavior:

<!-- A clear description of what you want to happen -->
Allow the user env variable of `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=''` to take precedence over npm config. Or add a new keyword of `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=auto` or something like that.

### Test code to reproduce

<!-- If we cannot fully run the tests as provided the issue WILL BE CLOSED -->
<!-- Issues without a reproducible example WILL BE CLOSED -->

<!-- You can fork https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-test-tiny repo, set up a failing test, then link to your fork -->

1. Add `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=0` in a project's `.npmrc` (or `~/.npmrc`)
2. Add `export CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=''` in shell profile (e.g. `~/.bash_profile`)
3. Run `npm install cypress`

### Possible fix

In https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/lib/util.js#L473

```js
const envVar = process.env[varName]
// Instead of `if (envVar)`, prefer:
if (varName in process.env) {
  result = envVar
}
```

Or we can add an extra option of `allowEmptyVar` for `getEnv` to avoid potential breaking for all other env variables.

### Versions

<!-- Cypress, operating system, browser -->
Cypress: 5.1.0
Operation systems: Mac OS 10.15, CentOS 7

title: cy.route2 documentation: delay/throttle function examples not right?

In the documentation for `cy.route2` there's [this example](https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/route2.html#Simulate-delay) of the `delay` function:

```
cy.route2('/users', (req) => {
  req.delay(200)
})
```

When I tried that I got a compilation error: `Property 'delay' does not exist on 'InocmingHttpRequest'`. From looking at the code, looks like it's on `IncomingHttpResponse`, not on the request itself.

Same thing applies to the `throttle` function. The `redirect` one does seem to compile OK though.

There's a couple of other minor issues too (let me know if you want separate issues logged for these):
1. [One of the code snippets](https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/route2.html#Making-multiple-requests-to-the-same-route) talks about `beetle` items in a response - it's not really clear what this is referring to.
2. The section about multiple requests isn't quite clear in terms of how to stub a single route, and give it a different response every time it's called (particularly required for GraphQL endpoints). For example, can you call `cy.route2` multiple times in a test, to set up a different way to handle the call each time?

title: Add API for cy.intercept() to only reply to the first N requests
body:
<!-- Is this a question? Questions WILL BE CLOSED. Ask in our chat https://on.cypress.io/chat  -->

### Current behavior:
To change the response for a route over time, currently, the user must implement counting themselves:

```js
      let k = 0;
      cy.intercept('/favorite-fruits', (req) => {
        k += 1
        switch (k) {
          case 1:
            return req.reply(['apples 🍎'])
          case 2:
            return req.reply(['grapes 🍇'])
          case 3:
            return req.reply(['kiwi 🥝'])
          default:
            return
        }
      })
```

### Desired behavior:
There is an API for the user to specify the number of times to use a route's handler. Something like this:

```js
cy.intercept({ url: '/favorite-fruits', times: 1 }, ['apples 🍎'])
cy.intercept({ url: '/favorite-fruits', times: 1 }, ['grapes 🍇'])
cy.intercept({ url: '/favorite-fruits', times: 1 }, ['kiwi 🥝'])
```

feat: Print folder sizes with cypress cache list command.
body:
* Closes #6404

### User facing changelog
You can list the cypress cache folder sizes with `cypress cache list --size` command. 

I added `--size` as an option here because it makes command too slow. -> More about the implementation details below. 

### Additional details
#### Why was this change necessary?
Some users might want to check the size of cypress cache folders. 

#### What is affected by this change?
N/A

#### Any implementation details to explain?
1. At first, I used [`get-folder-size`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/get-folder-size) library. But it is dependent on `tiny-each-async` and `gar`. Maybe because of them, it slows down when I used over 10 cypress caches. And it didn't use the promise. So, I decided to create our own get-folder-size.
1. And this `getFolderSize` function recursively loops the folder and add the sizes of the files. Because of that, it's really slow. That's why I added it as `--size` option.
1. Finally, `getFolderSize` returns actual folder size, not the allocated disk space.

### How has the user experience changed?
![Screenshot from 2020-09-16 14-42-33](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8130013/93296828-fde24200-f82a-11ea-821e-22b78bd52532.png)

title: Workflow proposal to make tests extremely easy to write and maintain
body:
This is a draft. I don't have time now to write a full specification. I will improve the specification of this ticket if there is enough interest.

This is my attempt to make tests extremely easy to write and maintain. Debugging is already pretty good with cypress.
The proposed workflow is different way of working with tests but please hear me out.

The proposed workflow:
- Create an new test case in the UI and give it a name
- Record user interactions in the browser and store them either as reusable actions or directly in the test case
- You can name sequences of actions such as "login", "go to profile", "go to user settings" etc.
- One action can call other actions
- When the login page changes, changing the login action will fix all test cases that depend on login action
- This makes composing tests easy and allows re-usability which makes tests easily maintainable
- Those actions will be stored as data and not as code to allow editing them later (maybe standardized json file format)
- You can also write actions manually in a text-area which highlights the code and does syntax checking
- Add simple assertions to actions by
  - right click on selected text and click "assert presence of this text"
  - right click on any element and click "assert presence of element"; maybe some settings pop-up allows finer tuning of the assertion
- Of course instead of right click a modifier key can be used (Ctrl, Alt etc.)
- If you need to write a complex assertion that require code you can add a manual assertion and paste the assertion code in a text-area which highlights the code and does syntax checking
- Cypress can read this json file and execute it. Looping through all the test groups, test cases, actions and executing them calling the cy API
- The UI allows replaying a test case up to any breakpoint
- You can insert or overwrite user interactions at breakpoint in the action sequence by recording in insert or overwrite mode
- The json file can be comitted in git the diff of the file can be read
- You can use multiple json files when they get too big
- One json file can include another one to simplify sharing of actions
- You have a working history of the file using Ctrl + Z etc.

Example test case:
- login (action)
  - go to login page
  - put email
  - put password
  - click submit
- remove user photo (action)
  - go to profile page
  - click on remove photo
  - click submit
- go to profile page
- assert photo is not present

Actions like "login" and "remove user photo" can be reused.

What are your thoughts on this? Why this is not the way we do testing today?
Don't get me wrong you will still need to write code for some assertions and for simulating some interactions but this solution does not force you to write code if you don't have to.

cc: @flotwig @chrisbreiding

title: Cannot pass config-file option to parseRunArguments
body:
### Current behavior:
When passing `--config-file cypress.json` as part of the command line arguments to parseRunArguments, cypress fails with the following error:
```
The "path" argument must be of type string. Received type boolean
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE] [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "path" argument must be of type string. Received type boolean
```

### Desired behavior:
The --config-file argument should be properly parsed also when using the node module API.

### Test code to reproduce
```javascript
const cypress = require('cypress');
async function reproduceError() {
  const runOptions = await cypress.cli.parseRunArguments(['cypress', 'run', '--config-file', 'cypress.json']);
  const results = await cypress.run(runOptions);
}
reproduceError();
```

### Versions
Cypress 5.2.0
Windows 10

### Analysis
With debugging it is clear where the issue appears:
```
  cypress:cli:cli parsing args: [ null, null, 'run', '--config-file=myConfigFile.json' ] +3ms
  ...
  cypress:cli parsed cli options { configFile: 'myConfigFile.json' } +0ms
  cypress:cli:cli parsed options { configFile: 'myConfigFile.json' } +46ms
  cypress:cli:cli casted options { configFile: true } +1ms
```
`
Looking through the code, there is a coercion function applied to the configFile property when parsing arguments, since this argument may be a string or false. However, the coercion function always returns a boolean
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/ef2363ea7837cf55f88a4ba59615ad2b7d0b3b71/cli/lib/cli.js#L25-L27

### Suggested fix
If the coercion function is replaced with
```javascript
const coerceFalse = (arg) => { 
   return arg !== 'false' ? arg : false;
} 
```
it should work as expected.

title: "should" using a callback does change the subject
body:
### Current behavior:

On version 4.11.0 but seens also on some previous versions.

```js
cy.get("#something")
    .should($el => null)
    .click();
```

Will fail complaining that click was called not on a DOM element:

```
CypressError: `cy.click()` failed because it requires a DOM element.

The subject received was:

  > `Object{3}`

The previous command that ran was:

  > `cy.should()`

      at ensureElement (http://localhost:4200/__cypress/runner/cypress_runner.js:159904:24)
      at validateType (http://localhost:4200/__cypress/runner/cypress_runner.js:159728:16)
      at Object.ensureSubjectByType (http://localhost:4200/__cypress/runner/cypress_runner.js:159770:11)
      at pushSubjectAndValidate (http://localhost:4200/__cypress/runner/cypress_runner.js:167481:15)
      at Context.<anonymous> (http://localhost:4200/__cypress/runner/cypress_runner.js:167809:18)
```

The "Object{3}" above is a jquery object.

This is caused by two problems:
1. "should" with a callback is documented not to change the subject, but looks like it wraps it in jquery object (to pass it as a parameter) and from that moment on the subject is the jquery object, so it is changed
2. "click" does not handle properly a jquery object as a subject (?), the isElement test fails and throws the exception.

### Desired behavior:

The above lines should work, or be documented as not working.

See the three lines above.

4.11.0 electron linux

title: Proposal: A cypress command to add a class to the test reporter
body: ### Current behavior I am using BDD via [cypress-cucumber](https://github.com/TheBrainFamily/cypress-cucumber-preprocessor). This means I am writing a lot of feature files before I start writing tests. Therefore, when I do start writing tests I have a lot of passing tests that are empty. Initially, like others, I thought some kind of "ToDo" command that is like "skip" would work. ("Skip" doesn't solve the problem because skipping a test does not alert you to an empty test.) I would like to propose another option. ### Desired behavior If we had a command like: `cy.addReporterClass('my-todo')` we could then have a set of custom classes that could get added to the test reporter. This then is not specifically about "ToDo" but could be anything like 'my-fix-this-test' or 'my-wip' or whatever. In my spec I could then do something like: Then(`The name should be {string}`, (name) => { cy.addReporterClass('my-todo') }) Which would pass the test and display it with my custom css. ### Test code to reproduce Using Chrome tools I did this as a rough proof of concept. I added these classes to the cypress_runner.css file: .my-todo { color:orange !important; } .my-todo::before { content: "[ToDo] "; } Then manually added the class to these elements in the reporter: `expected Jane to equal Jane` and `Start this apppassed` giving this example: ![Greenshot 2020-09-24 09 25 50](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37637590/94084356-a8202200-fe48-11ea-9f1e-eb637fc7c1ac.png) The thing to note about this proposal is that it would allow an unlimited number of custom classes to be used (even multiple / compounding classes) without touching the test flow itself. One could still use "skip" and tagging if one wanted to without losing the knowledge that the test was empty or needed work or was possibly redundant, etc. eg The `cy.addReporterClass('my-redundant')` could be added to a written passing test as a note that yes, we have a test here but maybe we do not need it any longer (for example). The semantics and visuals of the classes are then up to the user so are not deterministic like "skip" or "todo" is. We would also need an entry in `cypress.json` to point to our custom css file. What do you think? Thanks, Murray PS: This could possibly be done with a plugin (which is probably beyond me to do) but my thinking is this could be fantastic core functionality.

body:
<!-- Is this a question? Questions WILL BE CLOSED. Ask in our chat https://on.cypress.io/chat  -->

### Current behavior
Currently if `log` is called (internally within a cypress command or by `cy.log`) all images which are in the process of loading will reload. On some pages this is generating so many network calls that xhr requests are getting stalled to the point that all tests time out.

I think this occurs when we clone the body element here https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/packages/driver/src/cy/snapshots.js#L155 

On some internal pages we have many XHR requests (which generate many logs) and many larger images. The reloading behavior is to the point that our tests time out due to requires xhr/fetch calls getting stuck behind all the images.

### Desired behavior
Calling cy.log shouldn't trigger a reloading of all images

### Test code to reproduce
Use this snippet with cy.open and disable cache off:

```js
    cy.visit('https://github.com/');
    Array(15).fill().forEach(() => {
      cy.log('Test log')
      cy.wait(100);
    })
```

Using the above there were 1762 image requests when loading github homepage. Each image was loaded 33 times

title: fix: within followed by should correctly changes the scope.
body:
* Closes #2106 * Closes #4672 * Closes #4757 * Closes #5183 These all 4 issues cover the same problem and this PR solves that. ### User facing changelog When a command is chained after `cy.within()` and `cy.get()` is called inside it, the scope was permanently changed. This PR solves this problem. ### Additional details #### Why was this change necessary? The command didn't work as the documentation says. #### What is affected by this change? Some codes that use this bug will be broken. Example below: ```html

My Blog Post

``` ```js cy.get(`article`).within(() => cy.get(`h1`)).should(`have.text`, `My Blog Post`); ``` This should fail because the `article` has text `\n My Blog Post \n`. #### Any implementation details to explain? When running tests, Cypress queues commands and runs them later. ```js cy.get('article').within(() => { cy.get('h1').should('contain.text', 'Blog') }) .should('have.class', 'post') ``` In the example above, Cypress creates a queue like below: ``` get('article') within should('have.class', 'post') ``` After running `within`, the queue becomes like below: ``` get('article') within get('h1', { withinSubject: 'article' }) should('contain.text', 'Blog') should('have.class', 'post') ``` Because `within` inserts commands inside the callback to the queue after itself. But the problem happens here. Because the code below generates the identical queue state. ```js cy.get('article').within(() => { cy.get('h1').should('contain.text', 'Blog').should('have.class', 'post') }) ``` And Cypress interprets that the code is written in that way. That's why the code failed. The solution is to insert the divider between the commands like below: ``` get('article') within get('h1', { withinSubject: 'article' }) should('contain.text', 'Blog') within-restore <= This is necessary. should('have.class', 'post') ``` And this PR inserts that internal command to the queue. ### How has the user experience changed? title: OpenSSL errors when cached SSL certificates are corrupted
body:
<!-- Is this a question? Questions WILL BE CLOSED. Ask in our chat https://on.cypress.io/chat  -->

### Current behavior

There is a race condition in `https-proxy` that can cause the CA store to become corrupted if multiple Cypress processes are sharing the same appdata directory simultaneously. This causes errors like the following when visiting HTTPS websites:

```
Error: error:0b000074:X.509 certificate routines:OPENSSL_internal:KEY_VALUES_MISMATCH
Error: error:0900006e:PEM routines:OPENSSL_internal:NO_START_LINE
```

And other errors relating to corrupt/mismatched private keys and SSL certificates.

### Desired behavior

The race condition is avoided, probably with the addition of a lockfile when generating/writing CA certificates.

Note:  Cypress is not generally designed to run as multiple processes sharing a home directory.

### Workaround (Linux-only)

A workaround is to set a different `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` environment variable for each Cypress process that is running. This will cause each process to have its own CA store, eliminating the possibility of a race condition.

Example:

```shell
# assuming these are somehow run simultaneously
XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/cyhome1 cypress run...
XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/cyhome2 cypress run...
```

This may have side-effects outside of just fixing this issue, but it is the only workaround for now.

title: fix: each followed by contains correctly changes the scope.
body:
* Closes #4921

### User facing changelog
When dual commands like `cy.contains()` is used `each()`, it didn't work properly. This PR solves this problem.

### Additional details
#### Why was this change necessary?
Unexpected behavior of `each()` and `contains()`.

#### What is affected by this change? 
Nothing

#### Any implementation details to explain?
This problem happened because `each()` didn't care about whether the command is called first or not.

Because of that, the code A was interpreted like Code B.

```js
// code A
cy.contains('New York')
cy.get('span').each(() => {})
cy.contains('New York')
```

```js
// code B
cy.contains('New York')
cy.get('span').each(() => {}).contains('New York')
```

### How has the user experience changed?
N/A

Update types for `Cypress.Chainable.task` to allow for parameterizing the task return type.

### Additional details
Previously, the return type of `task` would be determined by the previous subject's type. In this example:

```js
cy.task("task").then((val) => ...);
```

`val` is typed as `undefined` with no way to change it besides explicitly casting `val` inside the lambda function. This change supports specifying the type of `val` in a first-class way:

```js
// val now has type MyType
cy.task<MyType>("task").then((val) => ...);
```

### How has the user experience changed?
User experience has not changed -- developer experience is better!

title: Official Cypress 5.2.0 docker images (`cypress/browser`) contains >=1 security vulnerability (Debian-based)
body:
### Current behavior
- The official Cypress docker images (`cypress/browser`) contains >=1 security vulnerability (Debian-based)
- As a result, the images created in our CI pipeline (Azure DevOps based), that depend on `cypress/browser`, also contain the same security vulnerability (since `cypress/include` includes the `cypress/browser` because of the FROM command)
- Consequently, the custom Dockerfile that we use, that depends on `cypress/include`, also exhibits the same vulnerability
- The security vulnerabilities show up in Azure Security Center. We assume so far that the vulnerabilities are there for all.

### Desired behavior
- The official Cypress docker images (`cypress/browser`) *should not* contain several security vulnerabilities, especially since other Dockerfiles depend on the browser image, and it is not straight forward to control the contents of the (`cypress/browser`) image
- Similarly, the official Cypress docker images that depend on `cypress/browser` also contains security vulnerabilities (like `cypress/include`), or images that depend on `cypress/include` (we use our own Dockerfile that depends on `cypress/include`)
- *No* (derived) Cypress docker images *should* contain security vulnerabilities (you can check with Azure Security Center)
- Obviously, we would prefer not to have to combine Dockerfile contents, or maintain our own Dockerfiles, but the vulnerabilities were there for a while. In the end we wish-list that Cypress.io going forward try to avoid security vulnerabilities more swiftly.

### Vulnerabilities
**372894-Google Chrome Prior To 83.0.4103.116 Use After Free Vulnerability**
- Description: Google Chrome is a web browser for multiple platforms developed by Google.
- Affected by following vulnerability: CVE-2020-6509: Use after free in extensions.
- Affected Version: Prior to Google Chrome 83.0.4103.116
- Severity: High
- CVEs: CVE-2020-6509
- Links: http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2020-6509
- Vendor references: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2020/06/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_22.html

### Related Cypress.io issues:
- https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8771
- https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8772

### Version(s)
- [cypress/included:5.2.0](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-docker-images/blob/master/included/5.2.0) `FROM cypress/browsers:node12.18.0-chrome83-ff77`

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |

|[node-forge](https://togithub.com/digitalbazaar/forge) | dependencies | minor |[`0.9.0` -> `0.10.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/node-forge/0.9.0/0.10.0) |

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts
#### [CVE-2020-7720](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-7720)
The package node-forge before 0.10.0 is vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via the util.setPath function. Note: Version 0.10.0 is a breaking change removing the vulnerable functions.

- - -
### Release Notes
<details>
<summary>digitalbazaar/forge</summary>

### [`v0.10.0`](https://togithub.com/digitalbazaar/forge/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#​0100---2020-09-01)
[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/digitalbazaar/forge/compare/0.9.2...0.10.0)

##### Changed
*   **BREAKING**: Node.js 4 no longer supported. The code _may_ still work, and
    non-invasive patches to keep it working will be considered. However, more
    modern tools no longer support old Node.js versions making testing difficult.

##### Removed
*   **BREAKING**: Remove `util.getPath`, `util.setPath`, and `util.deletePath`.
    `util.setPath` had a potential prototype pollution security issue when used
    with unsafe inputs. These functions are not used by `forge` itself. They date
    from an early time when `forge` was targeted at providing general helper
    functions. The library direction changed to be more focused on cryptography.
    Many other excellent libraries are more suitable for general utilities. If
    you need a replacement for these functions, consier `get`, `set`, and `unset`
    from [lodash](https://lodash.com/). But also consider the potential similar
    security issues with those APIs.

<!--

<!-- Example: "Closes #1234" -->

* Closes https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8314
* Partially addresses https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/880

### User facing changelog
Remove usage of [node-webkit-updater](https://github.com/cypress-io/node-webkit-updater) which has multiple dependencies with vulnerabilities, including a critical one:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1497562/95657311-269ce500-0b14-11eb-8940-d71bccc3057b.png)

### Additional details
Cypress was using [node-webkit-updater](https://github.com/cypress-io/node-webkit-updater) kind of as a wrapper of the manifest. I rewrote the `updater`, replacing the entire class with two functions:

* `_getManifest`: given a machine it, it fetches and returns the [manifest that contains the latest version](https://download.cypress.io/desktop.json). I prefixed it with `_` to indicate it's private, since I exposed it to write a unit test
* `check`: same contract as old `Updater.check` (clients don't need to be updated). It gets the machine id, calls `_getManifest` to fetch the manifest and then compares the local version with the manifest's version. If there's a new version available then it calls the `onNewVersion` callback passing the manifest data; otherwise it calls `onNoNewVersion` (in case of any error this callback is called as well)

body:
<!-- Is this a question? Questions WILL BE CLOSED. Ask in our chat https://on.cypress.io/chat  -->

### Current behavior
cy.setCookie does not set complete hostname by default.  It seems to ignore subdomains.
For example, on `https://cloud.google.com`, `cy.setCookie` will set the domain to just `.google.com`.

### Desired behavior
cy.setCookie should set the complete `window.location.hostname` by default.

### Test code to reproduce
```js
describe('setCookie', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.visit('https://cloud.google.com');
  });

  it('sets cookie domain properly using default', () => {
    cy.setCookie('testcookie', 'testcookievalue');
    cy.getCookie('testcookie').then((cookie) => {
      expect(cookie.domain).to.equal('.cloud.google.com');
    });
  });

  it('sets cookie domain properly', () => {
    cy.setCookie('testcookie2', 'testcookie2value', { domain: window.location.hostname });
    cy.getCookie('testcookie2').then((cookie) => {
      expect(cookie.domain).to.equal('.cloud.google.com');
    });
  });
});
```

cy.get() querying behavior does not match jQuery's :visible and :hidden
body:
### Current behavior [The documentation on cy.get()](https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/get.html) states: >The querying behavior of this command matches exactly how $(…) works in jQuery. This is not true for the `:visible` and `:hidden` selectors. ### Desired behavior The documentation and the actual behavior should match. ### Test code to reproduce Consider this html: ```html
Hello
``` And this Cypress code: ```JavaScript cy.get('div:hidden') ``` Using the selector `'div:hidden'` in `cy.get()` finds the div. Using that same selector with the actual jQuery `$()` [does not find it](https://jsfiddle.net/cxrtbho6/). The reverse goes for `'div:visible'`: `cy.get()` finds nothing, actual jQuery finds the element. Note that jQuery is acting according to its own documentation here: https://api.jquery.com/visible-selector/ states >Elements with visibility: hidden (...) are considered visible. So `cy.get()` is deviating from an explicit statement in the jQuery documentation here. ### Versions Cypress: 5.3.0 OS: Windows 10 Pro Browser: Chrome 86 jQuery: 3.5.1 ### Additional notes When I report my first bug on a project, I like to say thanks. So, thank you for making an awesome testing tool, for making it available for free, for reading and responding to so many bug reports, for keeping on maintaining and extending and improving Cypress. Much appreciated 😊!

title: .npmrc 'cafile' option should be honored by binary postinstall
body:
### Current behavior
When developing, it is very convenient to have a repository-defined `.npmrc` file with all the custom options. We use self-signed certificates for the binary repository mirror which we have set via `cypress_download_mirror` in the `.npmrc`. We also have `cafile` set to our root certificate file and use that when running `npm install` and such.

When running `npm install cypress` - the https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/lib/tasks/download.js ignores the `cafile` configuration even if it exists and only takes the environment configuration.

A workaround is to set the `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` variable, but that is a global solution and we might have several separate cafiles for different projects.

### Desired behavior

title: fix: Register and run default preprocessor in child process
body:
<!-- 
Thanks for contributing!
Read our contribution guidelines here: 
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
-->

<!-- Example: "Closes #1234" -->

- Closes #8634

### User facing changelog

- Fixed an issue where certain preprocessor-related plugins would cause tests not to run and a duplicate instance of Cypress to be spawned.

### Additional details

We run user-registered file preprocessors in the plugins child process, but when the user hasn't registered their own prepocessor, we register the default preprocessor in the main Cypress process. This causes [issues with preprocessor-related plugins](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8634#issuecomment-697874253) like Istanbul that use `process.execPath` to execute code because `process.execPath` is the Cypress binary in the main process and not `node`.

This fixes that by always registering and running the preprocessor in the child process, even our own default preprocessor.

Also, we used to not create the plugins child process if the user didn't have a plugins file. Now we always create it since it is necessary for running the default preprocessor.

Add a configuration option `scrollBehavior` that controls the viewport position to which an element should be scrolled prior to action commands. title: fix: Fix desktop-gui build
"Experimental Fetch Polyfill" in v5.x results in 2nd "cy.visit" doing nothing forever
body: ### Current behavior When starting with Cypress at ~4.11.0 we polyfilled Fetch API on our own (the `win.eval(''); win.fetch = win.unfetch;` hack). It worked nicely. We need to polyfill fetch in order to mock HTTP requests that AWS Cognito/AWS Amplify do. After upgrading to Cypress 5.3.0 we tried to replace our fetch polyfill by the toggling `experimentalFetchPolyfill` to `true`. **Basically it works for all test suites (files) that use `cy.visit` exactly and only once**. Unfortunately we experienced that all test suites with **more than one cy.visit** failed. To be more precise: they run forever without timing out. In each of these tests the second call of `cy.visit` causes the test to "go into an infinite loop". It just does nothing for a very long time and does not proceed: This leads us to the conclusion that using `experimentalFetchPolyfill` could, under some circumstances, make `cy.visit` doing nothing anymore. ### Desired behavior `cy.visit` should visit the passed URL and the test should proceed. ### Test code to reproduce We can reproduce the behaviour with our closed-source application. This application is deployed to the internet publicly. Also a minimal Cypress test against this application can verify the bug. The only problem: my customer does not allow me to associate the URL of the page with a test code for reproduction here. It would be possible for me to provide the test scenario via DM on twitter for example: twitter.com/jverhoelen I setup a test application that just demonstrates the setup itself: web app with AWS Amplify/Cognito, tested by Cypress 5.3.0 with experimental fetch polyfill enabled. Unfortunately it's not possible to reproduce the problem with this - it could just help to illustrate how one of our problematic tests look like: https://github.com/jverhoelen/cypress-experimental-fetch-polyfill-failure ### Versions Tried with Cypress 5.2.0, 5.3.0, 5.4.0 on Mac OS 10.15.6 with Node 12.15.0

title: build: fix semantic release git plugin and remove accidentally committed node_modules
body:
Fixes an issue where our `semantic-release` configuration was set up to accidentally include `node_modules/**/CHANGELOG.md`. Because of the way that we use `semantic-release` with plugins and `lerna`, the path of the config file becomes local to the package that it's running in, so we don't need the `**` glob (you would think it would respect our `.gitignore` but I guess not). I've tested these changes quite a bit in an external repo to ensure that it does still commit the `CHANGELOG.md` but nothing more.

This also removes all of the mistakenly committed files from git.

This PR is currently titled with `build:`, which will not cause a new release on merge. If we do want to release, we can change this to `fix:` but I see no reason to trigger a new release for changes that don't actually reach `npm` users.

title: feat: create-cypress-tests wizard
body:
This PR adds a new project that can be run as `yarn create cypress-tests` or `npx create-cypress-tests` to install cypress and all required dependencies including component tests.

## Features of this approach:
0. Fails if user git status contains untracked or uncommitted changes
1. Automatically determines yarn or npm to use
2. Copies and creates plugins and support files so the developer can instantly start writing tests without `yarn cypress open` 
3. Determines if the project is using typescript and injects `tsconfig.json`  
4. Has `--ignore-examples` option, which will create a dummy spec file from scratch so if the user will open cypress initially it won't create examples. 
5. Asks for component testing, determine which framework (vue or react) is using and installs the right framework adapter
6. All the required configuration for component testing is automagically injected right to the user config using babel

## Things to do 
- [x] Describe if we need to automatically put the  config files for component testing
- [x] Add documentation about it and perfectly make this as recommended way for installation, cause it will definitely improve DX. (https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-documentation/pull/3321)

body:

* TR-387

### User facing changelog
Fixed regenerator option.

### Additional details
* Why was this change necessary? => Command doesn't work.
* What is affected by this change? => N/A

### Any implementation details to explain? 
It seems that `@babel/preset-env` transpiles async await to regenerator. In this case, the tests are run in native (node 7.6.0+ supports native async/await) but the release transpiles them. That's why we need `regenerator-runtime`.

### How has the user experience changed?
N/A

### About the test.
I intentionally didn't add tests. As the cause of the problem is the difference between the dev and release environment. To test this, we might need to create a CircleCI job that runs the command, `npx cypress cache list --size`. But I guess it's too much.

title: Feature request: Add the ability to configure the server wait behavior
body:
# Concrete case

I have a project with cypress running thanks to this `test` scripts: `run-p --race dev cy:run` (see `npm-run-all` package).

I recently added some webpack compilation complexity to my project making the build a bit longer than usual.

Because of that, the cypress test suite is failing, not waiting enough time to get the server ready:

```
Cypress could not verify that this server is running:

  > http://localhost:3000

We are verifying this server because it has been configured as your `baseUrl`.

Cypress automatically waits until your server is accessible before running tests.

We will try connecting to it 3 more times...
We will try connecting to it 2 more times...
We will try connecting to it 1 more time...

Cypress failed to verify that your server is running.

Please start this server and then run Cypress again.
```

So bad, it was missing only 2 or 3 seconds to get the server up and running.

I did not find any possibility to tell cypress to try more than 3 times or wait a bit longer on each connection test.

The only workaround I found so far is to add a wait command:

```diff
diff --git a/package.json b/package.json
index 1808277..835a1e9 100644
--- a/package.json
+++ b/package.json
@@ -6,7 +6,7 @@
     "dev": "sapper dev --no-hot",
     "build": "NODE_ENV=production sapper build",
     "start": "node __sapper__/build",
-    "cy:run": "cypress run",
+    "cy:run": "wait-on tcp:3000 && cypress run",
     "cy:open": "cypress open",
     "test": "run-p --race dev cy:run"
   },
@@ -25,6 +25,7 @@
     "svelte-loader": "^2.9.0",
     "svelte-preprocess": "^4.5.1",
     "tailwindcss": "^1.9.2",
+    "wait-on": "^5.2.0",
     "webpack": "^4.44.2"
   }
 }
```

# Proposed solution

Add a configuration key and/or cli option to either increase the timeout and/or the number of retries of Cypress.

Maybe this do exist, but I didn't find anything on the documentation or help usages.

title: cy.route2 errors leak between tests
body:
### Current behavior I have a few tests that I'd like to share some network stubs. My first thought was to use `before`: ```js context('Context', () => { before(() => { cy.route2(...) }) it('test a', () => { doSomethingThatShouldTriggerStub() // stub is triggered }) it('test b', () => { doSomethingThatShouldTriggerStub() // stub is not triggered }) }) ``` But the stubbed route isn't getting triggered on the 2nd test. I wasn't sure if that was intentional but I assumed it was either intentional or WIP and moved to `beforeEach`: ```js context('Context', () => { beforeEach(() => { cy.route2(...) }) ... }) ``` `beforeEach` solved the problem with the stubs only working on the first test, but seemed to create a sort of race condition; (I think) when a stubbed request happens in between tests. title: Export results from Cypress' UI
body:
### What would you like?
In short, I would like a way to export the results of my test run (especially the failures) that was run from the Cypress UI (i.e. via `cypress open`)

### Why is this needed?
Here is my use case:

I am running a suite that takes on the order of 10 minutes to complete. When a test fails, my normal process for investigating a test failure is to jump into the test file and stick a `.only` on my test case, because as I make changes to my app's code or to the test code, I want to quickly check if that issue is resolved instead of running the entire test suite over again for each change.

Now suppose I have 10 different failures scattered throughout my tests. After I fix the first test using my `.only` scheme mentioned above, I no longer remember which of the other tests failed, and neither does Cypress because the test run data is gone after re-running my test with `.only`. So now in order to find out which other tests failed, I have to re-run the entire suite again, which costs me ~10 minutes.

The workaround for me at the moment is to basically right down a list of the failures (or putting `.only` on all of them right away). I suppose I could also use the failure screenshots.

I'm not sure if any of the reporter options will satisfy this use case, but even then, changing the reporter is an after-the-fact problem. I still have to re-run the suite again. If, on the other hand, I could just export the results from the Cypress UI, I wouldn't need to change any of my reporter options. Instead I would simply refer to this exported file for a list of the failures, then fix each one individually, and finally run my entire suite again to make sure all of my tests are still passing.

title: feat: Support body option in RouteMatcher
body:
#8560

### User facing changelog

You can easily match the content of request body with the `body` option in `RouteMatcher`.

Before:

```js
const p = Cypress.Promise.defer()

cy.route2({
  url: "http://localhost:3000/graphql",
  method: "POST"
}, (req) => {
  if (req.body.includes('searchShippingTemplate')) {
    p.resolve() // resolve the deferred promise
  }
})
// ... do some more Cypress stuff here ...
cy.wrap(p)
```

```js
cy.route2({
  url: "http://localhost:3000/graphql",
  method: "POST",

- It's just unnecessary code to maintain.
- We could potentially reuse these APIs if we want.

`requestJSON` prop on XHRs | 0.12.0 | throws warning

`cy.wait(fn)` | 0.11.4 | throws warning
`cy.server({stub: false})` | 0.13.2 | throws warning

The `{meta}S` key triggers the save actions.

I'm running the tests on a Mac, so the `meta` key event works.

But on GH Actions, the test runner uses Linux.

So I'm using the following snippet in the test to change the modifier key.

```
before(() => {
    if (navigator.appVersion.indexOf('Mac') != -1) {

  },

    save: ['ctrlKey', 's'],
  },
};

### [`v2.1.4`](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/releases/v2.1.4)
[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/compare/v2.1.3...v2.1.4)

Introduced some non-breaking changes to the module in order to take better advantage of tree-shaking as suggested in [#​55](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/issues/55) and [#​58](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/issues/58).

This should reduce file size for most users who are able to take advantage of tree shaking, especially those who are only using a subset of this library's features.

Thanks to [@​EvgenyOrekhov](https://togithub.com/EvgenyOrekhov) and [@​OliverJAsh](https://togithub.com/OliverJAsh) for their suggestions and feedback on these issues.

<https://bundlephobia.com/result?p=http-status-codes@2.1.4>

### [`v2.1.3`](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/releases/v2.1.3)
[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/compare/v2.1.2...v2.1.3)

*   Fix an issue where the common.js bundle was not working with react native projects. [#​60](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/issues/60) [#​56](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/issues/56)
*   Mark the module as "side-effect free" for tree shaking [#​58](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/issues/58)

### [`v2.1.2`](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/releases/2.1.2)
[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/compare/v2.1.1...v2.1.2)

Exports ESM module for browser environments which fixes [#​56](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/issues/56)

Provides a default export for additional backwards compatibility with v1 [#​54](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/issues/54)

### [`v2.1.1`](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/releases/2.1.1)
[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/compare/v2.1.0...v2.1.1)

Fixes a bug with the way the TypeScript definitions were being built. [#​52](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/issues/52)

Thanks to [@​Benno007](https://togithub.com/Benno007) for finding and reporting this issue.

### [`v2.1.0`](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/releases/2.1.0)
[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/compare/v2.0.0...v2.1.0)

*   Adds a new status code: `451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons`

Thanks [@​ffflorian](https://togithub.com/ffflorian) for this contribution.

### [`v2.0.0`](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/releases/v2.0.0)
[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/prettymuchbryce/node-http-status/compare/v1.4.0...v2.0.0)

This release marks a new major version of http-status-codes.

Improvements include:

*   Project rewritten in TypeScript
*   TypeScript enums "StatusCodes" and "ReasonPhrases"
*   Test coverage
*   Automated source code generation of codes and documentation
*   Change the reason phrase "Server Error" to the correct one, "Internal Server Error"
*   Rename "getStatusText" -> "getReasonPhrase" to make the API more consistent

Thanks to [@​seanmhanson](https://togithub.com/seanmhanson) for their help on this new version.

##### Migrating from v1.x.x
http-status-codes v2 is mostly backwards compatible with v1. There is a single breaking change and two recommended changes.

##### [Breaking Change] 'Server Error'
The reason phrase for the status code `500` has been changed from `"Server Error"` to `"Internal Server Error"`. This is the correct phrase according to RFC7231. If you are migrating from v1, and have code that relies on the result of `getStatusText(500)` or `getReasonPhrase('Server Error')`, then this could affect you.

##### [Non-breaking change] getStatusText renamed getReasonPhrase
The function `getStatusText` has been renamed to `getReasonPhrase`. The old function is still available, but may be deprecated in a future version. To fix this simply rename instances of `getStatusText()` to `getReasonPhrase()`. The function is otherwise the same as it was before.

##### [Non-breaking change] StatusCodes
In http-status-codes v1, Status Codes were exported directly from the top-level module. i.e. `HttpStatus.OK`. In v2 all Status Codes live under an object called `StatusCodes`. i.e. `HttpStatus.StatusCodes.OK`. We made this change to cater to TypeScript users who prefer a dedicated value with an enum type. The previous values are still exported, but we won't continue to update them. Please migrate if you're using the old-style imports.

</details>

title: Shorthand syntax for action commands: cy.click('Login')
body:
<!-- Use the template below to request a feature. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. -->

### What would you like?
<!-- A clear description of the feature or enhancement wanted in Cypress -->
I am inspired by CodeCeption which we use at work. 
In CodeCeption you can use this syntax:
```PHP
// Click on an element with the text "Login"
$I->click('Login');
// Click on an element with the id "submit_button"
$I->click('submit_button');
// Fill the field with label "Username" with "Miles"
$I->fillField('Username', 'Miles');
```

A shorthand notation in Cypress could follow the following rule to achieve a similar syntax:  

**If a string is added to an action (click, type, select, ...) as the first argument, this string is read as one of:**
* **the css selector of an element (comparable with `.get()`)**
* **the textual content of an element (comparable with `.contains`)**
* **the textual content of the label `<label for="elementname">` of an input element**

**The action will be performed on the found element**

This way test code like this:

```javascript
cy.get('#username').type('John');
cy.get('#password').type('MySuperSecret');
cy.contains('label', 'Remember me').find('input[type="checkbox"]').check();
cy.contains('Login').click();
```
Can be written like this:

```javascript
cy.type('Username:', 'John');
cy.type('Password', 'MySuperSecret');
cy.check('Remember me');
cy.click('Login');
```

### Why is this needed?
<!-- Remember, we are not familiar with the application you are testing, so please provide a clear description of why this would be useful to your project. -->
It would make tests more readable.

title: Desktop GUI CSS Framework
body:
I have noticed that the Cypress Desktop GUI is using Bootstrap 3.

Bootstrap 3 went end of life on 24th of july 2019, see [here, on the Bootstrap Blog](https://blog.getbootstrap.com/2019/07/24/lts-plan/).

Naturally, it would be the most logic choice to go for the next version of bootstrap, which is Bootstrap 4.
Bootstrap 5 is still under active development and currently in alpha.

However, this situation also allows for revisiting the choice of the CSS framework.

New modern utliity CSS frameworks have risen, like [Tailwind](https://tailwindcss.com/).

Tailwind hits the nail on the head

> Most CSS frameworks do too much.
> They come with all sorts of predesigned components like buttons, cards, and alerts that might help you move quickly at 
 first, but cause more pain than they cure when it comes time to make your site stand out with a custom design.
> Tailwind is different.
> Instead of opinionated predesigned components, Tailwind provides low-level utility classes that let you build completely custom designs without ever leaving your HTML.

I would gladly refactor the desktop UI to use Tailwind. However, if that is not an option or considered and the only choice is to continue to use Bootstrap, I'd also volunteer to make a PR.

Having worked with Tailwind in production, I highly recommend the approach. It has a thriving community. I think it would be a great fit. I can also link a few articles showing the advantages.

What do you guys think?

As mentioned before, I will gladly provide a PR for the changes, but I wanted to get a commitment for a CSS framework before doing all that work.

title: Add option to remove browser cookies from cy.request
body:
<!-- Use the template below to request a feature. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. -->

### What would you like?
<!-- A clear description of the feature or enhancement wanted in Cypress -->
All requests in Cypress are currently sent "as if through the browser," meaning that all your browser cookies get copied into your request. This makes sense for the default behavior, but if I think you should be able to specify if you don't want them included. Perhaps `cy.request` could take an option `"includeCookies": "false"` . 

(I tried passing `Authorization: { cookie: "" }` and `Authorization: { cookie: null }` but neither had any effect.)

### Why is this needed?
<!-- Remember, we are not familiar with the application you are testing, so please provide a clear description of why this would be useful to your project. -->
Consider an application that supports both "read-only" users and "can make edits" users. Ours relies on message queueing and websockets, so that the view will update in realtime. What I'd like to do is test the "read-only" user functionality by POST-ing using a user token that has both permissions. I am currently getting an unauthorized error on my HTTP call because the session cookie associated with my logged in user is being passed in the request. The service accepts both Bearer auth and cookie auth, but in this case I'd like to send *only* the Bearer token.

My current workaround is to pull back my cookie values, clear them, make the request, and then set them again 😕

```

This used to work perfectly fine with Chrome 80. Since Chrome 83, the second `cy.get()` throws an error:

> Timed out retrying: cy.type() failed because this element is detached from the DOM.
> 
> `<input>`

As a workaround, we had to put an explicit `cy.wait(100)` between the two commands.

```js
cy.get("select").select("Second")
cy.wait(100)
cy.get("input").type("Hallo")
```

As we had quite a lot of those, this slowed down our tests. Also I don't think these should be required here. (I only just now noticed something curious, even a `cy.wait(0)` will work, at least in the testcase linked below)

This works in Firefox, and in Chrome version 80 (which I luckily still had on an old machine). As Google makes it almost impossible to download an older Chrome version, I couldn't really try different versions.

Cypress version otoh doesn't really seem to matter, it happens in old versions as well as in current version.

Here is a [small repo which reproduces the problem](https://github.com/marc-guenther/cypress-bug-element-detached). Simply run`npm start`.

title: fix: Fix issue with createSnapshot causing images to load too many times
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
-->

- Closes #8679

### User facing changelog

- Fixed a bug where snapshotting caused images to load too many times

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

The process for cloning the dom for a snapshot used to be:

- Use `document.importNode` to clone the dom (where `document` belongs to the `top` frame, essentially importing the dom from the AUT document into the `top` document)
- Immediately re-attach it to the AUT document with `autDocument.attachNode`

This caused the side effect of causing any cloned images to be re-requested.

Now the process is:

- Use `tempDocument.importNode` to clone the dom, attaching it to a "virtual" in-memory document (`tempDocument`) that we create for this purpose
- Only re-attach the dom to the AUT document at the last possible moment, when the user wants to restore the snapshot by hovering over the command in the command log

This prevents any side effects at the time of snapshotting.

### PR Tasks

Delete tasks if they are not applicable. -->

- [x] Have tests been added/updated?
- [x] Has the original issue or this PR been tagged with a release in ZenHub? <!-- (internal team only)-->

title: Cypress Times Out in Composed Custom Commands
body:
### What would you like?
When I write a Custom Command, obviously it is often composed of several lines that invoke cy methods and chains. It seems to me like these compositional custom commands time out if they contain to many composing things. I want a way to specify that the timeout for my custom command gets reset after each chain so that the overall custom command doesn't timeout prematurely even though it is plainly making progress.

### Why is this needed?
It really limits the usefulness of custom commands if I have to "keep them short" in runtime as a whole block.

title: Cypress not accepting 'text/html; charset=utf-8'
body:
I know Cypress is usually working with text/html. We're about to write Cypress tests for [OTRS][1]. I have written some example tests yet for public websites, everything worked well.  
Now I have the problem that OTRS (several dev- and test-systems) seems to return content-type as 'text/html; charset=utf-8' instead of expected 'text/html' when I use cy.visit() - tested in Firefox, Chrome and Electron:  

        cy.visit() failed trying to load:
    
    http://xx.xx.xx.xx/otrs/index.pl
    
    The content-type of the response we received from your web server was:
    
      > text/html; charset=utf-8;
    
    This was considered a failure because responses must have content-type: 'text/html'
    
    However, you can likely use cy.request() instead of cy.visit().
    
    cy.request() will automatically get and set cookies and enable you to parse responses.

Since this content-type is defined in so many parts of OTRS, it is not possible for us to change it - especially because this product is not developed by us, but imho the content-type 'text/html; charset=utf-8' should also be accepted from Cypress since it actually is text/html.

Any feedback on this is very much appreciated!

### Versions
Cypress 5.5.0 (via npm install cypress)
Running on MacOS 10.15.7 (first tests) and later inside docker image cypress/included:5.5.0
Chrome 86/Firefox81/Electron85

  [1]: https://github.com/OTRS/otrs
