title: Including native modules in plugins file fails on Mac
body:
### Current behavior
When referencing a native module (for example, `sqlite3`) from the `plugins/index.js` file, cypress is unable to process the plugins file and thus unable to run tests. The error is as follows:

```
Error: dlopen([path]/node_modules/sqlite3/lib/binding/napi-v3-darwin-x64/node_sqlite3.node, 1): no suitable image found.  Did find:
	[path]/node_modules/sqlite3/lib/binding/napi-v3-darwin-x64/node_sqlite3.node: code signature in ([path]/node_modules/sqlite3/lib/binding/napi-v3-darwin-x64/node_sqlite3.node) not valid for use in process using Library Validation: mapped file has no cdhash, completely unsigned? Code has to be at least ad-hoc signed.
    at process.func [as dlopen] (electron/js2c/asar.js:140:31)
    at Object.Module._extensions..node (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1196:18)
    at Object.func [as .node] (electron/js2c/asar.js:140:31)
    at Module.load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:981:32)
    at Module._load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:881:14)
    at Function.Module._load (electron/js2c/asar.js:769:28)
    at Module.require (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1023:19)
    at require (internal/modules/cjs/helpers.js:77:18)
    at Object.<anonymous> ([path]/node_modules/sqlite3/lib/sqlite3-binding.js:4:15)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1145:30)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1166:10)
    at Module.load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:981:32)
    at Module._load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:881:14)
    at Function.Module._load (electron/js2c/asar.js:769:28)
    at Module.require (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1023:19)
    at require (internal/modules/cjs/helpers.js:77:18)
```

If I try ad-hoc signing the package (`codesign --force --deep -s - node_modules/sqlite3/lib/binding/napi-v3-darwin-x64/node_sqlite3.node`) or signing it with a personal certificate, it still fails, but with `mapped file has no Team ID and is not a platform binary (signed with custom identity or adhoc?)` instead of `mapped file has no cdhash, completely unsigned? Code has to be at least ad-hoc signed`.

I found another issue that sounds similar (https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8258) but it seems that person may have found a workaround and closed the ticket. I believe this is still an issue overall (I see nothing suggesting issues with node version in my case), so I'm opening a fresh issue.

### Desired behavior
I should be able to use any node module that I can use in my app itself in the plugins file. I was able to work around it in this case, but it required a substantial reshuffling of functionality.

Of note - referencing the `sqlite3` library worked just fine in cypress version 3.4.1, which I recently upgraded from.

Some googling led me to https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/issues/3940, which suggests that a potential fix would be to add `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` to https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/scripts/entitlements.mac.inherit.plist - however, I don't know what other implications adding that would have/whether it's intentionally not included/whether there's another approach that would be better. I'd be happy to submit a PR to add this, if it makes sense.

### Test code to reproduce
- Make a new npm project (`npm init`)
- Install cypress (`npm install cypress`)
- Install sqlite3 (`npm install sqlite3`)
- Add the line `const sqlite3 = require('sqlite3');` to the freshly-generated `cypress/plugins/index.js`
- Run `cypress run`, and see that it fails with the above error.
- To ad-hoc sign the package as suggested, run `codesign --force --deep -s - node_modules/sqlite3/lib/binding/napi-v3-darwin-x64/node_sqlite3.node`. Re-run `cypress run`, and see the new variation on the same error.

### Versions
Cypress: 5.5.0 (last known working version, 3.4.1)
Sqlite3: 5.0.0
Node: 12.19.0
NPM: 6.14.8
OS: MacOS Catalina (10.15.7)

title: Generic for cy.request response body
body:
Having a type of response body would be more convenient for TypeScript users

Currently, I see that request and response type annotations look like
```ts
request(url: string, body?: RequestBody): Chainable<Response>

interface Response {
  allRequestResponses: any[]
  body: any
  duration: number
  headers: { [key: string]: string }
  isOkStatusCode: boolean
  redirectedToUrl: string
  requestHeaders: { [key: string]: string }
  status: number
  statusText: string
}
```

If we change it to
```
request<T = any>(url: string, body?: RequestBody): Chainable<Response<T>>

interface Response<T = any> {
  allRequestResponses: any[]
  body: T
  duration: number
  headers: { [key: string]: string }
  isOkStatusCode: boolean
  redirectedToUrl: string
  requestHeaders: { [key: string]: string }
  status: number
  statusText: string
}
```
then a user will be able to specify the response body type in their code.

Latest (v5.5.0), but I'm guessing all versions are affected.

title: Race condition when running multiple Cypress instances in CI
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
We run Cypress in parallel in our CI environment. Our CI provider (Google Cloud) shares the working directory between steps (which run in parallel), and we're noticing that Cypress will occasionally fail with the following error:

```
 /workspace/app/node_modules/.bin/cypress run --record --parallel --ci-build-id [redacted] --browser chrome
[17:40:44]  Verifying Cypress can run /root/.cache/Cypress/5.5.0/Cypress [started]
[17:40:47]  Verified Cypress!       /root/.cache/Cypress/5.5.0/Cypress [title changed]
[17:40:47]  Verified Cypress!       /root/.cache/Cypress/5.5.0/Cypress [completed]

================================================================================

  (Run Starting)

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Cypress:    5.5.0                                                                              │
  │ Browser:    Chrome 84                                                                          │
  │ Specs:      13 found [redacted]                                                                          │
  │ Params:     Tag: false, Group: false, Parallel: true                                           │
  │ Run URL:    https://dashboard.cypress.io/projects/pe6of4/runs/1316                             │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
                                                                                                    
  Running:  [redacted].spec.js                                                        (1 of 13)
  Estimated: 43 seconds
EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '/builder/home/.config/Cypress/cy/production/browsers/chrome-stable/run-462/CypressExtension'
Error: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '/builder/home/.config/Cypress/cy/production/browsers/chrome-stable/run-462/CypressExtension'


error Command failed with exit code 1.
info Visit https://yarnpkg.com/en/docs/cli/run for documentation about this command.
```

I believe the issue here is some sort of race condition caused by both build steps executing Cypress at the same time, attempting to install this chrome extension, and failing when it realizes that the other has already installed it. The other instance of Cypress appears to run without issue, at least until our CI automatically kills the process because the other has failed.

### Desired behavior
Both instances of Cypress succeed, not showing a `EEXIST` error.

### Test code to reproduce
Begin running two instances of Cypress at the same time on the same machine in the same directory with the following command:

```cypress run --record --parallel --ci-build-id $BUILD_ID --browser chrome```

Note that this appears to be a race condition, as this is an issue that maybe affects 20% of our builds.

### Versions
We've found this to be an issue on Cypress 5.5.0.

body:
### Current behavior
```
Oops...we found an error preparing this test file:

  cypress/integration/myTest.js

The error was:

TypeError: webpack is not a function

```

### Desired behavior
Cypress should run tests.

### Test code to reproduce
https://github.com/jwalton/cypress-test-tiny

```
git clone git@github.com:jwalton/cypress-test-tiny.git
cd cypress-test-tiny
npm install
npm cypress run
```

### Versions
This works fine in Cypress 4.x, 5.0.0, and 5.1.0, but 5.2.0 and higher, it breaks.

I did a little digging at the line it's failing on is [here](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/36a4289a98d65eb16ec5714a9e246dfc5fc56922/npm/webpack-preprocessor/index.ts#L226):

```js
    const compiler = webpack(webpackOptions)
```

Again, I couldn't figure out how to set a breakpoint here and hit this, so I added a `console.log(webpack)` to see what webpack actually was.  What's interesting here is that in our project, in the root folder we have a folder called "webpack" with some configuration files in it, and the contents of the `webpack` variable here are clearly from our `/webpack/index.js`, not from the real webpack.  (Perhaps this is related to https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8555?)

title: Incorrect domain when setting cookie
body:
### Current behavior

When setting a cookie with `cy.setCookie("foo", "bar")`, domain is not set according to doc:

Given the current URL is `https://another-level.subdomain.example.com`, a cookie is saved with the domain set to `.example.com`. Also, when setting the domain explicitly, it's prefixed with `.`

### Desired behavior

Domain should be set to `another-level.subdomain.example.com` as stated in docs: https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/setcookie.html#Arguments => default is `window.location.hostname`

### Versions

tested on 5.4.0 & 5.6.0

title: Overwrite cy.request/cy.visit - calling original function more than once?
Report bundled Node version
body:
When building `cypress/included:x.y.z` Docker image sometimes we miss the Node version and create a Docker image with Node version that does not match the Node version bundled with Cypress. It would be nice to validate the Node version during the CI build process. The problem is we do not output bundled Node version from Cypress.

Proposal:

Extend the `cypress version` command to output bundled Node version

```
$ npx cypress version
Cypress package version: 5.4.0
Cypress binary version: 5.4.0
Cypress includes Node: 12.14.1
```

Stretch goal:

For simple parsing add a parameter to output just a particular version

```
$ npx cypress version --package
5.4.0
$ npx cypress version --node
12.14.1
```

title: Unable to save fixture from response provided in route2
body:
The route2 reply handler doesn't allow any further commands, making it impossible to save fixtures, which is necessary for us to be able to use Cypress for mocking our backend.

Using the following example:

```
    cy.route2(matcher, request => request.reply(response => {
        const obj = {
          url: request.url,
          request: _pick(request, ['method', 'body']),
          response: _pick(response, ['body', 'headers', 'statusCode'])
        }
        cy.writeFile(
          path.join('cypress', 'fixtures', fixturePath, 'mock.json'),
          obj
        )
      })
    )
```

### Current behavior
Using the snippet above causes this error:
```
Uncaught CypressError: The following error originated from your test code, not from Cypress.

  > A response callback passed to `req.reply()` threw an error while intercepting a response:

Cypress detected that you returned a promise from a command while also invoking one or more cy commands in that promise.

The command that returned the promise was:

  > `cy.visit()`

The cy command you invoked inside the promise was:

  > `cy.writeFile()`
```

### Desired behavior
Make it possible to access the response outside route2, possibly by letting the handler inside `reply` yield it.

### Test code to reproduce
See the snippet above.

### Versions
5.6.0

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

Occasionally, Cypress will exit with `SIGABRT`, `SIGTERM`, or `SIGSEGV` and a non-zero exit code when `experimentalSourceRewriting` is active.

title: Print specific component's version when using "cypress version" command
body:
Building on top of https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/9180

Right now `cypress version` prints 4 versions

```text
$ npx cypress version
Cypress package version: 6.0.0
Cypress binary version: 6.0.0
Electron version: 10.1.2
Bundled Node version: 12.16.3
```

To make checking versions in cypress-docker-images easier, it would be nice to be able to specify which version we want to print and print just that (even without newline)

Something like 

```
$ npx cypress version --component package
6.0.0
$ npx cypress version --component binary
6.0.0
$ npx cypress version --component electron
10.1.2
$ npx cypress version --component node
12.16.3
```

title: Cypress assertions pass silently where they are expected to fail
body:
### Context

We are trying to mock some API requests which are common across all pages of our app. 
We wrote a custom command for this and ran it inside `beforeEach` in our tests. 

### Current behavior

We found some inconsistent behavior when we run some of our tests. We can only reproduce it once in every 7-10 test runs. 

1. Sometimes the custom command called in `beforeEach` doesn't run even though `beforeEach` runs.
2. Some of our assertions which use `cy.get` chained with `cy.contains` pass silently although no elements are matched. 
3. `beforeEach` doesn't appear in cypress command logs although its executed.

Note: We kept some `console.log`s and confirmed this behavior

Here's a screenshot when this behavior occurred:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4106656/99353895-71580c80-28cb-11eb-981a-d90786d05b48.png)

A screenshot where the same test passed as expected:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4106656/99359982-e16b9000-28d5-11eb-83c0-6dcd8ddc3926.png)

### Desired behavior

1. Custom commands must run consistently in `beforeEach`
2. The first assertion with 0 matched elements must fail consistently (please refer to the screenshot).
3. When `beforeEach` runs, it must be displayed in the command logs consistently

### Additional information

We used `cy.route2` for stubbing API calls and started noticing these issues after enabling `experimentalNetworkStubbing`. 
This inconsistency is reproducible in our local environment and Github CI

### Test code to reproduce

We're still trying to narrow down to the root cause of these problems. So, any pointers on what might be causing this inconsistent behavior would be great until we can give a repo that you can clone and run. 

### Versions

Cypress version: Can reproduce with 5.5.0 and 5.6.0
Browser version: Chrome 85.0.4183.102 (Official Build) (64-bit)

title: Cypress Custom Commands with dots or brackets
cy.request() failing on spec start
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
I have set up Cypress to use cy.request(METHOD, FQDN, DATA) to create a test user and seed the database prior to running tests. title: cy.intercept cannot properly wait for request against endpoint with multiple aliases
Automatically include CORS headers for network stubbing
body:
<!-- :wave: Use the template below to request a feature. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion :point_right: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. :pray: -->

### What would you like?
Currently, users must specify CORS headers manually, if needed:

https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-realworld-app/commit/2df6ef737ce16a6c81a0a51e415ddb38d3a47399

```js
    // Before: cy.route("GET", "/bankAccounts", []).as("getBankAccounts");
    cy.intercept(
      { method: "GET", url: "/bankAccounts" },
      {
        // TODO: automatically handle applying these headers
        headers: {
          "access-control-allow-origin": window.location.origin,
          "Access-Control-Allow-Credentials": "true",
        },
        body: { results: [] },
      }
    ).as("getBankAccounts");
```

This is some manual work that could probably be avoided in 99% of cases.

We should set `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: ${request's origin header}` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` by default on stubbed responses so users don't need to do this manually.

body: ### Current behavior The function cy.contains() will not locate text outside of the `` element. I thought this was a feature, and not a bug, until I tried cy.get() and it's able to grab DOM elements from outside of `` just fine. I recognize this is an extreme edge case, as putting page content outside of `` is bad practice. I created this quick demo repo to show the behavior: https://github.com/meerkat-citronella/cypress-body-test. When you run the test, you can see that cy.get() is able to locate the out-of-body element, while cy.contains() cannot. ### Desired behavior I would like cy.contains() to have access to the same scope as cy.get(). ### Test code to reproduce Repo: https://github.com/meerkat-citronella/cypress-body-test . Clone and run. Here is some relevant code showing how I am rendering an element outside of the document's `` tag: index.js: ```js // render inside of the element ReactDOM.render( , document.getElementById("root") ); // render outside of the element const insertionPoint = document.createElement("div"); insertionPoint.id = "insertion-point"; document.body.parentNode.insertBefore(insertionPoint, document.body); ReactDOM.render( , // <---- cy.contains() won't be able to locate the text in insertionPoint ); ``` ### Versions My package.json: ```json { "name": "cypress-body-test", "version": "0.1.0", "private": true, "dependencies": { "@testing-library/jest-dom": "^5.11.4", "@testing-library/react": "^11.1.0", "@testing-library/user-event": "^12.1.10", "cypress": "^5.6.0", "react": "^17.0.1", "react-dom": "^17.0.1", "react-scripts": "4.0.0", "web-vitals": "^0.2.4" }, "scripts": { "start": "react-scripts start", "build": "react-scripts build", "test": "react-scripts test", "eject": "react-scripts eject" }, "eslintConfig": { "extends": [ "react-app", "react-app/jest" ] }, "browserslist": { "production": [ ">0.2%", "not dead", "not op_mini all" ], "development": [ "last 1 chrome version", "last 1 firefox version", "last 1 safari version" ] } } ``` Chrome version: 86.0.4240.198 OS: macOS Catalina 10.15.7

- Closes #8477

- Addresses [TR-398](https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/TR-398)

### User facing changelog

- Webpack preprocessor now allows passing the path to TypeScript via the `typescript` option.

### Additional details

When we run the default preprocessor and require typescript, it ends up requiring cypress's own version of typescript and not the user's. This prevents us from monkey-patching the correct version of typescript for source maps compatibility. 

We already search out the path to the user's typescript and pass it to the preprocessor. This utilizes that path to require typescript.

In Cypress 6.0.0, using `cy.intercept()` with a `routeMatcher.url` that also contains minimatch syntax fails to match.

The help at https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/intercept.html#routeMatcher-RouteMatcher says:
> All properties are optional. All properties that are set must match for the route to handle a request. If a string is passed to any property, it will be glob-matched against the request using minimatch.The available routeMatcher properties are listed below:

### Desired behavior
Glob-matching should succeed with string properties passed to `cy.intercept()` in a `routeMatcher`.

title: Test runner window when occluded affects test results
body:
### Current behavior
We have a "global loading" element in our app that covers the entire screen any time a component `fetch()`es data (well, it's more sophisticated than that, but it doesn't matter). I've noticed that if I put another window on top of Cypress's "Test runner" window, my tests will consistently fail, claiming something can't be clicked because it's being covered by another element (our "global loading" element). The same tests will consistently pass if the window isn't covered, even if it's only a few pixels that are exposed.

I believe this is Chromium detecting it's _fully_ covered and throttling itself somehow. However, I don't think it's only slowing its rate of processing things, I think it's fully halting things. If I add a `{ timeout: 10000 }` to my commands, they still fail when the window is covered.

I can also reproduce this by minimizing the window.

I've played around with covering the window with _a lot_ of different apps -- because at first I couldn't make it fail when SQL Server Management Studio was covering it up, but now I can't even reproduce that. That is, SSMS covering Cypress consistently fails the test now.

### Desired behavior
Cypress test runner window state should not affect the results

### Test code to reproduce
[I tried to put together a simple repro](https://github.com/OlsonDev/cypress-test-tiny), forking [cypress-test-tiny](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-test-tiny), but of course it passes regardless of windows covering it or being minimized. I'll have to come back to this; but I'm still submitting this now in case anyone has ideas.

### Versions
6.0.0, but probably earlier and 6.1.0

<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
<!-- A description including screenshots, stack traces, DEBUG logs, etc. 👉 https://on.cypress.io/troubleshooting -->
Calling `cy.visit` with headers in options won't send these headers.



### Desired behavior
<!-- Remember, we are not familiar with the application you're testing, so please provide a clear description of what should happen.-->
Adding headers to the visit `options` parameter is [supposed](https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/visit.html) to add request headers:
```js
cy.visit('https://cypress.io',{
  'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 13_2_3 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/13.0.3 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1',
  'My-Header': 'foo'
})
```

### Test code to reproduce
<!-- Provide test code that we can copy, paste, and run on our machine to see the issue. -->

Test repo: https://github.com/warpdesign/cypress-change-user-agent

title: calledOnceWith & calledOnceWithExactly sinon matchers missing
body:
### Current behavior

> CypressError: The chainer calledOnceWith was not found. Could not build assertion.

But TS types define this as allowed:
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/c616af48ee1c8d9fe00687fb1e54cc69c765830d/cli/types/cypress.d.ts#L4264
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/c616af48ee1c8d9fe00687fb1e54cc69c765830d/cli/types/cypress.d.ts#L4276

### Desired behavior

Working matcher

### Description

I've even started looking into fixing this but this seems to be over my head in a timeframe that I could spend on this right now. 

It's not obvious to track what version are you even using because you rely on npm hoisting - your packages define **very different** versions of `chai`, `sinon`, `chai-sinon` & `@cypress/chai-sinon`. I believe that it would be great to:
- unify those versions
- provide at least a peer dep range where applicable

From what I've analyzed you are actually using your `@cypress/chai-sinon` fork in the Cypress' public API:
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/c1daab066db40d5a3cdc932de0d659f358b935d5/packages/driver/src/cy/chai.js#L7
and the driver package requires the v1 of that fork package, but only in its dev dep:
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/c1daab066db40d5a3cdc932de0d659f358b935d5/packages/driver/package.json#L16
so in reality a different version gets probably loaded at runtime in the final product.

At the same time, your fork is already at v2 and it just doesn't really add those methods to the `expect` object. The only ones that are handled are listed here:
https://github.com/cypress-io/sinon-chai/blob/3af9baa3b2981db8ade653bcbff58da1a1094a32/lib/sinon-chai.js#L174

Additionally links to the Sinon docs in the JSDOCs above types for all `sinon-chai` method are pointing to Sinon v4 docs but I also don't believe this is actually a version that is used. Note that you link to different methods above those 2 missing methods because they have not been implemented in Sinon v4.

### Test code to reproduce

```js
const foo = cy.spy().as("foo")

setTimeout(() => {
    foo({ bar: "test" })
}, 500)

cy.get("@foo").should(
  "be.calledOnceWith",
  Cypress.sinon.match({
    bar: "test",
  })
);
```

### Versions

6.1.0

title: Loading custom webpack config expects an object, not just an environment name
body:
According to Webpack 4.x docs https://webpack.js.org/configuration/configuration-types/#exporting-a-function the webpack.config.js file can export a function. That function takes `env` object as first argument

For some reason our current implementation passes `development` string as `env`, but the `env` config should be an object

```
module.exports = function(env, argv) {
  env.production //
}
```

`env` should have properties from https://webpack.js.org/api/cli/#environment-options

title: Dynamic module imports not getting resolved
body:
This is probably not a bug. I suspect a mis-configuration on my part or a technical limitation of how unit testing works in cypress.

#### Summary

I am trying to set up component testing for a quite extensive Vue app and am running into problems with the `@` alias not getting resolved leading to errors like this one:

`Error: Cannot find module '@/components /<path_to_child_component>'`

when the component to be tested contains a child component that is lazy loaded from that path.

#### Setup

I am using [lazy loading](https://router.vuejs.org/guide/advanced/lazy-loading.html) to import child components via this function:

```javascript
export function lazyImport (component) {
    return () => import(/* webpackChunkName: "view-[request]" */ `@/components/${component}`);
}
``` 

I also use lazy loading for i18n as per their [instructions](https://kazupon.github.io/vue-i18n/guide/lazy-loading.html).

Cypress plugin setup (vanilla + splicing in webpack options):
```javascript
const preprocessor = require("@cypress/vue/dist/plugins/webpack");
const webpackOptions = require("../../node_modules/@vue/cli-service/webpack.config.js");

module.exports = (on, config) => {
    const _config = {
        ...config,
        webpackOptions,
    };
    preprocessor(on, _config);
    // IMPORTANT return the config object
    return _config;
};
```

Relevant part of the `webpackOptions` used in the plugin setup above:
```javascript
{
  mode: 'development',
  resolve: {
    alias: {
      '@': '/Users/foo/bar/src',
      'vue$': 'vue/dist/vue.esm.js'
    },
  plugins: [
    VueLoaderPlugin {},
  ],
    ...
}
```

Cypress config:
```
{
  "baseUrl": "http://localhost:8080",
  "pluginsFile": "tests/plugins/index.js",
  "supportFile": "tests/support/index.js",
  "fixturesFolder": "tests/fixtures",
  "integrationFolder": "tests/e2e",
  "testFiles": "**/*.spec.js*",
  "experimentalComponentTesting": true,
  "componentFolder": "tests/components",
  "nodeVersion": "system"
}
```

My dev environment:
```
macOS: 10.15.7 (19H2)
Node: v12.18.4
Chrome: Version 86.0.4240.80 (Official Build) (x86_64)
```

My dev dependencies:
```
"@cypress/code-coverage": "3.8.1",
"@cypress/vue": "1.0.0-alpha.4",
"@vue/babel-preset-app": "4.5.7",
"@vue/cli-plugin-babel": "4.5.7",
"@vue/cli-plugin-e2e-cypress": "4.5.7",
"@vue/cli-plugin-eslint": "4.5.7",
"@vue/cli-service": "4.5.7",
"babel-eslint": "10.0.3",
"babel-plugin-istanbul": "6.0.0",
"cypress": "5.3.0",
"eslint": "5.16.0",
"eslint-plugin-vue": "6.1.2",
"node-sass": "4.14.1",
"sass-loader": "10.0.3",
"string-replace-loader": "2.2.0",
"vue-cli-plugin-cypress-experimental": "1.2.0",
"vue-template-compiler": "2.6.11",
"webpack": "4.41.6",
"webpack-bundle-analyzer": "3.6.1"
```

#### Symptoms

The `@` alias resolution works in the test spec. E.g. importing the component  to be tested and other dependencies works just fine:
```javascript
import {  mount } from "@cypress/vue";

import AssetCard from "@/components/base-elements/AssetCard.vue";

import Buefy from "buefy";
import icons from "@/icons";
...
```

But the AssetCard.vue component tries to lazy load it's child components and for those imports the `@` alias resolution does not seem to work. 

#### Possible mitigations 

I have verified that the proper alias resolution options get passed to webpack, I have tried separately invoking `on("file:preprocessor", webpack(webpackOptions))` (possibly not relevant and also shouldn't be necessary as it is being invoked by cypress later). 

I can make use of the `components` option of the `mount()` function to avoid all of the errors relating to child components. However, this involves loading all the components in the chain of child components which makes the test highly coupled to irrelevant implementation details.

I can change the lazy loading functions to use absolute paths. This is not ideal as it requires additional logic to make test and production server builds work nicely.

#### Question

Is there just something that I am doing wrong here? Is there just a technical problem to using dynamic imports in this kind of setup? Any help in figuring this out is greatly appreciated!

title: Can't disable source maps for create-react-app
body:
Thanks for working on cypress component testing!

Currently when using the `reactScripts` plugin there's no way to disable the source map generation from webpack, since `find-webpack` hardcodes `NODE_ENV` to `development` and CRA only allows disabling source maps with `GENERATE_SOURCEMAP` in production builds.

What would be the preferred way to allow doing this? Passing some sort of webpack config overwrite/merge function to `reactScripts` as argument? Some sort of ENV variable?

My workaround currently is to hardcode

```js
preprocessorOptions.webpackOptions.devtool = false
```

at the end of `cra-v3/file-preprocessor.js`

title: Include VueLoaderPlugin() in documentation
body:
## Is this a bug report or a feature request? **Bug report**

**- version**
"cypress-vue-unit-test": "^1.11.0",
"cypress": "^3.1.5",
"@cypress/webpack-preprocessor": "^4.0.3",
"vue-loader": "^15.6.4",

**- steps to reproduce**

1. Create a fresh project (in my case, I installed a fresh laravel project through composer
2. `npm install --save-dev cypress cypress-vue-unit-test`
3. `npm install` (for other project dependencies)
4. follow [manual instructions ](https://github.com/bahmutov/cypress-vue-unit-test#manual) to load and test single-file vue components

**- expected behavior**
In the following screenshots, I used [the component example](https://github.com/bahmutov/cypress-vue-unit-test#component-example).  FYI, I had to remove [the <style> tag](https://github.com/bahmutov/cypress-vue-unit-test/issues/151#issuecomment-467421879) because it was causing a similar (i.e. loader) error, but that's irrelevant to this issue.

![screenshot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13646646/53410568-0dfcad00-3979-11e9-831b-ae50212f5482.png)

**- actual behavior**

![screenshot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13646646/53410690-56b46600-3979-11e9-98f9-8f57ae3d5c0a.png)
`vue-loader was used without the corresponding plugin. Make sure to include VueLoaderPlugin in your webpack config.`

**- suggested fix** 
Add the VueLoaderPlugin in webpack config. I read from [this comment](https://github.com/symfony/webpack-encore/issues/311#issuecomment-390491179) that VueLoader v15 and above requires the VueLoaderPlugin to be added in the webpack config.

```
const { VueLoaderPlugin } = require("vue-loader");
const webpack = require("@cypress/webpack-preprocessor");
const webpackOptions = {
....
plugins: [
    new VueLoaderPlugin()
  ]
};

const options = {
....
```

It would be nice to add this to the documentation to save others time.

Perhaps related issue:
https://github.com/bahmutov/cypress-vue-unit-test/issues/151 - [Someone ]( https://github.com/bahmutov/cypress-vue-unit-test/issues/151#issuecomment-441649778) posted a working code that already has the VueLoaderPlugin() in but it was not explicitly pointed out.

title: Test Runner: Expand and highlight matched get elements
body:
### What would you like?
When using the [test runner](https://docs.cypress.io/guides/core-concepts/test-runner.html#Spies), the get command returns all matches for an element which can be cycled through with the eq() method. This however can be improved if each match on the DOM snapshot could be labelled according to which index exactly it matches. 

### Why is this needed?
Usually the selection process for eq() method is to get all element matches then guess which element matches the eq() index from 0 to ... Lots of trial and error here that can be solved by labelling each element matched  y its index or by allowing the get log to expand into a more detailed list per item.

### Current behavior We have quite simple nextjs project where tried to use cypress to run [component tests](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/tree/master/npm/react) for our components. If using just plain JSX in our components without CSS imports, component tests work just fine. But when running cypress component tests for components which have CSS module imports, cypress fails to run the test and shows below error message in cypress window: **Title:** Error running plugin **Message:** The following error was thrown by a plugin. We stopped running your tests because a plugin crashed. Please check your plugins file (`/home/user/git/my-project/cypress/plugins/index.js`) **Details:** Error: Callback was already called. at throwError (/home/user/git/my-project/node_modules/neo-async/async.js:16:11) at /home/user/git/my-project/node_modules/neo-async/async.js:2818:7 at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:79:11) **Stack trace:** ``` Error: The following error was thrown by a plugin. We stopped running your tests because a plugin crashed. Please check your plugins file (`/home/user/git/my-project/cypress/plugins/index.js`) at Object.get (/home/user/.cache/Cypress/6.1.0/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/lib/errors.js:946:15) at EventEmitter.handleError (/home/user/.cache/Cypress/6.1.0/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/lib/plugins/index.js:159:20) at EventEmitter.emit (events.js:315:20) at ChildProcess. (/home/user/.cache/Cypress/6.1.0/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/lib/plugins/util.js:19:22) at ChildProcess.emit (events.js:315:20) at emit (internal/child_process.js:876:12) at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:85:21) ``` Above error message is not that good, but when running in debug mode, from console I noticed this error: ``` error: "No module factory available for dependency type: CssDependency" ``` So the above error and the fact that without CSS imports all is ok, indicates that something is wrong with cypress handling CSS imports in these tests. Our components work just fine in development server and also in storybook, so components should be just fine. I tried with just default nextjs config in our project without any special webpack configs and same issue persists, so config should also be fine. ### Desired behavior Should be able to run tests for components which import CSS without errors. Also cypress example components for example nextjs project should have some components which import CSS/SCSS in here: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/tree/master/npm/react/examples/nextjs/components . Now they are super simple components which have just some inline styles. But could also add there CSS module imports like these to verify that cypress can run tests against these components: https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/built-in-css-support#adding-component-level-css . CSS module imports are pretty basic stuff in nextjs and should work out of the box without any extra configurations. ### Test code to reproduce I have these files: MyComponentWithCss.tsx: ``` import React from "react" import styles from "./MyComponent.module.css" export interface MyComponentProps { value: string } export const MyComponentWithCss: React.FC = ({ value }) => { return

{value}

) cy.get("[data-test-id=testing]").should( "have.text", "testing this" ) }) }) ``` ### Versions Our configuration was done using instructions from https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/master/npm/react/docs/recipes.md: ``` // cypress/plugins/index.js module.exports = (on, config) => { require('@cypress/react/plugins/next')(on, config) // IMPORTANT to return the config object // with the any changed environment variables return config } ``` Cypress etc. versions from package.json: ``` "cypress": "6.1.0", "@cypress/react": "^4.16.0", "next": "10.0.3", "css-loader": "^5.0.0", "@babel/core": "^7.12.3", "react": "16.14.0", "react-dom": "16.14.0", "next-transpile-modules": "^4.1.0", "classnames": "^2.2.6", ```

body:

- Closes #9359 

### User facing changelog
<!-- Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog-->
We fixed an issue with `cy.intercept()` where multipart/form-data was wrongly encoded by the internal proxy, thus resulting in differences between the `content-length` header and the actual byte length of the request body buffer, which led to `Unexpected end of multipart data` errors on the backend service where the request was pointing to. Fixes #9359. 

### Additional details
#### Why was this change necessary?
This change is necessary because otherwise it is not possible to use `cy.intercept()` on multipart/form-data file upload requests. 
For a more technical answer please read my [comment](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/9359#issuecomment-747354545) on the issue.

#### What is affected by this change?
The `InterceptRequest` middleware and internal proxy are affected by these changes.

### How has the user experience changed?
The usage of cypress for the user has not changed.

title: Replacing cy.route with cy.intercept, having trouble with wildcard use
body:
I'm currently trying to rewrite a test using the deprecated cy.route command to use the cy.intercept command, but I'm having trouble getting the latter to work when using wildcards as part of the service reference. I'm currently running Cypress 6.1.0.

The code below is the old code that works properly.

```js
cy.server()
cy.route('GET', 'services/api/agenda/Appointment?id=**').as('appointmentService')
cy.wait('@appointmentService').should('have.property', 'status', 200)
```

I tried replacing it with the following code, but that results in a time-out:

```js
cy.intercept('GET', 'services/api/agenda/Appointment?id=**').as('appointmentService')
cy.wait('@appointmentService').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 200)
```

Curiously, if I try using a fixed id like in the code below, it DOES work. (though only once and only if other tests involving that part succeed, which is why I wanted to use a wildcard instead of a fixed id to begin with since the id changes every time a new appointment is created)

```js
cy.intercept('GET', 'services/api/agenda/Appointment?id=35').as('appointmentService')
cy.wait('@appointmentService').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 200)
```

Is this a technical issue or does the intercept command handle wildcards differently that I missed?

Cypress | Docker and cypress included 6.1.0, complains about missing plugins
body:
From following this helpful link: https://www.cypress.io/blog/2019/05/02/run-cypress-with-a-single-docker-command/

And mass googling (a few links as example):

https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-docker-images/issues/265

https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-docker-images/issues/178

I've managed to get the tests running correctly without plugin/support (by setting them to false in cypress config). BUT when I want to use cypress-axe to test accessibility and use docker, I receive the following.

The command to execute:

```
docker run -it -v $PWD:/e2e -w /e2e cypress/included:6.1.0 --spec "**/components/button.spec.js"
```

The resulting error:

```
Error: Cannot find module 'cypress-axe' from '/e2e/tests/UI/cypress/support'
This occurred while Cypress was compiling and bundling your test code. This is usually caused by:
- A missing file or dependency
- A syntax error in the file or one of its dependencies
Fix the error in your code and re-run your tests.
```

Also dependent on what version of the cypress included I use also get another error (I believe this error is coming from .babelrc, again missing plugin issue):

```
Error: Webpack Compilation Error
./tests/UI/cypress/integration/components/button.spec.js
Module build failed (from /root/.cache/Cypress/6.2.0/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/node_modules/babel-loader/lib/index.js):
Error: Cannot find module '@babel/plugin-syntax-dynamic-import'
```

So, by the looks of the errors it cannot find any installed plugin dependencies as the dependencies are not inside the image/container as of yet. Which makes sense. I was wondering is there a way to leverage the cypress-axe plugin all from this one command? Something like:
```
docker run -it -v $PWD:/e2e -w /e2e cypress/included:6.1.0 /bin/bash -c 'npm install cypress-axe && cypress run --spec "**/components/button.spec.js"'
```
BUT wanting to avoid creating a docker file and just use one command to run cypress inside docker and use plugins. Along with caching this as we do not want to install the plugins each time we run the command.

Any suggestions would be much appreciated!

title: chore(component-testing): Converting @cypress/react to use dev server plugin
body:
After merging, you can run `cy:open` and `cy:run` from the `npm/react` package.

Beware, in Open Mode the socket disconnect bug (currently CT-189) requires you to wait until the bundle is finished before interacting with the UI. Run mode does not have this problem. This bug is not as visible in `npm/vue` because the bundle is significantly smaller (2s instead of ~22s for React)

* adds cy:run and cy:open tasks to react
* hooks up `@cypress/react`'s component tests to use the dev server plugin.
* turns off a lot of the `specType === 'component'` checks
* moved hook logic from support.js to the top of the mount utility
* fixes existing cy:run task in Vue
* renaming `devserver` to `devServer (variables)` or `dev-server (strings, filenames)` for consistency

title: fix(component-testing): hot replace of dependencies of specs in component testing mode
body:
makes test re-run after every save of the spec file or any of the dependencies

closes CT-182 

- [x] made the logs a little cleaner by making webpack dev server logs optional. It was impossible to choose which logs were output by the dev server. Now if you want the dev server logs ON use ` DEBUG=cypress:webpack-dev-server:start` before your start the test server

### Testing steps

1. `yarn install` on root
1. `yarn install` on `/packages/server-ct/crossword-examples`
1. move to `/packages/server-ct`
1. start `yarn cypress:open`
1. open Cell.spec.js in cypress
1. open Cell.vue in code and change something in the code of the component
1. save 

It should re-run the tests in cypress

<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 
Hi,
Im trying to select the specific date in future in reservation site by clicking on next > in Date picker overlay. but im unable to select a date
can we use each in if block, i used but it works clicking 2 times but my selection date is based on 3rd click (April 31)
My code clicks on next twice only but i  need to see the April date by clicking on 3rd time.


### Current behavior
Im trying to select the specific date in future in reservation site by clicking on next > in Date picker overlay. but clicks on > twice and stops

### Desired behavior
From the Date calendar popup it should select April 31

### Test code to reproduce
import 'cypress-iframe'
import SearchPage from '../Aircanada/SearchPage'
describe('Aircanada TestSuite', function(){
 
it('Testcase02', function(){
    cy.visit('https://www.aircanada.com/ca/en/aco/home.html#/')
    cy.get('input#tripTypeField').click({force: true})
    cy.wait(3000)
    cy.get('ul.select-list').find('#tripTypeIdtripType_O').click()
    cy.get('span.flight-calendar-label').click()    
    cy.wait(2000)
    cy.get('.ui-datepicker-title').find('div').each(($monyear, index, $list) => 
    {
                if($monyear.text()==="April 2021")
                {

                        const date = $date.find('span.ui-calendar-date').text()
                        if(date==='31')

                    cy.wait(2000)
                    cy.get('a.ui-datepicker-next span:visible').find('span.sr-only').click({force: true})
                    cy.wait(2000) 
                    })
 
            })
})

title: fix: use stdio for CDP instead of TCP
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
-->
- TR-594
- Closes #6540
- Closes #7450
- Closes #8674
- Closes #8986

### User facing changelog

- Updated the CDP connection to attempt to use the stdio transport first with Chrome 72 and above, before falling back to using TCP. This should remediate issues causing sporadic 'Cypress failed to make a connection to the Chrome DevTools Protocol after retrying' errors.

### Additional details

- forked chrome-remote-interface to enable sessionId and stdio, see: https://github.com/cypress-io/chrome-remote-interface
	- upstream PRs: cyrus-and/chrome-remote-interface#440 cyrus-and/chrome-remote-interface#441
- using `CYPRESS_REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT` will force Cypress to use CDP in TCP mode
- warns and falls back to TCP if stdio cannot find a target after 60 seconds (default, can be configured with `CYPRESS_CDP_TARGET_TIMEOUT`)
	- i expect that some users wrap Cypress in a script that will sever stdio, but we'll see
- not removing TCP code yet since plugins rely on it/would potentially change our supported Chrome version

### How has the user experience changed?

- this warning: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1151760/104245028-719ffe80-545b-11eb-81b8-ae326c91e928.png)
- `CYPRESS_CDP_TARGET_TIMEOUT` (undocumented, like `CYPRESS_REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT`, since it's just for testing purposes)

N/A

Previously `cy.get('.error').should('be.empyt')` would be valid typescript and the typo would only be caught at runtime, rather than by the IDE or at compile-time. After this change `'be.empyt'` is highlighted as an error.

title: `Cypress run` similar CLI usage as Mocha: --bail and --exit
body:
There is a npm module available [cypress-fail-fast](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cypress-fail-fast), which enables fail fast in Cypress, skipping the rest of tests on first failure.

Since Cypress has structured is integrations the same way as Mocha test suites, then why does not `Cypress run` have the same rules and behaviors (CLI usage) as Mocha: https://mochajs.org/

```
  --bail, -b                 Abort ("bail") after first test failure   [boolean]
  --check-leaks              Check for global variable leaks           [boolean]
  --exit                     Force Mocha to quit after tests complete  [boolean]
```

title: Page load timeout will not fail the test if page is in redirection loop
body:
### Current behavior

Page load timeout will not stop the test if page is in redirection loop. The test may run forever. No log output is generated indicating what is happening.

Video: https://github.com/henrikauppinen/cypress-redirect-loop/blob/main/cypress/videos/redirect-loop.spec.js.mp4

The problem is obvious when looking at the UI but when this happens in headless mode in CI it may be extremely difficult to detect as the outcome may be just a long-running cypress process killed by CI.

We had a situation where tests completed successfully locally in headed mode and failed in CI. There was an oversight in test mocks and the application under test behaved differently in CI with drastically different performance constraints.

### Desired behavior
Page load timeout should trigger and stop the test even when page redirects continuously.

title: Test runner refreshes in middle of test when visiting a page whose superdomain is not the same as baseUrl.
body:
### Current behavior
When you `cy.visit` a page whose superdomain is different from `baseUrl`, the test runner reloads in the middle of a test and the test starts running again.

### Desired behavior
The test runner does not reload in the middle of a test causing the test to restart.

This is important in the application my organization is testing because the test setup steps (prior to visiting a page) are complex and make up a significant portion of the test time. Having them run twice adds significantly to our overall test runtime.

### Test code to reproduce

Using `cypress-test-tiny` as the starting point, set the `cypress.json` file to be
```
{
  "baseUrl": "https://en.wikipedia.org"
}
```
and create a spec file containing
```
describe('Runner Refresh in Middle of Test', () => {
  it('Issue', () => {
    cy.wait(5000)
    cy.visit('https://www.google.com/')
  })
})
```

Open Cypress, and run the spec file. You'll see the test load, the 5 second wait occur, and then when the `visit` action starts, the page reloads and the test starts running a second time. It does pass on the second run.

[Here's](https://share.vidyard.com/watch/JWMJ4T1aK7KrKjVu6JHjjW?) a video you can watch showing the refresh.

### Versions

I could reproduce this problem using Cypress 6.2.1 in Chrome/Edge/Election 87 and in Firefox 84 on macOS 10.15.7.

title: feat: change cy.intercept override behavior
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes #9302
- Closes #7788
- Closes #15209

### User facing changelog

- BREAKING CHANGE: Request handlers supplied to `cy.intercept` are now matched starting with the most-recently-defined request interceptor. This allows users to override request handlers by calling `cy.intercept` again. This matches the previous behavior that was standard in `cy.route`.
- There are now new events on the `req` object for `cy.intercept`: `before:response`, `response`, `after:response`.
- Response handlers (supplied via event handlers or via `req.continue(cb)`) supplied to `cy.intercept` will be called in reverse order until `res.send` is called or until there are no more response handlers. 
- A new option, `middleware`, has been added to the `RouteMatcher` type. If `true`, the supplied request handler will be called before any non-middleware request handlers.
- A new function, `req.continue(cb)`, is available on request objects yielded by `cy.intercept`. It is functionally the same as `req.reply(cb)` - the request will stop propagating to other event handlers, will be sent outgoing, and the response will be handled by `cb`.
- `cy.intercept` can now be called with a new overload: `cy.intercept(url, routeMatcher, handler)`. `routeMatcher` will be merged with `url`, and the handler is required.
- Fixed an issue where the `response.body` would be incorrect after stubbing a response using `res.send({ fixture })` in a `req.continue` callback or a `before:response` or `response` handler.

### Additional details

See changes to `net_stubbing_spec` for new + updated tests.

### How has the user experience changed?

* New `RouteMatcher` option: `middleware: boolean`
    * Handlers with `middleware: true` will be called in the order they are defined and chained.
    * With `middleware: true`, only dynamic handlers are supported - makes no sense to support `cy.intercept({ middleware: true }, staticResponse)`
* `req` now emits events (regardless of `middleware` setting)
* Events on `req`: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/762d6eb22d27e371e3d004bac76543800b236640/packages/net-stubbing/lib/external-types.ts#L207-L226
* `req.continue(cb)` has been added. `req.reply(cb)` still works.
* A third overload of `cy.intercept` has been added, to allow users to more easily do things like `cy.intercept('/url', { middleware: true }, ...)` to set middleware, etc: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/042050c460a16293fd707d362eeb7bce68f3e268/packages/net-stubbing/lib/external-types.ts#L459-L470

title: Intercepted calls are queued before cy.wait
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
<!-- A description including screenshots, stack traces, DEBUG logs, etc. 👉 https://on.cypress.io/troubleshooting -->
After calling an intercept for method and path and assigning it an alias, all calls intercepted in this manner are stored in a queue form rather than stacked as I would expect. Meaning if 2 such calls are intercepted but the first one isn't interacted with via `.wait(<alias>)`, then interacting with the second call in this way will return information from the first one instead.

In larger, more complex app and testing code base, it is easy to unintentionally intercept a different, unwanted call prior to interacting with the desired one. So this behaviour is not ideal for that.

### Desired behavior
<!-- Remember, we are not familiar with the application you're testing, so please provide a clear description of what should happen.-->
Intercepted call should be rather stacked or possible those that aren't being interacted with forgotten. Maybe ideally there should be an option parameter to define which of these approaches will be used.

### Test code to reproduce
<!-- Provide test code that we can copy, paste, and run on our machine to see the issue. -->

<!-- You could also provide a repo that we can clone and run. You can fork 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-test-tiny repo, set up a failing test, then link to your fork. -->
```js
const baseUrl = 'https://swapi.dev';

const enterRequest = (path: string) => cy.get('[type="text"]').clear().type(path);

const sendRequest = () => cy.contains('button', 'request').click();

it('processes the intercepted requests in a queue', () => {
  cy.visit(baseUrl);

  cy.intercept({method: 'GET', path: '/api/people/*'}).as('getPeople')

  enterRequest('people/4/');
  sendRequest();
  // intercepted but not waiting for the getPeople here, let's assume I am not interested in this one

  enterRequest('people/6/');
  sendRequest();
  // same situation here

  enterRequest('people/10/');
  sendRequest()

title: fix: Improve uncaught error handling
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist

- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes #243
- Closes #8802
- Partially addresses #8236

### User facing changelog

- Cypress now catches uncaught errors and fails the test even if the app-under-test has defined `window.onerror`.
- Cypress now fails tests if there is an unhandled promise rejection in the app-under-test. Unhandled rejections will trigger the `uncaught:exception` event with the promise as the third argument.

### Additional details

Instead of use `window.onerror` to catch uncaught errors, we now use `window.addEventListener('error')`. Before, if the app overwrote `window.onerror`, we would no longer catch any uncaught errors, but that's no longer the case. 

We also now use `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection')` to catch and fail if there's an unhandled promise rejection.

### How has the user experience changed?
<!-- Provide before and after examples of the change.
Screenshots or GIFs are preferred. -->
If a user's app overwrote `window.onerror` or had unhandled rejections, tests will fail that trigger errors/unhandled rejections. They will need to fix those errors in their app or return false from `uncaught:exception` to get those tests to pass.

title: Documentation and types do not reflect behaviour of `then` when returning element
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
Given

```ts
const event = new Event('click');

cy.get('div')
  .then((el$) => {
    const el: HTMLDivElement = el$[0];
    return el;
  })
  .then((el) => el.dispatchEvent(event));
```

This _doesn't_ produce a TypeScript type error.

At runtime it throws an exception:

```
TypeError: el.dispatchEvent is not a function
```

This appears to happen because `el` is not actually a `HTMLDivElement`, despite what TypeScript thinks. It's actually a `JQuery` wrapped element.

### Desired behavior
- This should produce a type error at compile time (i.e. the types need to reflect the runtime behaviour).
- This "wrapping" behaviour should be documented [on the page for `then`](https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/then.html).

### Test code to reproduce
See above

title: Is it possible that Cypress is interfering with Django/JS webapp network requests?
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
Have been using Cypress for end-to-end testing in a Django (2.2)/JS application that uses Pdf.js and Tesseract to perform some conversions. Setup includes Webpack and Babel. One of the hurdles of this environment is that requests that involve Tesseract often require a long time to perform, which tends to be challenging for Cypress, but ok.

My issue is that in one test a completely unexpected behaviour seems to happen: the main (and longest, waiting time set at 140 seconds) _request gets fired twice during Cy tests_, while it does not during manual testing. This causes the server to hang for much longer and the test to fail. 

To try and exclude that this could come from other sources, and to reproduce the issue, I created a new test that performs all of the tested operations before the actual request (fired with a cy.get().click() ): when cy.get().click() is performed the server behaves as described and falls into a loop, while if the click is manual the server behaves normally and completes the request.
(I both checked that there is no strange bubbling of the click event nor double clicking, and placed an explicit control in the JS code for good measure.)

Is it possible that the cy.wait command interferes with the requests? I ask this because on the server it is obvious that it received a second one but I could not find any reason for this to happen.

This is the portion of code for the request part that fails, the one that if performed manually succeeds:

```
export const finalize = (est_time_in_s=20) => {

  cy
    .get("#currentPage")
    .invoke('attr', 'data-currpage')
    .then( page =>
      cy.log(`page ${page} running Finalize, est t: ${est_time_in_s}s /////////////`))


  cy
    .get('#finalize_conversion')
    .click()

  cy                    // main waiting part
    .wait(est_time_in_s * 1000)
    .wait('@sendToBackend')
    .then(({ request, response }) => {

      cy.log('request:\n', request)
      cy.log('response:\n', response)

      expect(response.statusCode).to.eq(200)

    })


  cy                                // checks that the button has modified its text
    .get('#finalize_conversion')
    .then( b => {

      cy.log('b is:', b)
      cy.log('b[0].innerText:', b[0].innerText)

      if (b[0].innerText != 'View conversion') {                    // in case it has not waits a little longer

        cy.wait(11 * 1000)

      } else {

        cy                                                                          // otherwise it fires a different request
          .get('#finalize_conversion')                                 // it never fulfills this one.
          .should('contain', 'View conversion')
          .click()

      }

    })




  cy
    .wait('@show')
    .then(({ request, response}) => {

      expect(response.statusCode).to.eq(200)

    })

}
```

As you might notice this is a module that gets imported inside the main test. In the failing test time to wait is set at 140 * 1000, i.e. 140s.

This the code setting up the intercept alias:
```
  before( () => cy.noUIlogin() )

  beforeEach(() => {
    Cypress.Cookies.preserveOnce(
      "sessionid",
      "csrftoken"
    );


    cy
      .intercept('POST', '/rectdata').as('sendToBackend')
      .intercept('GET', '/docs/show_simple_hocr/').as('show')


    cy.fileUploadInteractiveConversion(
      '../../../media/Test_collection-1.pdf')

  });
```
This is [an image of the results of the test](https://paste.pics/95d961c500f11b88687c67b2b0d32b60)



### Desired behavior
The request should complete, as it does in other tests and in this one if fired by clicking manually instead than through a cy.click() command

### Test code to reproduce
Unavailable, sigh. It would require the entire code base.

### Versions
Cy: 6.4.0
Browser: Chrome 88.0.4324.150 (official Build) (64 bit)
OS: Fedora 33 (updated)
Python 3.8.2
Django: 2, 2, 5, 'final'
webpack: ^4.43.0
npm: ^7.3.0

Thanks in advance for any support.

PS: A small but maybe relevant detail is that if I perform the manual click from within the Cypress Chrome browser, it still does not complete. While doing so on the same document in a regular Chrome instance it does. Everything else being equal, at least as far as I know.

title: fix: use app.whenReady and remove delay race for electron startup
body:
This change fixes an issue that caused the startup to be delayed by 500ms.
We used `app.on('ready')` without checking `app.isReady()`, however the
'ready' event may already have fired at this point and thus we never
resolved the Promise waiting for it.
Using `app.whenReady` fixes this and now that Promise resolves before
the delay expires.

Related links:

https://www.electronjs.org/docs/api/app#event-ready
https://www.electronjs.org/docs/api/app#appwhenready

- Closes <!-- issue number here. e.g. "Closes #1234" -->

title: JUnit result should contain browser name
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to request a feature. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### What would you like?
In the file `cypress.json` I configured the reporter using these settings:
```
{
  "reporter": "junit",
  "reporterOptions": {
    "mochaFile": "result/result-[hash].xml",
    "testsuitesTitle": "Cypress Tests"
  }
}
```

When executing the tests everything works as expected and the spec reporter shows some informations about the browser being used, something like this:

```
====================================================================================================

  (Run Starting)

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Cypress:    6.4.0                                                                              │
  │ Browser:    Chrome 88 (headless)                                                               │
  │ Specs:      1 found (sample.e2e.spec.ts)                                                       │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

When using the junit reporter the result looks like this:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<testsuites name="Cypress Tests" time="3.1030" tests="1" failures="0">
  <testsuite name="Root Suite" timestamp="2021-02-22T13:27:07" tests="0" file="src\integration\sample.e2e.spec.ts" time="0.0000" failures="0">
  </testsuite>
  <testsuite name="Test for login page" timestamp="2021-02-22T13:27:07" tests="1" time="3.1030" failures="0">
    <testcase name="Test for login page should check login url successfully" time="3.1030" classname="should check login url successfully">
    </testcase>
  </testsuite>
</testsuites>
```

When executing the tests against different browsers its impossible to say which result files are from which browser because there is no browser information available.

In the same project I'm also using [Karma-JUnit-Reporter](https://github.com/karma-runner/karma-junit-reporter) which is nearly the same reporter and by setting `useBrowserName` to true its possible to embed some browser information into the resulting file. This looks like this:

```
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<testsuite name="Chrome Headless 88.0.4324.182 (Windows 10)" package="" timestamp="2021-02-19T09:55:12" id="0" hostname="wchorsta4" tests="3871" errors="0" failures="0" time="206.499">
  <properties>
    <property name="browser.fullName" value="Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) HeadlessChrome/88.0.4324.182 Safari/537.36"/>
  </properties>
  <testcase name="Tests for login page" time="0.242" classname="Chrome_Headless_88_0_4324_182_(Windows_10).Tests for login page"/>
  ...
```

As you can see it adds the browser name and os to the testsuite attribute and adds a property to the property list. I think Cypress should handle this the same way.

### Why is this needed?
This is needed for CI purposes. I'm trying to setup a CI pipeline which runs the tests against multiple browsers like Firefox and Chrome. For this it is needed to identify the browsers within the resulting files.

title: Static replies in Intercept drop falsy values
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
<!-- A description including screenshots, stack traces, DEBUG logs, etc. 👉 https://on.cypress.io/troubleshooting -->
Currently, if a falsy, but not `undefined`, value is passed as a static response such as `req.reply({ body: false })`, the boolean value is dropped by the net-stubbing backend. This behavior does not match up with the behavior for `true`, where `req.reply({ body: true })` will return `true`.

### Desired behavior
<!-- Remember, we are not familiar with the application you're testing, so please provide a clear description of what should happen.-->
At the very least, there should be consistency in how net-stubbing handles boolean values. I see two reasonable options:

1. Return falsy static responses. This would provide consistent behavior with truthy values of the same type.
2. Throw a runtime error when non object or string values are used as static responses. Currently, when falsy values are dropped, a response is returned without any indication that something went wrong.

I think the first option is the preferable one, and while the type definition for static responses only includes strings and JSON objects, I expect others might also be implicitly relying on `req.reply` to handle other types like `boolean`s or `numbers`.

I have a [branch](https://github.com/jeremydorne/cypress/commit/f47c0348ec4376fcc77dc34c7635efc24a15a456) that adds a couple `undefined` checks in place of truthy `checks` that would match fix #1.

### Test code to reproduce
[This](https://github.com/jeremydorne/cypress/commit/f47c0348ec4376fcc77dc34c7635efc24a15a456#diff-801bb85bee26e7f7d674e624fae1fe6583afac01bd5de659b60f928783a3429eR763) is a test case that describes the current behavior. 

### Versions

Cypress 6.x

title: cy.exec always exits with code 1 and no output
body:
### Current behavior
I am new to Cypress trying to test a VSCode extension.
When I run `cy.exec('ls')`, the test runner exits with code 1, and empty strings for `stderr` and `stdout`. I've tried giving it an absolute path (`'/bin/ls'`), and also tried giving it gibberish ('`asdf`'), and I get the same result each time.

I'm running Cypress with `sudo` because it was breaking at the `--no-sandbox` flag as referenced in [this issue](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/4624): `DEBUG=cypress:* sudo node_modules/.bin/cypress open`



### Desired behavior
I want Cypress to either run the command or give me sensible output telling me why it's failing.

### Versions
Cypress package version: 6.6.0
Cypress binary version: 6.6.0
Electron version: 11.2.3
Bundled Node version: 12.18.3

### Impact
Passing HTML containing `<option>` elements from untrusted sources - even after sanitizing them - to one of jQuery's DOM manipulation methods (i.e. `.html()`, `.append()`, and others) may execute untrusted code.

### Patches
This problem is patched in jQuery 3.5.0.

### Workarounds
To workaround this issue without upgrading, use [DOMPurify](https://togithub.com/cure53/DOMPurify) with its `SAFE_FOR_JQUERY` option to sanitize the HTML string before passing it to a jQuery method.

### Impact
Passing HTML from untrusted sources - even after sanitizing it - to one of jQuery's DOM manipulation methods (i.e. `.html()`, `.append()`, and others) may execute untrusted code.

### Patches
This problem is patched in jQuery 3.5.0.

### Workarounds
To workaround the issue without upgrading, adding the following to your code:

jQuery.htmlPrefilter = function( html ) {

};

While investigating https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/15323 I stumbled upon a bug in desktop gui

```

title: feat: create new spec file from desktop-gui
body: - Closes GROW-173 ### User facing changelog Adds the ability to create a new spec file directly from the desktop gui ### Additional details **Dialog needs to be tested on Windows and Linux.** I had some issues when trying to run myself - while I'm confident it probably works well, its not a bad idea to test on the native system before merging. We use the system dialog to prompt for file location rather than a custom file picker since there are a number of benefits (eg. create folder, duplicate detection) that come with using the system dialog rather than a custom implementation (and there's no need to reinvent the wheel). The only downside (for less experienced users) is that the user is able to create a file outside of their Cypress project, which means it may not show up in their spec list. The system dialog provides no way to limit the user to selecting certain directories, so the best we can do is show is put them in their integration folder by default and show a message if they choose to add a file outside of their spec list (which some advanced users might actually want to do). After creating a file in the integrations folder, the new file will scroll into view and get highlighted for a second. Do docs need to be written for this? I feel like it's fairly self explanatory but we do document basically everything (and could give us a place to explain in a bit more detail why only recognized spec files in the integrations folder will show up). This should pair nicely with the changes introduced in #15144, especially once Studio hits GA. With Studio, a user is able to download Cypress for the first time and write a test without ever needing to open their filesystem or IDE. ### How has the user experience changed? Creating a new file ![ezgif-4-609b97b5ef41](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7033952/110398994-00d42780-8043-11eb-9081-c1cce92af10a.gif) Message when file is created in a different directory Content of created file ```js // spec_name.js created with Cypress // // Start writing your Cypress tests below! // If you're unfamiliar with how Cypress works, // check out the link below and learn how to write your first test: // https://on.cypress.io/writing-first-test ``` ### PR Tasks - [x] Have tests been added/updated? - [x] Has the original issue or this PR been tagged with a release in ZenHub? - [ ] Has a PR for user-facing changes been opened in [`cypress-documentation`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-documentation)?

title: `Cypress.Cookies.defaults()` return type is `void` but the code does return a value
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to request a feature. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### What would you like?
<!-- A clear description of the feature or enhancement wanted in Cypress -->
`Cypress.Cookies.defaults()` allow to preserve some cookies during the test execution.  

However, there is no official way to extend the existing list of defaults.

`Cypress.Cookies.defaults()` return the default object but the type tells it returns `void`

Ideally the returnType of `Cypress.Cookies.defaults()` should be change, or a method to retrieve defaults could be added

### Why is this needed?
<!-- Remember, we are not familiar with the application you are testing, so please provide a clear description of why this would be useful to your project. -->

We have a cypress plugin doing some user authentication.  
This plugin uses `Cypress.Cookies.defaults()` to make sure the authentication is working.  

In our code, we also have a special cookie that we set and we could like it to be preserved.

With current types it seems impossible.  

However, we can "hack" something because `Cypress.Cookies.defaults()`  does return a value:

```js
// the Cypress type wrongly says the default method is returning void.
		// in fact it returns the destination object (because the implementation is based on _.extends)
		// see https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/c12347dc9c4f9dc0662ad9350536c6c6b99225c4/packages/driver/src/cypress/cookies.js#L144
		// thanks to this hack we can extend the existing defaults and add our cookie
		const currentDefault = Cypress.Cookies.defaults({}) as unknown as Partial<Cypress.CookieDefaults> | undefined;
		if (currentDefault && 'preserve' in currentDefault) {
			const { preserve } = currentDefault;
			const toPreserve = [];
			if (Array.isArray(preserve)) {
				toPreserve.push(...preserve, USERNAME_COOKIE);
			} else if (typeof preserve === 'string') {
				toPreserve.push(preserve, USERNAME_COOKIE);
			} else if (!preserve) {
				toPreserve.push(USERNAME_COOKIE);
			} else {
				throw new Error(`could not extend the existing Cypress.Cookies.defaults, received: ${JSON.stringify(currentDefault)}`);
			}
			Cypress.Cookies.defaults({ preserve: toPreserve });
			cy.log(`Preserved cookies: ${toPreserve.join()}`);
		} else {
			// because this whole solution is hack, let's be verbose in case of failure
			throw new Error(`could not fetch the existing Cypress.Cookies.defaults, received: ${JSON.stringify(currentDefault)}`);
		}
```
