-->

- Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/CT-305?focusedCommentId=13398

Note: This behavior and API was discussed over the course of two meetings and validated with Brian, Zach, and Jess. 

### User facing changelog

<!-- Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog-->

## 1. Add support for runner specific overrides in `cypress.json`. Like this:

```bash
// cypress.json
{
    // defaults
    video: true,

    // added this e2e key
    e2e: {
	  video: false // override!
	},

    // added component
    component: { 
      viewportWidth: 500 // video is true - inherited.
    }
}
```

## 2. Pass `mode` to plugins function

Note the third argument is `mode`. This is `component` or `e2e`. The user can have conditional plugins using this flag.

```js

module.exports = (on, config, mode) => {
  if (mode === 'component') {
    // start webpack-dev-server, etc.
  }

  if (mode === 'e2e') {
    // e2e things
  }

  // You still need to return a config file.
  // e2e or CT specific config can be done in `cypress.json` using `e2e` or `component` keys.
  return config
}
```



### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

It's very useful now that we have two runners, CT and E2E.

### How has the user experience changed?

You can have runner specific config, and runner specific plugins.

- Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/CT-305?focusedCommentId=13398

Note: Some other changes here to support create-cypress-tests wizard. Ignore those for the purpose of this review.

### User facing changelog

<!-- Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog-->

## 1. Add support for runner specific overrides in `cypress.json`. Like this:

```bash
// cypress.json
{
    // defaults
    video: true,

    // added this e2e key
    e2e: {
	  video: false // override!
	},

    // added component
    component: { 
      viewportWidth: 500 // video is true - inherited.
    }
}
```

## 2. Pass `testingType` to `config` in plugin function 

`config` now includes a `testingType` property. It is either `e2e` or `component`. The user can have conditional plugins using this flag.

```js

module.exports = (on, config) => {
  if (config.testingType === 'component') {
    // start webpack-dev-server, etc.
  }

  if (config.testingType === 'e2e') {
    // e2e things
  }

  // You still need to return a config file.
  // e2e or CT specific config can be done in `cypress.json` using `e2e` or `component` keys.
  return config
}
```



### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

It's very useful now that we have two runners, CT and E2E.

title: [@cypress/react] React 17 support for support configuration
body:
### Current behavior
I am adding `cypress` and `@cypress/react` to an existing project which uses React 17. It works as expected when using the [using-babel-typescript template](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/tree/develop/npm/react/examples/using-babel-typescript) and changing `'@babel/preset-react'` so be `['@babel/preset-react': {runtime: 'automatic'}]` to make use of React 17's `_jsx` automatic import fanciness, which the project uses for all its components already. However, when I try and create a centralised `cy.mount` helper along the lines of:
```js
import { mount } from '@cypress/react';
import { ReactElement } from 'react';
import Wrapper from '/path/to/Wrapper';

Cypress.Commands.add('mount', (component) => {
  return mount(<Wrapper>{component}</Wrapper>);
});
```
I get the following error in Cypress:
```
The following error originated from your application code, not from Cypress.

  > Invalid hook call. Hooks can only be called inside of the body of a function component. This could happen for one of the following reasons:
1. You might have mismatching versions of React and the renderer (such as React DOM)
2. You might be breaking the Rules of Hooks
3. You might have more than one copy of React in the same app
See https://reactjs.org/link/invalid-hook-call for tips about how to debug and fix this problem.
```
After playing with various different scenarios this seems to be because support files are bundled separately without the custom plugin for bundling components, so it is referencing the usual "classic" react import instead of the new `_jsx` version.

### Desired behavior
"@cypress/react" has a peerDependency on React 16, so I guess the ideal scenario is 1st class React 17 support and the ability to use `runtime: 'automatic'` for support bundling.

### Test code to reproduce
Repro configs provided in the [Current behavior](#current-behaviour) section.

### Versions

`@cypress/react`: 4.16.4
`cypress`: 6.8.0
`@cypress/webpack-dev-server`: 1.1.0
`react`: 17.0.1
`react-dom`: 17.0.1

body:

-->

- Closes #3738

### User facing changelog

- `cy.click()` will no longer fail with "coordsHistory must be at least 2 sets of coords" when specifying `{ multiple: true }`

### Additional details

There was a bug where using `cy.click({ multiple: true })` would time out because all clicks needed to be finished in the time we normally give one click (4000ms by default). If the system was slow, the timeout was lowered, and/or there were a lot of elements to click, this became more likely.

Now, each click when using `{ multiple: true }` gets a full timeout (4000ms).

Also, the error message "coordsHistory must be at least 2 sets of coords" was confusing and not useful to users. It appeared because it happened to be the error we use to trigger an initial retry in order to test that the element is not animating between ticks. I improved the error, though with the timeout change, it's very, very unlikely now that a user will encounter it.

### How has the user experience changed?

The main experience change is that users shouldn't have to worry about click timeouts for multiple elements since each click now has more time to execute.

With the timeout change, it's much less likely users will encounter this new error message, but in case they somehow do, here's the before and after:

title: feat: make cy.intercept url matching more closely match cy.route
body:
- Closes ### User facing changelog - Removed `matchUrlAgainstPath` `RouteMatcher` property. - Removed the "substring match" from `cy.intercept` URL matching. Previously, a URL would match if it contained the supplied string anywhere. Now, the URL (incl. querystring) only matches if it is an equality match or a minimatch. ### Additional details ### How has the user experience changed? - Removed `matchUrlAgainstPath` since it's redundant, removing it doesn't break any use case. - Substring match was removed because it ends up capturing more than the user intends. - The most likely place this will trip users up: querystrings. Previously, `cy.intercept('/widgets')` would match `/widgets?limit=50`. Now it does not. This matches `cy.route`'s behavior, but now requires the user to do something like `cy.intercept('/widgets?limit=*')` or `cy.intercept({ pathname: '/widgets' })` #### Table of changes:
Does the request match?
Code Request path Before this PR After this PR
cy.intercept('/widgets') /widgets?limit=50 :heavy_check_mark: :x:
cy.intercept('/filename') /directory/filename :heavy_check_mark: :x:

title: Stubbing window.open doesn't work with redirects
body: I am working with Cypress, and I have a test with the following flow: 1. Cypress gets a button and clicks it, which submits a form 2. Form redirects to a "loading" url, which then redirects to another url 3. On the last page, there is a single line of inline JavaScript: ```javascript window.open("https://mockurl.com/", "_blank", "menubar=no,status=no"); ``` 4. This line opens a print dialog immediately on page load, so tests will hang until the dialog is manually closed. I cannot seem to find a way to deal with this print dialog and prevent it from opening each time. I'm stubbing window.open like so: ```javascript cy.visit('index.html', { onBeforeLoad: (win) => { cy.stub(win, 'open'); } }) cy.window().then(function (win) { cy.get('button').click() cy.contains('This is the last page').then(() => { expect(win.open).to.be.called }) }) ``` ### Current behavior I get this error: `[Function: open] is not a spy or a call to a spy!` The popup appears normally and the test process hangs until the dialog is manually closed. ### Desired behavior Cypress should detect the popup, and it should not appear, allowing tests to continue running. ### Test code to reproduce [Repo with sample code.](https://github.com/Koenshi/cypress-popup) This includes an index.html with a button, which when clicked navigates to redirect.html, that after 2 seconds navigates to info.html. This last page, info.html, has the inline javascript that opens popup.html. ### Versions Cypress 6.8.0 Chrome 89 MacOS Big Sur 11.2.3

title: Intercept data is empty for 304 status codes
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
<!-- A description including screenshots, stack traces, DEBUG logs, etc. 👉 https://on.cypress.io/troubleshooting -->

When an intercepted route has a 304 status code (i.e. has been retrieved from the browser cache), the response data is empty:

```typescript
    cy.wait('@list-users').then((interception) => {
      console.log('Intercepted:', interception); 
      console.log('Intercepted request:', interception.request); 
      console.log('Intercepted response:', interception.response); 
      
      // This body object is an empty string for 304 status codes.
      console.log('Intercepted response data:', interception.response?.body); 
    });
```

The current workaround (proposed in #14277) is to delete the `if-none-match` header:

```typescript
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/users*', (req) => {
    delete req.headers['if-none-match'];
  }).as('list-users');
```

On an even higher level, I don't believe that the `interception.response` should have a 304 status code at all. In the Cypress logs, there are only ever 200 status codes:

![cypress-intercept-bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20798889/112706505-dca98080-8e61-11eb-9a58-98829978d5a3.png)

You'll notice ☝️ that Cypress seems to log two of each request. One as an `(xhr)` request to `/api/users` with a 200 status code and the other as a `(req)` to `http://localhost:3000/api/users` (this second `(req)` is the one that is intercepted by Cypress).

I'm a little confused by this as well... Why are there two of each request? Which of those two requests is Cypress actually returning data for in `cy.wait()`?

### Desired behavior
<!-- Remember, we are not familiar with the application you're testing, so please provide a clear description of what should happen.-->

The response body for requests with 304 status codes should be the same as the original 200 status code response body. The HTTP response exposed by `cy.wait()` should have the same data as the HTTP response that is used by our application.

Again, on a higher level, Cypress should only log a single request (with a 200 status code), instead of logging both an `(xhr)` and a `(req)` event for the same HTTP request.

### Test code to reproduce
<!-- Provide test code that we can copy, paste, and run on our machine to see the issue. -->

<!-- You could also provide a repo that we can clone and run. You can fork 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-test-tiny repo, set up a failing test, then link to your fork. -->

The original repository is [`tutorbookapp/tutorbook`](https://github.com/tutorbookapp/tutorbook) (completely open-source).

The test in question is in [`cypress/tests/org/users/index.spec.ts`](https://github.com/tutorbookapp/tutorbook/blob/develop/cypress/tests/org/users/index.spec.ts) but the same issue is happening everywhere I use `cy.intercept()` in conjunction with `cy.wait()`.

We did not support Electron in the Component Test Runner. This means that users would have needed to install Chrome on their CI machines, which isn't acceptable. Now, we support Electron, Chrome, and Firefox.

I tried to refactor server/lib/browsers.js to make sure the instance wasn't cached so we couldn't destroy it twice, but this led to other test failures.

Rather than risk deeper breaking changes, we limited the fix so that we only tear down the browser when we're not in Electron. This behaves as expected.

title: cy.fixture using 'this' context not working as per the documentation
Support application/xhtml+xml content-type in cy.visit() command
body:
### What would you like?
The `cy.visit()` command only supports text/html response content-type or documents which can be parsed as HTML. We need the ability to support XHTML documents by allowing response content-type containing `application/xhtml+xml.*` and avoid the following error message.

```
cy.visit() failed trying to load:

http://localhost:5000/index.xhtml

The content-type of the response we received from your web server was:

  > application/xhtml+xml

This was considered a failure because responses must have content-type: 'text/html'
```

### Why is this needed?
Our applications run on some devices that use XHTML, which is a stricter extension of HTML based on XML, which browsers can render in the same way as text/html documents.

The content type is allowed in the accept header, but does not seem to be allowed on the response content-type. The current code that checks if the response body looks like html seems to fail to detect it as XHTML documents often begin with XML declarations.

I have had success asserting on-screen elements of XHTML documents with Cypress by disabling the current error messages and will submit a PR allowing the `application/xhtml+xml.*` response content-type.

title: Can't run Typescript tests in Cypress when I have @cypress/webpack-batteries-included-preprocessor enabled
body:
### Current behavior
Because of this [issue](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8373) we have to use `@cypress/webpack-batteries-included-preprocessor enabled` in our setup. This looks like this: 
// cypress/plugins/
```typescript
import webpackPreprocessor from '@cypress/webpack-batteries-included-preprocessor'
module.exports = (on: (arg0: string, arg1: any) => void, config: { env: { ENVIRONMENT: any } }) => {
    // We need to enable webpack preprocessing because Webpack doesn't play nice with
    // Swagger generated clients: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8373
    const options = webpackPreprocessor.defaultOptions

    options.webpackOptions.module.rules.push({
        parser: { amd: false },
    })

    on('file:preprocessor', webpackPreprocessor(options))
    // other unrelated stuff

}
```
We have 2 `tsconfig.json` files in the project. 
If we don't set `tsconfig.json` in the root folder, then we get : 
```
TypeError: Cannot read property 'defaultOptions' of undefined
    at module.exports (/Users/andrew/Work/New10/Testing/cypress/cypress/plugins/index.ts:43:41)
```

Root `tsconfig.json` looks like this : 

```json
{
  "extends": "@new10com/new10-standard/tsconfig.base.json",
  "include": [
    "cypress/**/*.ts",
    "cypress/**/.*.ts",
    "index.d.ts"
  ],
  "exclude": [".vscode", "deploy", "node_modules/**"],
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "allowJs": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "types": ["cypress"],
    "typeRoots": ["./typings", "./node_modules/@types"],
    "rootDir": ".",
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "noEmit": false,
    "lib": ["esnext.asynciterable", "esnext", "dom", "es5"]
  }
}
```
Cypress tsconfig.json looks like this:

// cypress/tsconfig.json
```json
{
  "extends": "../tsconfig.json",
  "include": ["./**/*.ts", "./**/*.*.ts", "@cypress/webpack-batteries-included-preprocessor"],
  "exclude": [],
  "compilerOptions": {
    "rootDir": "../",
    "types": ["cypress"],
    "lib": ["es2015", "dom"],
    "isolatedModules": false,
    "allowJs": true,
    "noEmit": true

}
```

If we have webpack preprocessor enabled, then at the run of typescript spec we get this error:
```
Error: You are attempting to run a TypeScript file, but do not have TypeScript installed. Ensure you have 'typescript' installed to enable TypeScript support.

The file: /Users/andrew/Work/New10/Testing/cypress/cypress/integration/regular/smokeTests/signup-user.spec.ts

    at tryCatcher (/Users/andrew/Library/Caches/Cypress/6.8.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/server/node_modules/bluebird/js/release/util.js:16:23)
    at Function.Promise.attempt.Promise.try (/Users/andrew/Library/Caches/Cypress/6.8.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/server/node_modules/bluebird/js/release/method.js:39:29)
    at Object.wrapChildPromise (/Users/andrew/Library/Caches/Cypress/6.8.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/server/lib/plugins/util.js:40:23)
    at Object.wrap (/Users/andrew/Library/Caches/Cypress/6.8.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/server/lib/plugins/child/preprocessor.js:28:8)
    at execute (/Users/andrew/Library/Caches/Cypress/6.8.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/server/lib/plugins/child/run_plugins.js:119:27)
    at EventEmitter.<anonymous> (/Users/andrew/Library/Caches/Cypress/6.8.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/server/lib/plugins/child/run_plugins.js:202:5)
    at EventEmitter.emit (events.js:315:20)

    at process.emit (/Users/andrew/Library/Caches/Cypress/6.8.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/server/node_modules/source-map-support/source-map-support.js:495:21)

But js specs that use our generated API client work just fine. 

If will disable preprocessing, then typescript spec runs just fine, but specs with generated API client will fail just like described in [issue](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8373)

- The events `before:spec`, `after:spec`, `before:run`, and `after:run` can now fire in interactive mode in addition to run mode. This requires the `experimentalInteractiveRunEvents` flag to be enabled.


### Additional details

* `before:run` fires when opening a project. It has more limited system information than in run mode.
* `before:spec` fires when the browser opens
* `after:spec` fires when the browser closes (and may not fire at all (if, for example, you force quit Cypress). It only has the spec argument and not the results.
* `after:run` fires when you close the project (and may not fire at all (if, for example, you force quit Cypress). It does not have the results argument.

title: [7.0.0] cy.intercept(): stubbed responses still send request to server
body:
### Current behavior
After upgrading from 6.7.1 to 7.0.0, I noticed my tests are still working as expected, but my server logs show requests being made to my server for intercepted requests using fixtures, objects, or strings.
```
    cy.intercept('/api/getThings', { fixture: 'getThings' });
    cy.intercept('/api/getAnotherThing', 'AnotherThing');
    cy.intercept('/api/getYetAnotherThing', { text: 'YetAnotherThing' });
```
Each of these intercepts _will_ return the stubbed response, but the requests are still being made afterward.

Example server log:
```
GET /api/getThings 200 4.389 ms - -
error: GET - 500 - /api/getThings -- some error because I'm not using a live service
GET /api/getAnotherThing 200 2.312 ms - -
error: GET - 500 - /api/getThings -- some error because I'm not using a live service
GET /api/getYetAnotherThing 200 4.231 ms - -
error: GET - 500 - /api/getYetAnotherThing -- some error because I'm not using a live service
```

### Desired behavior
The requests should NOT go to the server after returning the stubbed response.
```
GET /api/getThings 200 4.389 ms - -
GET /api/getAnotherThing 200 2.312 ms --
GET /api/getYetAnotherThing 200 4.231 ms --
```

### Current workaround
`req.reply` works as expected, blocking the requests to the server.
```
    cy.intercept('/api/getThings', (req) => req.reply({ fixture: 'getThings' }));
    cy.intercept('/api/getAnotherThing', (req) => req.reply('AnotherThing'));
    cy.intercept('/api/getYetAnotherThing', (req) => req.reply({ text: 'YetAnotherThing' }));
```

### Versions
7.0.0

title: cy.fixture fails if file extension does not match casing (only CI)1
body:
* Host a file like "FILE.txt" in the fixtures folder
* Write a test which includes the following. Notice how the extension for the file is written in uppercase:
`cy.fixture('FILE.TXT')`
* Run the test in both local UI and in CI (Issue seen in GitLab)

**Observed behaviour**
When running in local UI the file is found as expected
When running in CI, the test fails, stating "FILE.TXT" can not be found.

**Expected**
The behaviour for both local UI and CI should be the same.
Ideally, both runners should not be caps lock sensitive, at least on the extension of the file

**Workaround**
1. Change the extension to have the same casing as the file
2. Remove the extension altogether from the test code, assuming the extension is one of those Cypress automatically look for.

title: cy.contains shouldn't use content from script/style tags in the body
body:
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/56234e52d6d1cbd292acdfd5f5d547f0c4706b51/packages/driver/src/dom/elements.ts#L1066

Since `elem.textContent` will include strings that are inside non-visible nodes like `<script>` and `<style>` tags, `cy.contains` can result in false-positives and false negatives. I discovered this while writing tests for a SSR app (using Next.js).

```
[Click Delete button]
cy.contains(deletedText).should("not.exist");
```

In this case, the test failed because the value of `deletedText` was found in `body.textContent` since that value was present in a `<script>` tag that was part of the original HTML.

```
cy.contains("Button that doesn't exist").click();
```

In this case, an element may get clicked if it contains a script tag that contains the text `Button that doesn't exist`. This happens pretty easily with our SSR app, where the react component names end up in a script tag, regardless of whether they are visible or not. So the test will pass on that line and proceed after clicking the `body`.

Is it possible to add an option to allow only visible contents to be matched (and internally use `innerText`)?
E.g. `cy.contains("Visible text", {visibleOnly: true});`

title: fix: XHR event listener AUT redirect bug
body:
- Fixes #3975
- Fixes #7439

May also address #15490, #9261, #7871

### User facing changelog

Fix for incorrect redirect when `location.href` is set to a relative path within the call stack of an XHR event handler, which incorrectly sets the user's AUT to `/__/` rather than the correct path. 

~Additionally, adds code to detect when a form submit target is set to `_top` and sets to `''` to avoid redirecting the parent frame.~ Edit: Split out to #16394

### Additional details

This was caused by the changes in this Chromium commit: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=849236 (big thanks to @jennifer-shehane doing the initial range narrowing on that one) which changed the mechanics of how the window is bound around events, which I believe had an inadvertent side affect that affects `location.href` assignment. 

This ticket: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1195471 seems like it will possibly address the issue, but this behavior is consistent in both Firefox & Chrome, so it's likely worth fixing on our end for now. 

By wrapping the handlers in a function defined in the AUT window (@brian-mann had the idea for that one), the event handler is correctly associated with the AUT, and it doesn't impact the `location.href` assignment.

### How has the user experience changed?

User's AUT is no-longer redirected incorrectly to `/__/path` but instead to the correct relative window location path.

title: fix: Prevent null snapshots from being stored and causing errors
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes #15816

### User facing changelog

- Fixed an issue where hovering over a command log without a snapshot would cause the error `Cannot read property 'name' of null`

### Additional details

Snapshotting can fail for various reasons. In the issue this closes, it was because the snapshot happens before the page fully loads, but it can also fail if the page is cross-origin. We [catch such failures when creating the snapshot and return `null`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/e9457e2d09546cb6a5e78413367fcb32a5f056b3/packages/driver/src/cy/snapshots.js#L219-L221), but the log [adds that `null` value to the list of snapshots](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/e9457e2d09546cb6a5e78413367fcb32a5f056b3/packages/driver/src/cypress/log.js#L331-L334). When the user hovers over the command and we try to display the snapshot, it's expected to be a proper snapshot object and throws when we try to access properties on it. The solution is simply to not add `null` snapshots to the list of the log's snapshots. Then it's properly recognized as "missing" (which is correct, since we can't get a snapshot of it) and we display that to the user without erroring.

### How has the user experience changed?

Hovering over commands with a missing snapshot no longer errors.

title: Test-level config env replaces (rather than merges with) suite-level config env
body:
### Current behavior
When a suite is provided a `config` argument with an `env` property, and a contained test is also provided a `config` argument with an `env` property, the test's `env` **entirely replaces** the suite's `env`.

### Desired behavior
Properties of the test's `config` `env` should **override/merge** into the suite's `config` `env`, similarly to how the rest of the config/env overrides work.

### Test code to reproduce
```js
describe('Suite with a config env',
  { env: {
      var0: 'I was set on the suite!',
      var1: 'I was set on the suite!'
  }},
  () => {
    it('Test with a config env',
      { env: { var1: 'I was set on the test!' } },
      () => {
        expect(Cypress.env('var0')).to.exist.and.to.equal('I was set on the suite!') // AssertionError: expected undefined to exist
        expect(Cypress.env('var1')).to.exist.and.to.equal('I was set on the test!')
    })
})
```

### Versions
Cypress 7.1.0

title: cy.wait() does not see call when initial intercept registration is overwritten with intercept with mocked data
body:
We are trying to migrate our cy.route functionality to cy.intercept.

And while doing so we came across an issue with cy.wait. 

When we register an intercept without mocked data, and then overwrite that registration with an identical intercept, only with mocked data the cy.wait no longer sees the call.
This will cause the wait to fail on timeout.

The same functionality does work with cy.route.

### Current behavior
We see that cypress correctly intercepts the call, and gives back the mocked data. 
cy.wait does not see the call and fails after timing out. 
![afbeelding](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35066969/115535017-a8768380-a298-11eb-9905-5e713fd8b941.png)

cy.wait sees the mocked call and correctly awaits it.

7.1

title: chore: Improve CI build time by caching node_modules
body: Improves the CI time by caching `node_modules` in a way that they can be re-used between CI runs if any items that would influence the `node_modules` have not changed (`yarn.lock`, `{dev,peer}dependencies`, `*.patch` files). Before (on every run): ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/154748/115579122-dd340c00-a293-11eb-84ce-54058647e91f.png) After (on runs where with no module changes): ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/154748/115578982-bd9ce380-a293-11eb-9835-ac01eddd6f1b.png) Because the workspace persisted across layers is smaller, it also means that the restore phase will be quicker for e2e tests. ### How has the user experience changed? - Tests run faster in CI Part 2 to this might involve splitting into two workspaces, one for `/npm` and one for root, to allow us to cache `node_modules` independently, but that will likely require other changes to the workflow, so I didn't attempt that for now.

title: Unexpected error when stubbing a request with `cy.intercept(string, { headers: {} })`

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior

In Cypress 7, the `cy.intercept(url, routeMatcher)` overload was added. Now, when doing the following:

```
cy.intercept('/url', { headers: { foo: 'bar' }, body: '' })
```

or a variation, you get the following error:

> When invoking cy.intercept() with a RouteMatcher as the second parameter, a handler (function or StaticResponse) must be specified as the third parameter. If you intended to stub out a response body by passing an object as the 2nd parameter, pass an object with a body property containing the desired response body instead.

Obviously this is not quite the case, since the object DOES have a `body` property.

### Desired behavior

2nd argument is treated as StaticResponse in this case

This check: `      if (_.isString(matcher) && hasRouteMatcherKeys(handler)) {` should probably do `hasONLYRouteMatcherKeys(handler)` to avoid this problem.

title: Address performance issues with video recording in Chrome 89+/Electron 12+
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior

We cannot upgrade to Electron 12 because of a major slowdown when video recording is enabled. We are stuck on 12.0.0-beta.14, the last version before the issue appeared.

The issue appears to be related to the Chrome 89 upgrade that occurred in 12.0.0-beta.16. Similar slowdowns occur when video recording in Cypress with Chrome 89, regardless of Electron version.

With some changes released after Chromium 89.0.4328.0 and before/at 89.0.4336.0, capturing screencasts via CDP is now causing performance issues. It seems like our CDP client is receiving many, many more frames before, to the point where the user's CPU is saturated with transmitting/encoding video frames, especially when users run in resource-constrained machines in CI.

The issue can be reproduced by changing the  Chrome version as well, independently of Electron's CDP.

### Desired behavior

Slowdown is isolated and fixed so that we can continue to ship the latest Electron version.

Relevant:

* https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/15853 - slowdown issue
* https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/16113 - downgrade PR

body:
### Current behavior
I have a simple test that logs into our atlassian jira cloud server and upon successful login attempts to navigate to another page on the same server. The login process is successful but the second cy.visit() call fails with a CORS like error.

Here's the extent of the test:
```js
describe('Authentication', () => { 
    it('logs in and out', () => {
      cy.visit('/login.jsp');
      cy.get('#username').type(Cypress.env('UILOGIN_USER'));
      cy.get('#login-submit').click();
      cy.get('#password').type(Cypress.env('UILOGIN_TOKEN'));
      cy.get('#login-submit').click();
      cy.get('#createGlobalItemIconButton');  // visible on successful login

      cy.visit('/logout.jsp');
      cy.get('#logout-submit').click();
      cy.get('#form-login');  // should return to login page
    });  
  })
```
The test fails on the 2nd cy.visit (to /logout.jsp) with the following message:

```
cy.visit() failed because you are attempting to visit a URL that is of a different origin.

The new URL is considered a different origin because the following parts of the URL are different:

  > superdomain

You may only cy.visit() same-origin URLs within a single test.

The previous URL you visited was:

  > 'https://id.atlassian.com'

You're attempting to visit this URL:

  > 'https://jmwe-test-react.atlassian.net'

You may need to restructure some of your test code to avoid this problem.
```

Some things to note:

- I've configured the baseUrl to point to my site: 'https://jmwe-test-react.atlassian.net'
- The two cy.visit() calls I make are to paths under the same baseUrl
- The initial visit(/login.jsp) triggers a redirect to 'https://id.atlassian.com' where the script then finds the screen elements and submits the login request. Upon successful login, the browser is redirected back to a page on my baseUrl and the subsequent get successfully finds an element on that page.

title: Create separate log source for commit and build information
body:
When running Cypress you can enable debug logs from different sources https://on.cypress.io/troubleshooting#Log-sources

A common question that comes up a lot is the Dashboard missing CI or Git commit information. This information is collected in https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/packages/server/lib/modes/record.js with most of the info coming from https://github.com/cypress-io/commit-info and some from https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/packages/server/lib/util/ci_provider.js

The record and the ci_provider do not have a good way to show _just_ the commit and CI information. You show the collected info via the `DEBUG=cypress:server:record` setting, but that would expose a LOT of API calls with potentially sensitive information.

I think we can create limited log source in record.js to just log the CI and Git commit info in these lines

https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/29b803f54b9a8b5c3b336d3e696d4795276a763e/packages/server/lib/modes/record.js#L307-L327

Then the users can safely see what we have collected without exposing the sensitive data or without being overwhelmed by all API calls

title: feat(webpack-dev-server): support custom index-template for webpack dev server
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes #16243

### User facing changelog
<!-- Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog-->

Support passing a custom `index-template.html` to the Webpack Dev Server `startDevServer` function.

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

Some frameworks like Next.js expect certain HTML tags to exist in the document, [as explained here](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/16243#issuecomment-828121505). Specifically an element with the id `__next_css__DO_NOT_USE__` should exist when the component is imported. This PR also updates the Next.js plugin to provide a modified `index.html` with the required tag.

This has a secondary use of letting users include things like CDN links in their default template, like Storybook's `preview-head.html`. They'll also need to include `<div id="__cy_root">`, and asking them to do so is not really ideal, so I'm not really advertising this feature at the moment, other than a small note in the Webpack Dev Server README. Long term, I think we should take a custom `index.html` and inject `__cy_root` programatically, so the user does not need to think about this sort of thing when providing a custom template.

title: chore: optimize resource_class usage
body:
Closes #16252

Based on the data collected here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nkpeZ2dGAq-Es1fKCALiMgWSHCzl6I1PU7y5adSlHes/edit#gid=0

* The default `resource_class` was set to `small` (from `medium`) for all Linux jobs.
* Jobs that increased in runtime by 20 seconds or more when running with `small` (or that OOMed) were bumped to `medium`.
* All bottleneck jobs (`node-modules-install`, `build`, `create-build-artifacts`, `npm-release`) were bumped to `medium+`.
* In the end, 24/54 non-bottleneck jobs were able to run without degradation on `small` (44.444%)
* See spreadsheet column Q+R for job-by-job diff of the changes in this PR

- Closes #15898
- Closes #16223

### User facing changelog

- Cypress no longer crashes with an error when testing a binary file upload

### Additional details

We recursively merge request properties after running the request through middleware, but in the case of a binary request body, which is a buffer, lodash identifies it as an array and the merging turns it into an array of numbers. That causes the error when it hits `request`, because it loops through the array and tries to write numbers into the request, which are invalid. It needs to remain a buffer for `request` to properly write it.

This fixes it by not trying to recursively merge binary buffers but overwriting them entirely after middleware runs.

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior

webpack-dev-server introduced breaking changes to their configuration object in their beta version. Cypress component tests fail when running with  "webpack-dev-server": "^4.0.0-beta.2",

I know that this is beta, but my team is using this to be able to serve our web app via `encore` for development. We need to have this installed at ^4 as a dev dependency

The following error is thrown:

```
 WARNING  The value passed to setManifestKeyPrefix "/dist" starts with "/". This is allowed, but since the key prefix does not normally start with a "/", you may have just changed the prefix accidentally.
Invalid configuration object. Object has been initialized using a configuration object that does not match the API schema.
 - configuration has an unknown property 'noInfo'. These properties are valid:
   object { bonjour?, client?, compress?, dev?, firewall?, headers?, historyApiFallback?, host?, hot?, http2?, https?, liveReload?, onAfterSetupMiddleware?, onBeforeSetupMiddleware?, onListening?, open?, port?, proxy?, public?, setupExitSignals?, static?, transportMode?, watchFiles? }
ValidationError: Invalid configuration object. Object has been initialized using a configuration object that does not match the API schema.
 - configuration has an unknown property 'noInfo'. These properties are valid:
   object { bonjour?, client?, compress?, dev?, firewall?, headers?, historyApiFallback?, host?, hot?, http2?, https?, liveReload?, onAfterSetupMiddleware?, onBeforeSetupMiddleware?, onListening?, open?, port?, proxy?, public?, setupExitSignals?, static?, transportMode?, watchFiles? }
    at validate (/Users/morgan/Documents/WineSpectator/git/ws/node_modules/webpack-dev-server/node_modules/schema-utils/dist/validate.js:104:11)
    at new Server (/Users/morgan/Documents/WineSpectator/git/ws/node_modules/webpack-dev-server/lib/Server.js:43:5)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/Users/morgan/Documents/WineSpectator/git/ws/node_modules/@cypress/webpack-dev-server/dist/startServer.js:57:16)
    at Generator.next (<anonymous>)
    at fulfilled (/Users/morgan/Documents/WineSpectator/git/ws/node_modules/@cypress/webpack-dev-server/dist/startServer.js:5:58)

Looks like this stems from line 55 in startserver.js

```js
const webpackDevServerConfig = Object.assign(Object.assign({}, userWebpackConfig.devServer), { hot: false, inline: false, publicPath: devServerPublicPathRoute, noInfo: false });
        // @ts-ignore types for webpack v5 are incorrect?
        return new webpack_dev_server_1.default(compiler, webpackDevServerConfig);
```

This is passing config options that are no longer supported/have moved

### Desired behavior

We'd love to be able to run cypress component tests alongside webpack-dev-server ^4 

I'm frustrated that the symfony team is requiring a beta version for their dev server to work with encore, and understand that it may be a stretch to support a beta version of webpack-dev-server, but this may be indicative of impending breaking changes at some point anyways.

`npx cypress run-ct`

body:
### What would you like?

I have too many tests to run them all before pushing. I typically want to run a bunch of tests, either in a folder, or close to each other alphabetically within a folder, after making a change. 

Imagine I updated the User Profile page. Maybe I want to run all the /User Profile tests, but I don't want to waste my time running other tests locally. I'll let CI handle it. Or maybe I worked on User Profile/Settings, and I just want to run a few Profile/Settings related tests. 

I would like to either: 
- Run all tests in a specified folder
- Highlight/run a bunch of selected tests
- Be able to queue up additional tests after the one I'm running (like a music app)

### Why is this needed?

Makes it easier to run a selected set of tests, before doing a push and relying on CI to run them. 



This is not super urgent. It's a nice-to-have. But I will be more likely to run the correct tests locally, before pushing and discovering that I missed something.

title: Cypress GUI window can open at non-existent coordinates.
body:
### Current behavior
When starting cypress from the command line, no check is performed to make sure that the coordinates the window is opening at actually exist. As a result, the window will be unreachable.

This issue happens if the window is closed while on a second monitor. X and Y coordinates are saved to state, and the next time cypress is started, it will start at those coordinates. If the second monitor is removed after state is saved, but before cypress is started again, cypress will start the window at the coordinates in state, even though they don't exist anymore.

This can be fixed by either manually finding and editing the state object, plugging the second monitor back in and moving the window, or re-installing cypress.

### Desired behavior
The window opens somewhere that can be reached.

### Versions

**Cypress version:** 7.2.0
**OS:** Windows 10 Pro v.2004

There is no way to make intercept work with URL that has brackets in them (for example `[i]`). It will work if those brackets are encoded in the actual URL and in the intercepted URL. But it is not an option to encode the actual URL.

### Desired behavior
```js
cy.intercept("https://test.something.com/api/v1/users?sort=email[i]", "something")
```
or at least with "*" 
```js
cy.intercept("https://test.something.com/api/v1/users?sort=email[i]*", "something")
```
to intercept request "https://test.something.com/api/v1/users?sort=email[i]"

For my case, the best fix would be to intercept if the request URL equals intercept URL exactly.
Currently, you can't even intercept plain exact URL
```js
cy.intercept("https://test.something.com/api/v1/users", "something")
```
and make a request to https://test.something.com/api/v1/users.
you have to append "*" to intercept URL

### Test code to reproduce

https://github.com/MayGo/cypress-test-tiny

### Versions

Cypress version 7.2.0

### Current behavior
In my usecase I use the cypress.json config, and extends it in separate cypress-e2e.json and cypress-smoke.json to have different baseUrls for different environments. But sometimes however I want to run tests on another environment, i.e. on another baseUrl. ### Desired behavior
The environment variables matching configuration properties should always overwrite properties from the config file(s).

### Test code to reproduce
CYPRESS_BASE_URL="https://example.environment3.com" cypress run --config-file smoketest-cypress.json

cypress.json:
```json
"baseUrl": "https://example.environment1.com",
...other properties

smoketest-cypress.json:
```json
"extends": "./cypress.json",

* `(req stub)`, for staticresponse stubs (same as cy.route's `(xhr stub)`)

title: feat(intercept): support regexp matcher with middleware intercepts
body:
### User facing changelog

`cy.intercept` accepts a RegExp matcher for `url` now when route matcher options are passed to it as the second argument.

### Additional details

When upgrading to Cypress 7 I had to figure out how to add a delay to one of our requests. In Cypress 6 we were just adding such intercept before other intercepts but now they are matched in the reverse order.

So we had a code like this:
```js
cy.intercept(/localization/, () => delay(500))
cy.customVisitWithSetOfCommonInterceptsInIt('')
```
but since this request was done immediately on startup of our application we couldn't just reorder those commands - because `cy.visit` only resolves after the `load` event.

So I've figured out that `{ middleware: true }` can actually save me here and to my surprise this both didn't work and didn't typecheck correctly:
```diff
-cy.intercept(/localization/, () => delay(500))
+cy.intercept(/localization/, { middleware: true }, () => delay(500))
```

The work around this is quite simple:
```diff
-cy.intercept(/localization/, { middleware: true }, () => delay(500))
+cy.intercept('**localization**', { middleware: true }, () => delay(500))
```
But I think that the DX could be improved here by just allowing a regexp matcher, unless there is a strong reason why this is not supported.

### How has the user experience changed?

It has been improved since now `cy.intercept` will accept more combination of arguments.

title: Inspecting boolean JSON responses crashes Cypress with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
<!-- A description including screenshots, stack traces, DEBUG logs, etc. 👉 https://on.cypress.io/troubleshooting -->
Attempting to inspect an HTTP response that is a simple `true`/`false` JSON value results in a crash.

```
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE] [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "chunk" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or Uint8Array. Received type boolean (true)
    at PassThrough.Writable.write (_stream_writable.js:285:13)
    at sendBody (/Users/bcheng/Library/Caches/Cypress/7.2.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/net-stubbing/lib/server/util.js:157:22)
    at Object.getBodyStream (/Users/bcheng/Library/Caches/Cypress/7.2.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/net-stubbing/lib/server/util.js:161:43)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/Users/bcheng/Library/Caches/Cypress/7.2.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/net-stubbing/lib/server/middleware/response.js:79:35)
    at Generator.next (<anonymous>:null:null)
    at fulfilled (/Users/bcheng/Library/Caches/Cypress/7.2.0/Cypress.app/Contents/Resources/app/packages/net-stubbing/lib/server/middleware/response.js:5:58)
    at runMicrotasks (<anonymous>:null:null)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:93:5)
```

The response in question was:
```js
{
  headers: {
    server: 'nginx',
    'content-type': 'application/json',
    'content-length': '4',
    connection: 'keep-alive',
    // Some additional fields redacted
  },
  url: 'REDACTED',
  method: null,
  httpVersion: '1.1',
  statusCode: 200,
  statusMessage: 'OK',
  body: "true"
}
```

### Desired behavior

Cypress 7.2.0 can inspect JSON responses that are plain `true` or `false` values.

### Test code to reproduce

```ts
cy.intercept("GET", "*", (req) => {
  req.on("response", (res) => {})
});
```

### Versions

<!-- Cypress version, last known working Cypress version (if applicable), Browser and version, Operating System, CI Provider, etc -->
<!-- If possible, please update Cypress to latest version and check if the bug is still present. -->
- 7.2.0

---

I added a few lines right before calling `getBodyStream` and the test works as expected afterward.

https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/1baa5ff454112cee51a7ed7adfc97dd578c4d5e7/packages/net-stubbing/lib/server/middleware/response.ts#L81

```diff
diff --git a/packages/net-stubbing/lib/server/middleware/response.ts b/packages/net-stubbing/lib/server/middleware/response.ts
index cae4b455fa..902cb2d81b 100644
--- a/packages/net-stubbing/lib/server/middleware/response.ts
+++ b/packages/net-stubbing/lib/server/middleware/response.ts
@@ -78,6 +78,10 @@ export const InterceptResponse: ResponseMiddleware = async function () {
 
   mergeChanges(request.res as any, modifiedRes)
 
+  if (_.isObject(modifiedRes.body)) {
+    modifiedRes.body = JSON.stringify(modifiedRes.body)
+  }
+
   const bodyStream = getBodyStream(modifiedRes.body, _.pick(modifiedRes, ['throttleKbps', 'delay']) as any)
 
   return request.continueResponse!(bodyStream)
```

Although I see the `if (_isObject()) { body = JSON.stringify(body) }` pattern in a few other places in Cypress, I suspect there's a deeper root cause. The diff here is just a hack to help show where the problem might be.

Thanks!

body:
Edited by @jennifer-shehane 

Removes `underscore` and `backbone` as dev dependencies from the project.

### Additional Details

This started out as a renovate PR to fix an underscore vulnerability, but then I saw:

- The `server` doesn't even use the `underscore` devDep that we're installing?
- The `driver` only uses the `underscore` devDep for a single driver test that requires Backbone. I rewrote the test so it doesn't require Backbone (and `underscore` as it's peer dep). So, this also removes `backbone` as a devDep from the driver. I assume this test has parity, but also this is such an old test who even knows if the code to fix it still exists in the driver.

title: fix: cy.intercept adds access-control-expose-headers for cors requests
body:
- Closes #15050

### User facing changelog

`cy.intercept()` adds `access-control-expose-headers` header for CORS requests. 

### Additional details
- Why was this change necessary? => This causes some unnecessary confusion for some use cases. 
- What is affected by this change? => N/A
- Any implementation details to explain? => When there is a custom header, we add `access-control-expose-headers` automatically to avoid confusion.

### How has the user experience changed?

**Before:** If it's a CORS request, you need to remember to add `access-control-expose-headers` to get header information from `cy.intercept()`.

```js
cy
.intercept('/cors*', {
  body: { success: true },
  headers: {
    'access-control-expose-headers': 'x-token', // This line is required
    'x-token': 'token',
  },
})
```

**After:** Cypress automatically handles it.

```js
cy
.intercept('/cors*', {
  body: { success: true },
  headers: {
    // It isn't necessary.
    'x-token': 'token',
  },
})
```

### PR Tasks
<!-- These tasks must be completed before a PR is merged.
Delete tasks if they are not applicable. -->

- [x] Have tests been added/updated?

title: xhr.send(formData) doesn't work when upgraded  to cypress 7.2.0 ,
Component testing does not honour configuration values provided by plugins.
body:
### Current behavior

In Cypress `^6.8.0` it was possible to configure component testing using a plugin file by modifying the received configuration. Since the release of 7 this is no longer possible and requires you to configure component testing
in the `cypress.json` file instead. 

### Desired behavior

It should honour the plugin overrides.

### Test code to reproduce

The Cypress.json that is now required, (this was empty on 6.8.0)

```json
{
  "component": {
    "componentFolder": ".",
    "fixturesFolder": false,
    "ignoreTestFiles": "**/node_modules/**",
    "testFiles": "**/*.cypress.js"
  }
}
```

The previous configuration merged in a plugin file:

```js
module.exports = function (on, base) {
    const config = require('deepmerge')(base, {
        testFiles: '**/*.cypress.js',
        integrationFolder: 'cypress',
        ignoreTestFiles: '**/node_modules/**',
        experimentalComponentTesting: true,
    });

    return config;
}
```

Packages:
-`cypress`: ^7.2.0
-`@cypress/react`: ^5.4.2
-`@cypress/webpack-dev-server`: ^1.1.6

Environment: 
-Node.js: v12.9.0
-NPM: 6.10.2

    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:988:32)
```
After some investigation, I found 2 things:
- `listr@0.14.3` -> `@samverschueren/stream-to-observable@0.3.0` -> `any-observable@0.3.0`
- `listr@0.14.3` -> `is-observable@1.1.0` -> `symbol-observable@1.1.0`

1st one is causing the main issue
2nd one is known to be a breaking change https://github.com/ReactiveX/rxjs/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#breaking-changes-4

Since `listr` doesn't seem to be maintained anymore (last release 2 years ago), I found [listr2](https://github.com/cenk1cenk2/listr2) which has a [PR in progress for rxjs@7](https://github.com/cenk1cenk2/listr2/pull/381).

title: `cy.intercept` StaticResponse headers cannot contain multiple `Set-Cookie` header values
body:
Hi, I've got a scenario where I'm stubbing an endpoint that sets multiple cookies on success via multiple set-cookie headers using the intercept API.

With a static response object, when you define the headers option it only enables you to define a single header/ set-cookie entry with the typings strictly only allowing strings, so if you have, for example:

```js
headers: {
     set-cookie: ['cookie1=1', 'cookie2=2']
}
```
Cypress throws and exception, but there's no alternative that I've seen to define the set-cookie header, with multiple entries with a static response. I've tried alternatives like hooking into the req/ res using the handler functions but this isn't fulfilling the upfront stub requirement as it appears to still allow the request through to the destination URL before modifying the response headers with our extra set-cookie header values.

### Current behavior
A single set cookie header will be set, or cypress fails to build and logs and error for the interception stating that StaticResponse can only be used with string values for headers.

### Desired behavior
You can define multiple Set-Cookie header values for a StaticResponse object

### Versions
The equivalent behaviour worked in 5.6.0  upgrading to 7+ and intercept we have observed the above.

-->

- Closes #16451

### User facing changelog

- Fixed an issue where `cy.wait()` could yield the incorrect result when used with `cy.intercept()` and several simultaneous requests.

### Additional details

- `cy.wait('@intercept')` was originally supposed to "latch" - it must wait for the request, then wait for the response. 
- it may seem unnecessary now, but the design for this emerged for the requirement for `cy.wait('@alias.request/response')`, which was scrapped
- regardless, #14885 broke the latching by allowing a request already in the `Complete` state to set requestWaited and responseWaited in one fell swoop
- this meant that in a race condition, the request yielded might not match the one which was marked as `requestWaited: true` when the request phase was waited
- reverted the `requestWaited = true` change and all tests still pass so it's good

title: Optimize potential video performance issues
body:
### Current behavior

There have been reports of performance issues when recording video, reportedly getting worse since 7.0 when running Cypress in a headless browser, the default screen size was increased from 1280x720 to 1920x1080. 

[Instructions to change screen size here.](https://on.cypress.io/browser-launch-api#Set-screen-size-when-running-headless) 

### User feedback

- Cypress dashboard video playback is not smooth: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/16153
- 7.2.0, Chrome, 1920x964 - "it seems that videos in Electron and Chrome browsers have different video quality. I find that the test video recording on Electron is much smoother that if the browser is set to Chrome."

### Todo

- [x] Investigate current video performance across environments, browsers, and Cypress versions to determine where the degradation exists.

### Theories as to degraded performance

>the root cause of the issue is simply that chrome is not opened in the correct xvfb size which was all that was ever needed to fix the blurry videos and screenshots and why changing the xvfb window size only created higher CPU pressure and never fixed the root cause
>And it’s also why we never experienced this with electron videos or screenshots
>The issue should be isolated to chrome in Linux with xvfb

### Versions

7.0+

title: Running cypress in headless mode should not use xvfb
body:

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

Currently, when I use cypress in headless mode via `cypress run`, xvfb is still invoked. Consequently, sometimes this can make my cypress tests error out due to an error.

When running in headless mode, there is no need to spawn xvfb at all. This should only be done when using `cypress run` to run a browser in headed mode.

All versions of cypress up to 7.3.0

N/A - for internal testing purposes

### Additional details

Adds a GitHub action to periodically check for a new version of each channel of Chrome (stable and beta) and issue a PR with the version bumped. 

This uses [OmahaProxy](https://omahaproxy.appspot.com/) to get the latest versions. Apparently it's what the Chrome team uses.

It's set up to run at 8am (UTC), which is 3am EST/4am EDT. If it detects a new version or new versions, it creates a branch named after the currently stored versions of Chrome stable and beta and creates a PR. 

If that PR isn't merged and there's a newer version or versions on a subsequent night, it will update the same branch and PR with a new commit.

<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
<!-- A description including screenshots, stack traces, DEBUG logs, etc. 👉 https://on.cypress.io/troubleshooting -->

When using Component Testing + Webpack 5, build errors produce a blank screen in the Cypress runner and the following error in the browser console:
```
TypeError: input.join is not a function
    at Filter.toHtml (cypress_runner.js:17794)
    at cypress_runner.js:193178

convert.toHtml(error.error?.message ?? error.error)

It should not crash 😅.

title: @cypress/react/plugins/babel doesn't work in a monorepo
body:
### Current behavior

If you import @cypress/react/plugins/babel in your cypress code in a package in a monorepo, and run`yarn cypress open-ct`, it doesn't resolve the babel config from the monorepo route and throws an error:

```
ERROR in ./src/index.test.js
Module build failed (from ./node_modules/babel-loader/lib/index.js):
SyntaxError: ./packages/example-application/src/index.test.js: Support for the experimental syntax 'jsx' isn't currently enabled (6:9):
```

This is due to babel not searching upwards for the babel config by default.


### Desired behavior

Babel should be configurable to search upwards in a monorepo to find the babel config.

As explained here:

https://babeljs.io/docs/en/config-files#monorepos

```
        loader: 'babel-loader',
        options: {
          rootMode: "upward",
        },
```

`rootMode: "upward"` needs to be optionally specified in getBabelWebpackConfig.

I will open a PR to allow this to be sent via a config option.

### Test code to reproduce

https://github.com/govuk-react/govuk-react/tree/c7aea92bec8d5d6b0c65a6cb821ddf60cfb11233

### Versions

    "@cypress/react": "^5.7.0",
    "@cypress/webpack-dev-server": "^1.3.0",
    "cypress": "^7.3.0",

title: Allow logging output of cy.exec commands which fail due to timeout
body: ### What would you like? An option to log the `stdout`/`stderr` of a command run by `cy.exec` which failed because it exceeded the Cypress timeout. ### Why is this needed? We have a seeding command in our project which times out occasionally in our CI runs, never locally. It is difficult to debug this because we have no access to the output of the command. It is not logged and can't be inspected via Cypress Dashboard, which only offers screenshots and videos. ### Previous attempts to make this work I've tried this, without success: ```javascript cy.exec(command, { failOnNonZeroExit: false }) .then((result) => { if (result.code !== 0) { cy.log(result.stderr); cy.log(result.stdout); } }) .then((result) => { if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error('Seeding failed.'); }); ``` Cypress dashboard delivers the following screenshot, because `then` never gets called: There is already a `log` option, but this only logs the text of the command itself.

title: Cypress support for iFrame [Logs preview & Debugging]
body:
### What would you like?
As a end user, I want Cypress to handle iFrame, as it handles for sections outside iFrame (Specifically logs).

**Description:**

1. In general when we run our test cases using test runner we see the logs on left and its preview on right window.
2. After execution is complete. We can hover over the logs and see the execution preview one by one.
3. There is also a feature, If I pin a particular step in the log, I can debug using console (As it shows request and response for that particular step).

Now take any application that is entirely under an iFrame. And try to use the default Cypress feature of hovering over logs. You won't be able to see the preview. Debugging is also difficult.

<!-- A clear description of the feature or enhancement wanted in Cypress -->
Cypress by default supports iFrame to its full capacity.
No need for plugins to handle iFrames.
Cypress supports iFrames for logs preview & debugging (Just as it does for a web app without iFrame).

### Why is this needed?
All modern webapps are using iFrames extensively. At some point you will have to bring it to support your existing features.

title: Enable Video only on Retry
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to request a feature. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### What would you like?
Currently, we can disable video processing/compression to only occur on test failures.  Instead, or in addition, I propose a new configuration that would enable video recording only on retry of test.
```
"video": false
 "retries": {
    "runMode": 2,
    "openMode": 0,
    "video": true
  }
```
In the above configuration, all passing tests will not record a video, but if test is a valid failure, it would record the video on both re-tries. Additionally, if the first retry passes, there would still be a video recorded.

### Why is this needed?
Disabling video dramatically improves the performance of test runs. However, the video is extremely useful when trying to determine the cause of a failure. If a test fails and retries are configured it would be very nice if that is the only time a video is even recorded.

title: Chrome flag settings ignored when using Command-Line Test Runner
body:
### Current behavior
When the "**SameSite by default cookies**" flag is set within a Chrome browser instance opened from the _interactive test runner_ it will continue to persist for the _interactive runner_. However, when using the _command-line runner_ this flag reverts back to the "**default**" setting. 

This behavior breaks any tests in the _command-line runner_ that rely upon "**SameSite by default cookies**" being "**Disabled**" since there is currently no way to disable it for such a run. Attempting to disable it within a browser instance of the _command-line runner_ does not persist. After Chrome 90 the "**Default**" for "**SameSite by default cookies**" is "**Enabled**".

### Desired behavior
Any Chrome flag (chrome://flags) set within a Chrome browser instance opened from the _interactive test runner_ should continue to persist when using the _command-line runner_.

### Test code to reproduce
##### cypress interactive runner
1. open the interactive test runner: `yarn run cypress open`
2. select `Chrome 90` as the browser
2. run a spec file
3. disable the chrome "SameSite by default cookies" flag by doing the following:
    1. open a new tab
    2. enter `chrome://flags/#same-site-by-default-cookies` into the url
    3. set `SameSite by default cookies` to `Disabled`
4. follow steps 1 through 4 and observe the flag persists
##### cypress command-line runner
1. run the spec through the command-line test runner with the `--no-exit` option: 
    1. `yarn run cypress run --spec "[spec file]" --browser chrome --no-exit`
2. check whether the chrome "SameSite by default cookies" flag setting persists by doing the following:
    1. open a new tab
    2. enter `chrome://flags/#same-site-by-default-cookies` into the url
    3. observe `SameSite by default cookies` is `Default` rather than `Enabled`
3. repeat steps 1 and 2, and then disable the flag
4. repeat steps 1 and 2 again, observe that the flag reverts back to `Default`

### Versions
* Cypress 7.4.0
* Chrome 90.0.4430.212
* MacOS Mojave 10.14.6

title: cy.intercept doesn't handle binary data correctly
body:
<!-- 👋 Use the template below to report a bug. Fill in as much info as possible. 

Have a question? Start a new discussion 👉 https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/discussions

As an open source project with a small maintainer team, it may take some time for your issue to be addressed. Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### Current behavior
1. When intercepting a request that returns binary data (for example `application/octet-stream`) the response is corrupted by `cy.intercept`.
2. When trying to stub a request with an `ArrayBuffer` it is interpreted as JSON.

### Desired behavior
1. Intercepting a request does not alter the response if it is not stubbed.
2. It is possible to supply an `ArrayBuffer` to an intercept stub.

### Test code to reproduce
Reproduction code is here: https://github.com/simfeld/cypress-intercept-binary. There are three tests:

1. no intercept: This test succeeds, the response is loaded correctly from the server.
2. intercept without stub: This test fails. The request is intercepted but not stubbed. The response that arrives in the browser is `{}` or `[123, 125]` when interpreted as `ArrayBuffer`, instead of the response that the server delivers.
3. intercept with stub: This test fails. The request is intercepted and a stub is returned. The response that arrives in the browser is `{}` or `[123, 125]` when interpreted as `ArrayBuffer`, instead of the stub supplied to the intercept.

### Versions

Latest version as of filing this issue (`7.4.0`)

### Related issues

This issue is possibly related: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/15038

| [ws](https://togithub.com/websockets/ws) | [`5.2.2` -> `5.2.3`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/ws/5.2.2/5.2.3) | [![age](https://badges.renovateapi.com/packages/npm/ws/5.2.3/age-slim)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![adoption](https://badges.renovateapi.com/packages/npm/ws/5.2.3/adoption-slim)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![passing](https://badges.renovateapi.com/packages/npm/ws/5.2.3/compatibility-slim/5.2.2)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![confidence](https://badges.renovateapi.com/packages/npm/ws/5.2.3/confidence-slim/5.2.2)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2021-32640](https://togithub.com/websockets/ws/security/advisories/GHSA-6fc8-4gx4-v693)

### Impact

A specially crafted value of the `Sec-Websocket-Protocol` header can be used to significantly slow down a ws server.

### Proof of concept

```js
for (const length of [1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000]) {
  const value = 'b' + ' '.repeat(length) + 'x';
  const start = process.hrtime.bigint();

  value.trim().split(/ *, */);

  const end = process.hrtime.bigint();

  console.log('length = %d, time = %f ns', length, end - start);
}
```

### Patches

The vulnerability was fixed in ws@7.4.6 (https://github.com/websockets/ws/commit/00c425ec77993773d823f018f64a5c44e17023ff) and backported to ws@6.2.2 (https://github.com/websockets/ws/commit/78c676d2a1acefbc05292e9f7ea0a9457704bf1b) and ws@5.2.3 (https://github.com/websockets/ws/commit/76d47c1479002022a3e4357b3c9f0e23a68d4cd2).

### Workarounds

In vulnerable versions of ws, the issue can be mitigated by reducing the maximum allowed length of the request headers using the [`--max-http-header-size=size`](https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#cli_max_http_header_size_size) and/or the [`maxHeaderSize`](https://nodejs.org/api/http.html#http_http_createserver_options_requestlistener) options.

### Credits

The vulnerability was responsibly disclosed along with a fix in private by [Robert McLaughlin](https://togithub.com/robmcl4) from University of California, Santa Barbara.

Please be patient and we will respond as soon as we can. 🙏 -->

### What would you like?

This should be fairly straightforward, but the `headers` dictionary field in `CyHttpMessages.BaseMessage` within `packages/net-stubbing/lib/external-types.ts` can be expanded to include `string[]` as a valid value type (in addition to just `string`).

This improves typing in IDEs/Editors and also prevents TS2339 wherein calling `.filter` on `headers` is flagged as problematic when it is not.

title: All browsers when run via `cypress run` should run `headless` by default.
body:
### What would you like?

All browsers when run via `cypress run` should run `headless` by default.

Currently, whether a browser is run `headless` or `headed` by default is not consistent. It depends on the browser. We originally made this decision in order to not introduce a breaking change when Chrome headless was delivered. https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/5676 We intended to change this behavior in the next breaking change, but clearly didn't prioritize this work. 

- `cypress run --browser electron` - defaults to headless
- `cypress run --browser chrome` - *defaults to headed*
- `cypress run --browser firefox` - *defaults to headed*
- `cypress run --browser edge` - *defaults to headed*

### Why is this needed?

The larger reason this is necessary (besides maintaining consistency in our app) is because the browser size when Chrome is opened in headed mode is unpredictable. 

This causes a lot of unexpected video/screenshot sizes when someone wants to run their browser in chrome, not considering the (undocumented) differences between headed and headless screen sizes. 

People might additionally believe that passing browser flags for the size will fix the Chrome headed browser to a specific size when in reality it does absolutely nothing.

Chrome video sizes (browser size) during headed:

- Screensize: 2880x1800 at 2dpi = **2560x1050**
- Screensize: 1024x768 at 1dpt = **896x528**
- Xvfb size: 1280x1024 = **1050x838**
- Xvfb size: 1024x768 = **1004x582**

title: chore: correlate proxied HTTP requests with browser pre-request data
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes <!-- link to the issue here, if there is one -->

### User facing changelog

N/A - internal only.

### Additional details

- Preliminary work for #14843 and #14525
- User-facing work (driver, runner changes) for #14843 is not in this PR, only in #16730.
- Adds a connection to Firefox's implementation of the Chrome DevTools Protocol (known as the Remote Protocol), which is available when `remote.enabled` pref is set as of Firefox 86. Updated error messages to print the correct browser name, instead of hard-coded "Chrome".
	- Versions older than FF86 will still work, the Remote Protocol is considered optional at this point.
- Refactored `CdpAutomation` to be a class, since it fits nicely into an instance pattern.
- `CdpAutomation` is now created for Firefox, though the WebExtension is still used for all previous automation.
	- #16575 is a PR to swap to CDP for automating Firefox, instead of the WebExtension. There are some cookie-related failures.
- `CdpAutomation` now subscribes to `Network.requestWillBeSent` to gather metadata, including resource type (xhr, fetch, ...).
- The proxy layer can read the metadata from `Network.requestWillBeSent` and correlate it with incoming HTTP requests. Requests cannot be sent outgoing without this metadata.
	- Sometimes, it is possible for the proxy layer to receive a request before `Network.requestWillBeSent`, though it is very rare. In these cases, we wait 500ms before continuing the request, since some telemetry the browsers send will not have `Network.requestWillBeSent` events. Also, if the CPU load is high, the events can get out of order in this way. This should not impact user test cases. 
	- File downloads do not emit `requestWillBeSent` in Chrome, but do in FF.
	- There is a new debug log that will print out aggregate statistics about the pre-requests, to help debug this if it does become an issue.
- The proxy logs have been vastly, vastly improved. I removed a lot of noise and created a contextual debug wrapper so each debug log has the same info. Enable `cypress-verbose:proxy:http` and bask in the glory.

#### Todo

- [x] add tests
- [x] add debug metrics for delayed requests

### How has the user experience changed?

title: browser notification permission state
Make default screen size for headless runs to be 1280x720
body:
### What would you like?

The default screen size for headless runs in Cypress should be 1280x720.

### Why is this needed?

In an attempt to improve the resolution of screenshots and videos, we updated the resolution of videos to be 1920x1080 in Cypress 7.0: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/15686

After running many tests in different OS's, containers, screen sizes, hiDPI, etc, **we've concluded that this previous change did not improve the resolution of videos. In fact, it made the videos and screenshots less readable as the content is now tiny.**

Making the breaking change to set the size back to 1280x720 is part of a larger part of stories to improve default video and screenshot resolution. See https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/16832

#### Before 7.0 (1280x720)


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1271364/121219682-9309e880-c849-11eb-900e-54ad18ec567e.mp4



#### After 7.0 (1920x720)


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1271364/121219769-a7e67c00-c849-11eb-8ce1-35b35162337e.mp4

### Additional details
