**UNIFY-953**

The goal of this change is to wire up the focus button created in #19830. We will do this by adding a browser action that focuses to the currently opened browser. Note that firefox doesn't allow for setting focus in the browser via automation requests due to focusmanager.testmode set. Therefore we will handle firefox differently. 

For non-firefox, we will hook into the automation that is setup in the server as follows:

* Chrome (or chromium like browsers) - We will use CDP automation to call Page.bringToFront
* Electron - We will tap into the focus automation message and call win.show on the window since we already have access to that where the automation is set up

For firefox, we will use native commands to set focus to the main window in the browser process for MacOS and Windows. On linux, we will do nothing for now. We have decided to scope that combination out (firefox on linux) for the time being.

**UNIFY-922**

For this, we will hook into the dashboard login completion. If the launchpad was in focus previously, we'll set focus back there, otherwise we will call the action created in UNIFY-953.

```js
it('logs in before the main test' , () => { //ALT B Create domain and visit IDP before doing the test
```

If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->
n/a

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->
The following error thrown when accessing `cy.clock()` or `cy.tick()`:
```
TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'clock')
  at Object.clock (webpack:///../driver/src/cy/commands/clock.ts?:170:17)
```

The [`state('ctx')`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/1f70b21bc4427ff99d20d8b67d201d98d71021fe/packages/driver/src/cy/commands/clock.ts#L48) object was not set in the secondary domain which caused the error. In the primary domain the `state('ctx')` is set to the [`runnable.ctx`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/1f70b21bc4427ff99d20d8b67d201d98d71021fe/packages/driver/src/cypress/cy.ts#L845) when the runnable is set. Thus, in the secondary domain, I'm setting the `state('ctx')` to the `runnable.ctx` when the `state('runnable')` is set.

### How has the user experience changed?
<!-- Provide before and after examples of the change.
Screenshots or GIFs are preferred. -->
Users are now able to use `.clock()` and `.tick()` in multi-domain.

title: fix: correctly filter steps based on project migration requirements
body:
Follow up for [all the test cases added in here](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/19905/files) based on the Whimsical workflows. It also has some work done [here](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/19894#issuecomment-1022067401) by @elevatebart.

Resolves: https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-979

There's a bit going on here. Basically, the goal of this PR is we **only want to show the relevant steps in the migration workflow based on your project**. 

If you aren't using component testing, we won't ask you to move your component specs files. Likewise, if you have a custom `supportFile`, or `supportFile: false`, we don't migrate it for you to the new `cypress/support/e2e.js` format - we just add `supportFile` to your newly generated `cypress.config.js`. All these flows are [described in Whimsical](https://whimsical.com/cypress-app-user-journey-AgA9ujku8zpN9Smfr9Jjo3).

This ticket is focused on **showing the right steps for each of the different project combinations**. I added a bunch of projects in [this PR](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/19905/files), each with a README explaining which step(s) should be shown. This PR adds E2E tests for each of them, verifying the right steps are indeed shown.

title: Inconsistencies in CYPRESS_DOWNLOAD_PATH_TEMPLATE handling
body:
### Current behavior

There seem to be some inconsistencies in how CYPRESS_DOWNLOAD_PATH_TEMPLATE is handled from the .npmrc file depending on package manager and version.

Given
`CYPRESS_DOWNLOAD_PATH_TEMPLATE=${endpoint}/${platform}-${arch}/cypress.zip`

npm 7 works, though locally i've seen the env fail to get picked up because of casing.
npm 6 attempts to replay endpoint etc with other ENVs (this is unfortunate, but you can escape them but that doesn't work either)
Yarn 1 doesn't remove double quotes.

I haven't tested yarn 3 or npm 8 but they should be looked at, as well as windows useage.

### Desired behavior

Ideally you could set the CYPRESS_DOWNLOAD_PATH_TEMPLATE variable with any package manager

### Test code to reproduce

Try out setting variations of

```sh
CYPRESS_DOWNLOAD_PATH_TEMPLATE=${endpoint}/${platform}-${arch}/cypress.zip
CYPRESS_DOWNLOAD_PATH_TEMPLATE=\${endpoint}/\${platform}-\${arch}/cypress.zip
CYPRESS_DOWNLOAD_PATH_TEMPLATE="${endpoint}/${platform}-${arch}/cypress.zip"
CYPRESS_DOWNLOAD_PATH_TEMPLATE="\${endpoint}/\${platform}-\${arch}/cypress.zip"
```

### Cypress Version

9.3.1

### Other


Where CYPRESS_DOWNLOAD_PATH_TEMPLATE is used
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/lib/tasks/download.js#L67

getEnv implementation
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/lib/util.js#L459

We should probably be setting trim on getENV, that should resolve any double quotes problems.

body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md

- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes  #19709

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
--> N/A

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->
Extends off of #19805 to implement `uncaught:exception`s or application error events in `switchToDomain`.

When uncaught exceptions or errors occur in the secondary domain (SD), we want to fail the current command and test in the primary domain (PD) as long as the `switchToDomain` callback context is still 'open'. If a user wishes to bypass `uncaught:exception`s in the SD, a `cy.on('uncaught:exception')` handler can be defined in the `switchToDomain` callback and `false` can be returned just as described in the [docs](https://docs.cypress.io/api/events/catalog-of-events#Uncaught-Exceptions). However,  `uncaught:exception` events outside the `switchToDomain` context will NOT be called with errors occurring in the SD.  This is mainly due to difficulties serializing function arguments between domains to keep Cypress consistent with the way it works today. Here are a few examples as to how this is supposed to work:

#### Example 1
```js
cy.on('uncaught:exception', (err) => {
  // will NOT be called
})

cy.on('fail', (err, runnable) => {
  // will be called
})

cy.switchToDomain('foobar.com', () => {
  // throws an error
  cy.get('.trigger-sync-error').click()
})
```
#### Example 2
```js
cy.on('fail', (err, runnable) => {
  // will NOT be called
})

cy.switchToDomain('foobar.com', () => {
  cy.on('uncaught:exception', (err) => {
    // will be called
    return false
  })

  // throws an error
  cy.get('.trigger-sync-error').click()
})
```

In regards to the `switchToDomain` context still being open, the functionality should work as follows

#### Example 1
```js
cy.on('fail', (err, runnable) => {
  // Likely will NOT be called since the context window may be closed before the error actually throws
})

cy.switchToDomain('foobar.com', () => {
  cy.get('.trigger-async-error').click()
})
```

#### Example 2
```js
cy.on('fail', (err, runnable) => {
  // Likely will be called since the context window is still open by the time the error throws
})

cy.switchToDomain('foobar.com', () => {
  cy.get('.trigger-async-error').click()
  cy.wait(2000)
  // do some other cy commands
})
```


In the meantime, hopefully the added tests to exercise this behavior serve as documentation for how this functionality is supposed to work. Here are some code snippets followed by their test/runner outcome

#### sync error
```js
cy.switchToDomain('foobar.com', () => {
    cy.get('.trigger-sync-error').click()
  })
```
![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3980464/151238894-14e4aae5-cb5b-4b2a-a2d8-f63ba9d18a3e.png)

#### async error
```js
cy.switchToDomain('foobar.com', () => {
    cy.get('.trigger-async-error').click()
    cy.wait(2000)
  })
```
![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3980464/151238863-37e96bd2-a2f4-4607-9c50-dceed12828e9.png)

#### sync error expecting errors
```js
cy.on('fail', (err, runnable) => {
  done()
})

cy.switchToDomain('foobar.com', () => {
  cy.get('.trigger-sync-error').click()
})
```
![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3980464/151245802-ac756810-effa-4b15-88db-e11dc144b812.png)

#### async error that doesn't get caught as the context window is closed
```js
cy.on('fail', (err, runnable) => {
  // does NOT get called and test passes
})

cy.switchToDomain('foobar.com', () => {
  cy.get('.trigger-async-error').click()
})
```
![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3980464/151246121-c4047133-d12b-4ebd-8e34-2134bdadda03.png)

#### error thrown but `uncaught:exception` returns `false` in SD
```js
cy.on('fail', (err, runnable) => {
  // does NOT get called
})

cy.switchToDomain('foobar.com', () => {
  cy.on('uncaught:exception', () => false)
  cy.get('.trigger-sync-error').click()
})
```
![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3980464/151246523-e5b95308-5d67-4981-b3f9-e6527740cb80.png)

title: Bug: Data attributes not used as given during assertion
body:
### Current behavior

Browser: Chrome 97
NodeJS Version: v16.13.2
OS: Windows 10 Pro 20h2 (19042.1466)

Running a test using data attribute `data-cy`, assertions do not use the same context and fail. When using `cy.get("[data-cy=name]").should("exists")`, this passes as expected, but the element context being checked is different from what was given. 

`[data-toggle=collapse]` becomes `<button.navbar-toggle.collapsed>`

When using `cy.get("[data-cy=name]").should("be.visible")`, the test fails, even if the element is visible. 
When using `cy.get("[data-cy=name]").should("not.be.visible")`, it passes, but that's not the truth of the page.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5670441/151515500-6e41148f-37c9-4dc4-a1a9-99a3550c9a8f.png)

### Desired behavior

In this situation, Cypress should...

- Use the data attribute as it is given during an assertion.
- the .should("be.visible") should find the data attribute element that is clearly visible on the page

### Test code to reproduce

https://github.com/HybridEyeGrillage/cypress-test-tiny

### Cypress Version

9.3.1

### Other

This was also seen in #2130, but the OP had never found a solution.

### User facing changelog

This PR addresses some problems noticed when writing tests for some the components, so there are some user-facing changes, mainly for keyboard and screen reader accessibility for our Cards and the Specs List. There is more that can be done, especially to make the main Specs List match the Inline Specs List keyboard behavior, but I think these are still improvements worth having.

### Additional details

File by file, this PR:

- updates tests checking tabindex of Cards, since we no longer set tabindex on the outer element
- updates RowDirectory to render a button so that it can be toggled with keyboard in the Specs List
- adds Specs List test to catch Clear Search button bug, check link href, check keyboard interactions
- fixes Clear Search bug in Specs List - virtual list was failing after the no-results state because it had no DOM element to render into, `v-show` preserves the DOM of the list even when hidden by the "no results" state.
- prevents "cmd-click" from opening new tabs from specs list links (per Slack convo with Jennifer)
- gives directory rows in Specs List a unique ID to manage aria expanded state
- makes the rows have an outline more like the Inline Specs List when an item has keyboard focus
- adds cypress-real-events to `frontend-shared` (same version we already have)
- adds assertions and states to the Card component test
- tweaks card markup for accessibility
- adds an assertion to CopyButton. Our usual way of asserting text getting copied doesn't seem to work in component tests, need to look into this
- adds component tests for StandardModal. This is tested plenty in E2E but it is nice to gather the expectations in one place and test the props directly.
- adds some i18n imports in StandardModal components, and some class re-ordering caused by file save
- fixes a random font-weight that didn't get updated to semi bold in the header yet

title: Cypress GRPC plugin
body:
### What would you like?

Easy way to test GRPC backend calls.
Currently there is no clear description how to use GRPC with cypress.
There is an option to introduce REST gateway, but this is fallback to REST instead of using GRPC fully.

E.g. for REST
    cy.request({
        method: 'GET',
        url: appUrl/status
    }).then((response) => {
        expect(response).body('state').to.equal("running")
    });
    
    
    **what would be the equivalent for the GRPC service?**
    url is appUrl
    grpcMessage: "statusCheck"
    proto file is: my.proto    
    
    

### Why is this needed?

GRPC is 10x more efficient than using rest (speed and size of messages) according to the web tutorials.
Highly likely that GRPC is going to replace REST for a the new applications.

Cypress is great, but it lacks examples and tutorials how to use it with GRPC if GRPC server has no rest-like endpoints like swagger (REST gateway).

body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...

- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes #19712

Move logic for determining whether or not the `--openssl-legacy-provider` flag should be passed for Node17 built with OpenSSL v3+ from binary to CLI package. The last change to check for OpenSSL version is checking the version of Node process bundled with Cypress, not the system Node process on the user's machine. This caused the check to be false and always skip adding the `--openssl-legacy-provider` flag when the system node version is Node 17 built with OpenSSL v3+. 

Moving this logic aligns with where we determine the system Node version and parse the ORIGINAL_NODE_OPTIONS.

I have updated the cypress-test-node-versions repository to perform a simple test to verify that run mode works as expected. [PR](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-test-node-versions/pull/62). You can verify the commit with this change builds successfully with Node 17.

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

- Fix regression in [9.3.0](/guides/references/changelog#9-3-0) where the bundled Node process was checked to determine if the `--openssl-legacy-provider` flag should be passed the plugins' child process. This always resolved to Cypress's bundled Node version of 16.5.0 which was built with OpenSSL v1, when it should have been checking the system Node process's OpenSSL version. Fixes [#19712](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/19712).

title: v9.4.0 regression with lerna monorepo setup: invoking cypress open from a sub folder causes "env: node\r: No such file or directory"
body:
### Current behavior

In a given lerna monorepo setup, for example [this one](https://github.com/muratkeremozcan/lerna-react-ts-cypress):

* Cypress is installed at the root, but the spec files live with the app / package / service
* We can trigger `cypress run / open` from the root  level, in order to hit app level `package.json`
I.e.
```bash
# while at repo root

yarn start:a
yarn cy:open-a  ## starts cypress runner for app a

yarn start:b
yarn cy:open-b ## starts cypress runer for app b
```

This has been working up to 9.3.1, but with 9.4.0 there is a regression.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34237651/151871045-0c1ef2fd-21d1-45c8-a314-30da0b2d079c.png)


### Desired behavior

Lerna mono repo setup allows Cypress to be launched from root level, the way it did prior to v9.4.0.

### Test code to reproduce

Clone [lerna-react-ts-cypress](https://github.com/muratkeremozcan/lerna-react-ts-cypress.git). Install. Stay on repo root level.

```bash
yarn install / yarn i / yarn # at root level; all sub-level dependencies are taken care of
yarn start:a / start:b / start:c # start app-*
# on a different tab
yarn cy:open-a / cy:open-b / cy:open-c #  open cypress test runner at app level
# on a different tab
yarn cy:run-a / cy:run-b / cy:run-c # run cypress headlessly at app level
```

Upgrade to 9.4.0 and repeat.

### Cypress Version

9.4.0

### Other

May be a duplicate of https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/19986

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

n/a

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->
#### Update 2/16/2022

The goal of this PR is to make namespaces, methods, and properties work on the Cypress API ([`Cypress.*`](https://docs.cypress.io/api/cypress-api/custom-commands)) within the `switchToDomain` context.

In order to get most of the properties to work properly, the `Cypress.config()` from the primary is now being synced with the secondary via #20102. This allows for a lot of properties, like `arch`, `platform`, `spec`, etc to match what is available in the primary, as well as default configurations registered on the new Cypress instance. 

`config`  and `env` are the only things that are synced to the spec bridge. Every other configuration method, such as `Cypress.*.defaults()` or `Cypress.env()` are NOT synced to the secondary and are considered their own isolated world where configuration changes persist between `switchToDomain` calls between the same spec bridge. 

Another important implementation detail in this PR is the outlawing of using `Cypress.Server.*` and its related methods such as `cy.server()` and `cy.route()`. We did not want to consider supporting these methods since server is deprecated and will be removed in the future. Also, `Cypress.Cookies.*` configurations are also forbidden as they do not apply to secondary domains. Likely this API is going to be replaces by `cy.session` and other related methods in the near future. Little `cy` session methods can STILL be used in `switchToDomain`.

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3980464/152235042-e016c511-2afd-4bc5-beff-e9cfd972bf85.png)

NOTE: decisions around `cy.intercept` still need to be worked out within multi-domain.

NOTE: The use of `Cypress.session.*` and `cy.session` still needs to be explored in multi-domain, and is out of scope for this PR.

fix: Fix issues with stack traces and command log in Chrome 99
body:
### User facing changelog
Fixes multiple issues in Chrome 99:
- No longer throws an exception when attempting to display a `Document` or `ShadowRoot` in the Cypress command log.
- Stack traces were not reporting properly.

### Additional details
Chrome 99 includes an updated version of v8, which breaks our stack trace trimming. A fix is included with commentary on why the change is needed.

It also updates the behavior around enumerating properties of StyleSheets. There's no good reason we should be doing this at all though.

## How has the user experience changed?
In older versions, when a ShadowRoot was rendered to the command log, it would treat it as a Javascript object, and enumerate its properties, looking like this:

![Screenshot_20220210_082740](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3003404/153459301-f260c3cd-f3d9-42f6-99b5-e93554133396.png)

After this change, it is treated like an HTML element, resulting in displaying this in the command log:

![Screenshot_20220210_090443](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3003404/153459517-abcbc003-2023-4ed4-b9fc-df7e00059234.png)

The same is true for a `Document`. They now render their inner html to the command log rather than a verbose enumeration of their properties (which includes the innerHTML).

Fixed poor network issue in MacOS on initial requests.

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->
I have been experiencing tests hangs when run cypress locally and always timed out. Digging into the issue, finally narrowed down `net.connect` makes super slow when http agent makes requests. 
This eventually turned out that NodeJS bug in MacOS. I have reported in https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/41699 for more details.

In Cypress, when outgoing requests happen, http agent first lookup DNS records and find out the fasted IP family.
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/packages/network/lib/connect.ts#L24
When there are 4 hosts in a DNS record like www.google.com, it tries 4 net.connect() for the hosts which eventually makes 4x slower than usual request without net.connect() in my experiment.

Simplified sample code to reproduce the issue from https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/packages/server/lib/request.js#L434
```js
// test.js
let r = require('@cypress/request')
const { agent } = require("./packages/network");

const url = 'https://www.google.com'
const defaults = {
  agent,
  headers: {
    'Connection': 'keep-alive',
  },
  proxy: null, // upstream proxying is handled by CombinedAgent
}

console.time(url)
const reqStream = r({url, ...defaults});
reqStream.on('request', (req) => {
  console.timeLog(url, "on request")
})
reqStream.on('socket', socket => {
  console.timeLog(url, 'socket created')
  socket.on('lookup', () => {
    console.timeLog(url, 'socket lookup')
  })
  socket.on('connect', () => {
    console.timeLog(url, 'socket connected')
  })
})
reqStream.on('response', (incomingRes) => {
  incomingRes.on('data', data => {
    console.timeLog(url, 'data received')
  })
})
```

```bash
https://www.google.com: 96.893ms socket lookup
https://www.google.com: 2.167s socket connected
https://www.google.com: 10.292s data received
https://www.google.com: 10.293s data received
https://www.google.com: 10.293s data received
https://www.google.com: 10.293s data received
https://www.google.com: 10.293s data received
```

#### After fix
```bash
  cypress:network:connect beginning getAddress { hostname: 'www.google.com', port: 443 } +0ms
https://www.google.com: 10.707ms on request
  cypress:network:connect got addresses { hostname: 'www.google.com', port: 443, addresses: [ { address: '172.253.62.99', family: 4 }, { address: '172.253.62.103', family: 4 }, { address: '172.253.62.104', family: 4 }, { address: '172.253.62.105', family: 4 }, { address: '172.253.62.106', family: 4 }, { address: '172.253.62.147', family: 4 }, { address: '2607:f8b0:4004:835::2004', family: 6 } ] } +79ms

https://www.google.com: 325.534ms socket connected
https://www.google.com: 509.304ms data received
https://www.google.com: 509.633ms data received
https://www.google.com: 509.929ms data received
https://www.google.com: 510.103ms data received
https://www.google.com: 510.251ms data received
```

<!-- Provide before and after examples of the change.
Screenshots or GIFs are preferred. -->
I have observed http requests hangs or pending status initially and randomly fails with timeout. Once the website has 3rd party dependencies such as Segment, Heap, Google Analytics etcs, it all goes slow for the net.connect issue and finally made the tests unreliable.
I verified with my colleagues that it works and this improves network performance significantly running tests in MacOS. This would solve most problem with timeouts or flakiness due to tests hang for Mac users.

title: docs(data-context): explain concepts in data-context
body:
- Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1016

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

N/A

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

Explain interplay between `data`, `actions` and `sources` in `data-context` package. It's a work in progress; we should continue to update this as we go. I got this information [here](https://www.notion.so/cypressdx/TR-Unification-Development-0c9636f71d5748e6b8f0048f35114061), as well as my personal experience and looking at the patterns @tgriesser introduced.

I noticed a lot of our code doesn't actually adhere to these conventions, since they were not really set in stone when we started the unification project. Many Sources update `coreData` directly, not ideal. We should try to match these conventions as closely as possible.

### Discussion/Question

One thing that does not have a clear practice is data that does not live in `coreData`. For example we have a bunch of flags such as `hasComponentTesting`, which is used for the migration workflow. [It's currently on a Source](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/703548e16ce436b0f23b6962348a43c68d2e0545/packages/data-context/src/sources/MigrationDataSource.ts#L58) and also updated by the Source, which goes against our rules. Should this data:

1. Go in `coreData.migration`? My concern is `coreData` will become a dumping ground for everything, kind of like `config` and `options` in server, where people just stick there variable on one of those so they can access it whenever they want.
2. Leave the data that does not need to be exposed on `coreData` in the Source? If so, should we update it using an Action? Eg `MigrationAction` should always up `MigrationSource`? It's a bit verbose to have these in different files, you need to keep switching back and forth, but if that's going to give us better separation of concerns (write vs read) it might be okay.
3. `this.ctx.update` is only used for `coreData` right now. I wonder if we want a similar pattern for Actions to update temp data in Sources.

### How has the user experience changed?

Screenshots or GIFs are preferred. -->

* This change adds many event-related tests to `type_spec.js`. I decided to move event-related tests to `type_events_spec.js`.

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

Fixes the first comment in the ticket description:

> When you initially click to run the specfile, there's a flash of a plain white screen before the specs panel/runner begins to load. Investigate why this is happening, can we reduce this load time?

It was happening because we were doing `await injectBundle` when injecting the webpack bundle (which has the driver and reporter) when running a spec for the first time, which blocked rendering the runner UI. 

Now, we inject the webpack bundle earlier in the workflow, but don't `await` it, so we don't block the UI. To avoid the chance of a race condition (for example, we run a spec before the bundle is injected, if you refresh on the runner page, for example), we use a deferred promise, so it will wait for the bundle if necessary. In practice, this only happens if you navigate straight to a spec (with `--spec`) or you refresh the page, as opposed to going to the spec list first and clicking one.

Here is the comparison. The main speed up is when you click a spec -> go to the spec runner page. Notice the empty white page that is shown before the UI renders is far shorter in the after video.

### After

title: chore: support vite 2.5
body:
We need to upgrade to the latest version of Vite in order to use our application to test out the Vite team's fix for Cypress component testing. We need to get all the way from 2.4.4 to 2.7.x (and be able to test against 2.8.0-beta.5 internally, even if we don't use it in our normal day-to-day).

The main issue when going from 2.4.4 to 2.5 is that previously, we were (incorrectly) able to import types alongside normal imports. Our linter forced us to do this.

```ts
// Old linter requires this, but Vite will throw an exception when we run this code
import { Ref, ref} from 'vue'

// Vite 2.5+ requires two separate imports
import type { Ref } from 'vue'
import { ref } from 'vue'
```

I updated the linter to support a Typescript-friendly version of "no-duplicate-imports". More information can be found [here](https://github.com/import-js/eslint-plugin-import/blob/main/docs/rules/no-duplicates.md).

- Closes #20093

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

### Additional details
UPDATED 2/15/2022

From our multi-domain discussions, we have currently decided on inheriting in (what we can) for `Cypress.config` and `Cypress.env` and excluding out. This means the values for these two configurations are synced in the secondary domain anytime `switchToDomain` is invoked. Once `switchToDomain` is done, either executing synchronously via assertions or other sync methods or when the command queue is empty, `Cypress.env` and `Cypress.config` are synced back into the primary domain.

It's important to note that only serializable values can be synced between domains. To determine this, we are using the `structuredClone()` algorithm to determine whether a value can be cloned. If the browser under test does not support `structuredClone()`, a ponyfill provided by `core-js-pure` will be used. If a value cannot be cloned, the value is omitted entirely from the config/env object on sync.

This means that in certain cases, some data types in one browser are syncable while in other browsers the may not be. For instance, `Error`s cannot be cloned in firefox but are able to be cloned in most chromium based browsers. At the time of this PR, `structuredClone()` is implemented since firefox 94 and chrome 98. All other browsers need the ponyfill implementation

Serializable values are always synced between domains. However, if both values in any domain are deemed unserializable, those unserializable values persist in their respective domains. However, if one domain contains a serializable value and the other contains an unserializable value of the SAME key, the serializable value is synced (not sure if this is correct). Objects within the config that contain unserializable values are treated entirely as unserializable values. Objects/Arrays will not be merged.

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

n/a

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

This PR accomplishes several things:

* When checking for updates, check the current published version of our manifest, and then decorate the version with metadata coming from NPM

* Whenever a Testing Type context is set (via the CLI, upon configuration, upon opening a testing type, etc) we should immediately be sending another "checked for updates" call and passing "x-testing-type": [testingType] in the headers when checking for updates. The rationale is that normally cypress "checks for updates" upon first launching in `cypress open` mode, but at that point, its unlikely to have had a Testing Type set (unless it was set in the CLI). The existing logic subsequently "checks for updates" once an hour - but the point of the telemetry of "Checked for updates" is to know which testing type users are using. Therefore we need to "check for updates" on initial launch, but subsequently immediately "check for updates" AGAIN once a testing type is selected.

* Use the @packages/network package agent to ensure that remote requests to the Cypress Dashboard support HTTP proxies

* In the process of working with the network agent, I discovered some nuances that were previously handled by [request-promise](https://github.com/cypress-io/request/blob/master/request.js#L301-L303) where the appropriate port was being set based on the protocol type. Since this is a combined agent rather than a full on http or https agent, node [defaults](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/master/lib/_http_client.js#L164) the port to 80 and this causes a problem if we're not using a proxy. Thus, I'm ensuring that the appropriate port is being used in this scenario.

title: feat: CLI `config` not supporting nested properties correctly
body:
- Closes UNIFY-1028

### User facing changelog
Can now pass in testing-type specific config options via `--config` without nesting JSON. 

### Additional details
With the addition of more testing type specific config options, and especially with the requirement that `specPattern` be configured per testing type, using `--config` via command line was a bit clunky, requiring a user to nest the config value.

### How has the user experience changed?
#### Before

```sh
$ cd packages/driver
$ node ../../scripts/cypress run '--config={"e2e": {"specPattern": "**/*.spec.jsx"}}'
# Works!

$ node ../../scripts/cypress run '--config={"specPattern": "**/*.spec.jsx"}'
`specPattern` is not a valid configuration option

https://on.cypress.io/configuration

`specPattern` is not a valid configuration option
```

#### After

```sh
$ node ../../scripts/cypress run '--config={"e2e": {"specPattern": "**/*.spec.jsx"}}'
# Still works!

$ node ../../scripts/cypress run '--config={"specPattern": "**/*.spec.jsx", "baseUrl": "https://example.com"}'
# Now also works
```

This example resolves to the the config of

title: Handle future Chrome version making document.domain immutable
body:
### What would you like?

Chrome is planning to [make `document.domain` immutable](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/immutable-document-domain/).

In Chrome 100, setting `document.domain` will display the following warning in the Issues panel. 

![emNay9XjqqyNy3wEi0Aa](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1157043/153471515-3a9e7707-8fdc-4c45-83e0-510ee2491e34.png)

In Chrome 106 (due for release in April 2022), support for setting `document.domain` will be removed. It will log the following warning in the console and setting it will silently fail, causing a cross-origin error to be thrown when Cypress attempts to interact with the AUT. The exact release is subject to change based on the response to the [Intent to Ship](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/_oRc19PjpFo/).

![Screen Shot 2022-02-10 at 12 56 13 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1157043/153467656-bd8030a3-4d59-4e56-9156-223df6d8086f.png)

### Mitigation

This issue can be mitigated by attaching a `Origin-Agent-Cluster: ?0` header to the top page's request, any requests for the AUT frame's src, and any requests for the spec frame and support file frame. That will allow `document.domain` to be set as needed.

### More Information

- [Chrome blog announcement](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/immutable-document-domain/)
- [RFC](https://github.com/mikewest/deprecating-document-domain)
- [document.domain docs](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:docs/security/document-domain.md)



### Why is this needed?

Cypress relies on setting `document.domain` so that a test can visit multiple subdomains under the same super-domain in a single test.

Once support for setting `document.domain` is removed, tests that rely on that behavior will no longer function and will fail with a cross-origin error.


### Other

_No response_

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

If there are no existing projects on the connect to dashboard page, choose an existing project will be hidden.

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

UNIFY-1065 brings up a situation where the current project does not have a project id and there are no existing projects for the selected organization. When that happens and the user selects "Choose an existing project" nothing happens (since there's no list of projects to display to connect to). Instead of letting nothing happen, we will not allow the user to even select "Choose an existing project" in that scenario.

In addition to "Choose an existing project" not working correctly, the user has the choice to "Connect project" rather than "Create project" which is more appropriate in this case. Additionally this button does nothing as well. We will fix this so that we fall into the "Create project" workflow in this scenario.

### How has the user experience changed?
<!-- Provide before and after examples of the change.
Screenshots or GIFs are preferred. -->

title: fix: Ensuring browser 'Focus' button is safe if browser window has been closed
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

There's a couple things going on here:

* With Chrome, we send a `focus:browser:window` automation event to refocus the window; if we do this after the automation client disconnects (i.e. the window is closed), it fails and triggers a reconnect attempt, which locks up more ore less all interactions in the launchpad. We can check the socket status prior to sending the event, resulting in a no-op when the Focus button is pressed.
* With Firefox, we execute a command through the launchpad to show the browser instance. However, this is failing even before closing the window; investigation is ongoing, this PR will be updated with findings.
* With Electron, the process is killed when the window is closed, so we have no problems currently (or after this PR).

- Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-430

### Summary

This adds two new error states to the login modal - one to cover the existing `AUTH_COULD_NOT_LAUNCH_BROWSER` error and another that acts as a catchall for errors during auth process. We also add one new component to correctly format text to copy in way that doesn't look like a terminal. 

### Additional details

The biggest change is to change `isAuthBrowserOpened` in graphql to `authState` so it can contain all the properties needed to drive the UI according to the messages from the auth process.

Other notable changes are a new `catch` and unit test in `auth.ts`, and new CT and E2E coverage for the new errors.

title: No log cy.intercept()
body:
### What would you like?

In most use cases of cy.intercept() logging the intercepted request to the step logs is great. And logging should be the default. But in one particular case I wish I could turn it off. 



### Why is this needed?

In `beforeEach` in `index.js` we have a `cy.intercept()` set up that all it does, is take the incoming request and adds a new header to the API request. We are adding a unique header so that we can trace it in our API logs later. 
For those intercepts I do not need to see the interception in the logs. 

So my feature request would be to add a `cy.intercept(....., { log:false})` feature. 

### Other

_No response_

title: chore: Refactor multi-domain communication lifecycle
body:
Refactors the communication lifecycle and how command and logs are handled for multi-domain.

Previously, commands in the secondary domain had proxy versions in the primary domain. A similar mechanism was in place for logs. This meant that they had to be kept in sync and that certain event listeners had to set up and torn down at the right time in order to support them. This led to various timing issues and complicated workarounds. It also required adding a convoluted pausing mechanism to the command queue in the secondary.

Since the command proxies only needed to exist in the primary domain for the purpose of sending messages to the reporter, it's easier to do that directly (more or less) from the the actual command instances in the secondary. The same applies for logs. This simplifies things greatly as the events are simply a stream and can be listened to globally, removing the need to worry about setting them up and tearing them down in sync with the switchToDomain command.

One unfortunate side effect is that this PR removes support for the `done` callback. It was failing with the refactor, and since we had decided not to support it inside the switchToDomain callback after all, I didn't deem it worthwhile to spend time fixing it. As demonstrated in this PR, promises can be used instead of done callbacks.

This PR also makes some file name and test name changes that aren't strictly necessary, they're just some cleanup I did while implementing the refactor.

body:
[![WhiteSource Renovate](https://app.renovatebot.com/images/banner.svg)](https://renovatebot.com)

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | Age | Adoption | Passing | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [next](https://nextjs.org) ([source](https://togithub.com/vercel/next.js)) | [`^10.1.2` -> `^12.0.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/next/10.1.2/12.1.0) | [![age](https://badges.renovateapi.com/packages/npm/next/12.1.0/age-slim)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![adoption](https://badges.renovateapi.com/packages/npm/next/12.1.0/adoption-slim)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![passing](https://badges.renovateapi.com/packages/npm/next/12.1.0/compatibility-slim/10.1.2)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![confidence](https://badges.renovateapi.com/packages/npm/next/12.1.0/confidence-slim/10.1.2)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2022-23646](https://togithub.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-fmvm-x8mv-47mj)

Next.js is a React framework. Starting with version 10.0.0 and prior to version 12.1.0, Next.js is vulnerable to User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information. In order to be affected, the `next.config.js` file must have an `images.domains` array assigned and the image host assigned in `images.domains` must allow user-provided SVG. If the `next.config.js` file has `images.loader` assigned to something other than default, the instance is not affected. Version 12.1.0 contains a patch for this issue. As a workaround, change `next.config.js` to use a different `loader configuration` other than the default.

### Impact
- **Affected**: All of the following must be true to be affected
  - Next.js between version 10.0.0 and 12.0.10
  - The `next.config.js` file has [images.domains](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/next/image#domains) array assigned
  - The image host assigned in [images.domains](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/next/image#domains) allows user-provided SVG
- **Not affected**: The `next.config.js` file has [images.loader](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/next/image#loader-configuration) assigned to something other than default

### Patches
[Next.js 12.1.0](https://togithub.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v12.1.0)

### Workarounds
Change `next.config.js` to use a different [loader configuration](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/next/image#loader-configuration) other than the default, for example:

```js
module.exports = {
  images: {
    loader: 'imgix',
    path: 'https://example.com/myaccount/',
  },
}
```

Or if you want to use the [`loader`](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/next/image#loader) prop on the component, you can use `custom`:
```js
module.exports = {
  images: {
    loader: 'custom',
  },
}
```

### [`v12.0.9`](https://togithub.com/vercel/next.js/releases/v12.0.9)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/vercel/next.js/compare/v12.0.8...v12.0.9)

**This upgrade is completely backward-compatible and recommended for all users on versions below 12.0.9**

Vulnerable code could allow a bad actor to trigger a denial of service attack via the `/${locale}/_next/` route for anyone running a Next.js app at version >= 12.0.0, and using built-in [i18n routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/advanced-features/i18n-routing) functionality.

##### How to Upgrade

-   We have released patch versions for both the stable and canary channels of Next.js.
-   To upgrade run `npm install next@latest --save`

##### Impact

-   **Affected:** All of the following must be true to be affected by this CVE
    -   Next.js versions between `v12.0.0` and `v12.0.9`
    -   Using next start or a custom server
    -   Using the built-in i18n support
-   **Not affected:**
    -   Deployments on Vercel (vercel.com) are not affected along with similar environments where invalid requests are filtered before reaching Next.js.

We recommend everyone to upgrade regardless of whether you can reproduce the issue or not.

##### How to Assess Impact

If your server has seen requests to any route under the prefix `/${locale}/_next/` that have triggered a heap overflow error, this was caused by the patched issue.

##### What is Being Done

As Next.js has grown in popularity and usage by enterprises, it has received the attention of security researchers and auditors. We are thankful to our users for their investigation and responsible disclosure of the original bug.

We've landed a patch that ensures this is handled properly so the requested route no longer crashes and triggers a heap overflow.

Regression tests for this attack were added to the [i18n integration test suite](https://togithub.com/vercel/next.js/pull/33503/files#diff-ed73e662e3c049828f92017b8104734e08b868acf10d4d621c44266a72825df6)

-   A public CVE was released.
-   We encourage responsible disclosure of future reports. Please email us at `security@vercel.com`. We are actively monitoring this mailbox.

<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->
n/a

### Additional details
The goal of this PR is to fix the `err.onFail` is not a function bug we are seeing while writing multi-domain unit tests, as well as unify the error serialization across domains. 

`err.onFail` was failing due to non serializable properties being stringified back to the primary domain, causing the error to fail. Instead of trying to send non serializable values as a serialized string, we now just omit these properties before sending the error (similar to env and config). Now that we process errors in the `ran:domain:fn` context, we need to also account for scenarios when `throw 'oops'` or something is thrown in the secondary that may/may not be an error object. This PR should cover this at a basic level.

I would have liked to use the `structuredClone` algorithm to clone Errors where applicable, but interestingly all properties declared on the error are removed when trying to clone, either with native Chrome implementations or the ponyfill. Once the Error is sent through `postMessage`, it loses it's prototype hierarchy and ultimately just becomes an object. Therefor, I figured the method we had to pre/post process errors how we do it now is likely preferable.

title: chore: fix system-test-firefox screenshots_spec flake
body: ### User facing changelog n/a ### Additional details There is logic in our screenshots that, if the image is big enough, and thus multi-part, we compare each part to the previous part to make sure that we are truly getting new data and not just the previous data. If the parts are the same, we retry until they are different or a timeout is reached. In some of the system tests, we are taking pictures of pages that are purely one color. In the tests I've changed, we don't limit the size of the screenshot to the viewport, so we are receiving huge images in 10 parts that are all exactly the same. This triggers the retry logic. In the two tests I've updated, we do this 4 times and over time this is pressing on memory consumption which may cause firefox to crash. I'm fixing the tests as a part of this PR by limiting the screenshots to the viewport, but I think it's worth investigating if there's a less memory-intensive way of doing the retries (though this scenario may not occur too much outside of tests like this). <!--

If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

### Additional details

#20250 was merged with a bad assumption:

> Removed {{ arch }} from Circle cache keys - this is slightly different b/t docker and machine runners, and we need the machine runner to be able to run docker commands. This is fine because we use a workflow per arch and caches are scoped to a single workflow: [circleci.com/docs/2.0/caching/#writing-to-the-cache-in-workflows](https://circleci.com/docs/2.0/caching/#writing-to-the-cache-in-workflows)

In fact, this was a misreading of the docs, caches are shared across workflows. Merging #20250 broke the cache for darwin and windows by using the linux cache for all 3 workflows.

This PR avoids the mentioned `arch` issue by using the checksum of $PLATFORM instead. Unfortunately there's not a way to just put the literal $PLATFORM in the cacheKey, only the checksum. {{ Environment.PLATFORM }} won't work - and {{ arch }} can't be used because it differs between Docker and `machine` executors, which we want to share a cache.

There is currently a failure in test-binary-against-recipes that is unrelated to this PR and has to do with https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/20144

The net_stubbing test [should delay the same amount on every response](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/20297/files#diff-801bb85bee26e7f7d674e624fae1fe6583afac01bd5de659b60f928783a3429eR1660) has been flaky. It typically fails because the delay ends up being slightly over the acceptable buffer of 50 ms. 

The other tests in this file handle the buffer slightly differently giving a window of 200 ms by saying the actual delay needs to be within (delay + 100 +/- 100). I updated this test (which is really just testing that each subsequent interception also applies the delay) to do the same and it seems to be passing more consistently. It's worth noting that the delay specified is a "minimum" and not really intended to be super accurate (https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/intercept#Response-object-properties).

title: chore: optimize circle ci jobs to increase performance and cleanup incorrect configurations
body:
## Details

### Default Resource Class
- Set `resource_class` to be `medium` by default as most of our jobs ended up using `medium`, and some jobs that should have been `medium` were really `small`. The exception should be something other than `medium`.

### Increase Parallelism
- Increased parallelism on several jobs were long running jobs blocking others:
  - `run-launchpad-integration-tests-chrome`
  - `run-frontend-shared-component-tests-chrome` 
  - `run-app-integration-tests-chrome`
  - `reporter-integration-tests`

### Decrease Parallelism
- Removed parallelism of several jobs because they were not parallelizing anything and instead were duplicating the exact same steps N number of times, increasing resource cost for zero gain
  - `npm-vue`
  - `cli-visual-tests`

### Increase Resource Class
- Several jobs were previously on `small`, which I have bumped to `medium` because they are either running Cypress tests, were fairly long-running, were maxing out their CPU, or because they stand in the critical path blocking other jobs
  -  `ui-components-integration-tests` was running Cypress tests
  - `npm-vite-dev-server` was running Cypress tests
  - `npm-angular` was running Cypress tests and fairly long running
  - `check-ts` fairly long running, pegged CPU
  - `server-performance-tests` fairly long running, pegged CPU
  - `server-unit-tests` fairly long running, pegged CPU
  - `linux-lint` fairly long running, pegged CPU
- One job is in the critical path and blocks other jobs and its worthwhile to try to squeeze out all time savings we can at the expensive of higher resource cost
  -  `system-tests-node-modules-install` was bumped from `small` to `medium` 

### Decrease Resource Class
- Several jobs were downgraded to `small` from `medium` because they don't need extra resources
  - `unit-tests-release`

## Needs Additional Eyes

cc @lmiller1990 and @elevatebart 

I couldn't tell offhand, but from what I read in the code I believe that `npm-react` is not actually testing all of the examples we intended it to test. It uses `CIRCLE_NODE_INDEX` to manually "chunk" and parallelize the example tests for vue across around 8 machines, but I don't think the logic is written correctly, and in fact it's **only running** up to 8 examples and not all of them. I could be wrong though.

title: chore: fix net stubbing flaky tests due to bleeding interceptions
body: ### User facing changelog n/a ### Additional details There is a bug (logged [here](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/20397)) that will cause intercepted requests to bleed over into the next test. This seems to happen when you're just testing that the request is intercepted and then immediately move on to the next test. By moving onto the next test the response doesn't actually make it back to the client and the browser triggers an automatic retry. This can cause a problem if the next test is also testing the same route since it will intercept the retried call causing duplicate interceptions or interceptions when there weren't supposed to be any when testing that the interception doesn't occur. In the spirit of trying to ensure that builds are less flaky, we are tweaking the flaky tests in net_stubbing_spec that tend to do this kind of thing a lot so that they have unique routes being tested each time. We are then deferring the fix for the actual [problem](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/20397) since this tends to be something that will cause a problem when testing intercept itself rather than something that a consumer might run across frequently. ### How has the user experience changed? This is an example of the issue occurring. Note that the test that does not send any XHR calls actually sees two: With the changes on this PR we now have different routes as you can see here: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4873279/156015250-d094b9f6-15ba-474c-bf46-330ec7ec2e48.png) ### PR Tasks - [X] Have tests been added/updated? - [na] Has the original issue (or this PR, if no issue exists) been tagged with a release in ZenHub? Our previous approach was to try and create a config file dynamically based on your framework and bundler. There is far too many combinations for this to be reliable. In addition, there were no tests verifying the generated config file actually worked correctly, so a lot things were not working as you'd expected.

This PR does a few things:

1. move to a more simple approach of hard-coding the config for each framework/library combo. It's simple but scales, we can easily add more.
2. Improve framework detection. Now we can recommend the correct version(s) of things like `@cypress/vue`, `@cypress/webpack-dev-server` etc, depending on the version of your libraries.
3. Move all the logic around detecting frameworks out of `data-context` into a new package called `scaffold-config`.
4. Adds a project for each framework/library combo we support in `system-tests`. There's some duplication across `npm/{react,vue}`, but ultimately we want to collapse most of those tests into `system-tests`, so this is a good place to start.
5. Adds tests around the launchpad config generation workflow, at the end verifying that the generated config file matches one that's known to work (based on a system-test using the same config file).

I documented how to add more projects and configurations here: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/20306/files#diff-8b46b4bb0349c91b80c3f521cb760e26fb444cca40a712b4dd9040384cd6bb0f

title: Give users an option to ignore --parallel or --record flags when Cypress Dashboard is down
body:
### What would you like?

A new configuration option to instruct the cypress runner to handle failures from the Cypress Dashboard servers without fully failing the test run. Allow users to configure the runner to continue running the tests without smart orchestration and without recording test results if the Dashboard is down.

### Why is this needed?

When tests are run with `--record` or `--parallel`, the cypress runner attempts to communicate with the Cypress Dashboard servers before proceeding with any tests. If the server returns a 5** status three times in a row, the runner prints an error and exits the process.

It would be helpful if there was an option to fail gracefully here and automatically switch over to running the tests without parallelization, or without any of the dependencies that require the Cypress Dashboard to be available. If the dashboard is not available, it's important to me that my CI builds can continue to run and pass or fail based on the test results.

The servers are generally stable, but we've had two incidents where the servers went down and caused all of our CI builds to fail. Those failures mean we can't merge PRs, since a passing build is a required status check in our Github config. Luckily, the two times where the Dashboard went down were resolved fairly quickly, but it would have slowed down our response time if we needed to merge and deploy an urgent fix to our application.

### Other

_No response_

title: webpack-dev-server always compiles all spec files
body:
### Current behavior

Webpack-dev-server currently compiles all spec files even when only a single one is needed, resulting in slow compilation of even simple component tests when an application is large.

### Desired behavior

When we only need one spec file, we should only compile that one file (and its dependencies).

### Test code to reproduce

With https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-realworld-app/tree/10.0.0: 

```sh
$ npx cypress run --ct --spec src/components/AlertBar.cy.tsx
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3003404/155610141-5d061db0-27f2-44be-98b9-514e84cfe147.png)

Notice how even though only AlertBar.cy.tsx is needed, there are chunks for spec-0, spec-1, spec-2, etc - one for each component test in the repo. The dependency graph is therefore extremely large. The same thing happens in open mode - opening a single spec results in the entire application being compiled.

### Cypress Version

9.5.0

### Other

In `npm/webpack-dev-server/src/makeWebpackConfig.ts`, we pass a list of every spec file in the repository into `CypressCTOptionsPlugin`. We should instead consider passing in only the support file initially, and in the plugin listening for server events requesting specific additional files. We can then compile them on-demand, rather than all up-front.

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

- Ensure we are always recommending a `cypress.config.js` that is guaranteed to work with your framework.
- Ensure we recommend correct dependencies to install for component testing.

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

__This is Lachlan's work from #20350 with the example projects__

______

Our previous approach was to try and create a config file dynamically based on your framework and bundler. There is far too many combinations for this to be reliable. In addition, there were no tests verifying the generated config file actually worked correctly, so a lot things were not working as you'd expected.

This PR does a few things:

1. move to a more simple approach of hard-coding the config for each framework/library combo. It's simple but scales, we can easily add more.
2. Improve framework detection. Now we can recommend the correct version(s) of things like `@cypress/vue`, `@cypress/webpack-dev-server` etc, depending on the version of your libraries.
3. Move all the logic around detecting frameworks out of `data-context` into a new package called `scaffold-config`.
4. Adds a project for each framework/library combo we support in `system-tests`. There's some duplication across `npm/{react,vue}`, but ultimately we want to collapse most of those tests into `system-tests`, so this is a good place to start.
5. Adds tests around the launchpad config generation workflow, at the end verifying that the generated config file matches one that's known to work (based on a system-test using the same config file).

I documented how to add more projects and configurations here: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/20306/files#diff-8b46b4bb0349c91b80c3f521cb760e26fb444cca40a712b4dd9040384cd6bb0f

title: chore: fixing eslint duplicate imports
body:
### Summary

- Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1213

This PR:
1. Adds `*.vue` to the lint configuration so that we lint Vue files and catch broken rules like `no-unused-variables`.
2. Fixes all the `*.vue` errors and warnings.
3. Swaps `no-duplicate-imports` and `imports/no-duplicates` for `@typescript-eslint/no-duplicate-imports` for the entire codebase to (correctly) support type-only imports vs code imports.
4. Adds `import type` where necessary in the few places outside of the Vue files.

### Why

I'm running into issues when writing new Vite Dev Server code where type-only imports aren't supported like they are elsewhere in the codebase. Then, I noticed that that's the case for most of our codebase. After fixing it, I saw that Vue files were being skipped during some linter tasks, which led to a ton of unused variables and the like making it into the codebase.

Instead of ignoring this issues and spot-fixing it, I updated all Vue files to pass the lint rules.

### no-duplicate-imports rules is functioning incorrectly

```ts
import { createServer as viteCreateServer } from 'vite'

/* 
 * eslint in `npm/vite-dev-server` will error here,
 * whereas it's fine in `packages/launchpad`
 * and elsewhere in the codebase.
*/
import type { ViteDevServer } from 'vite' 
```

### no-unused-variables doesn't throw a linter error in Vue (more rules are also broken)

```vue
<script>
// an entire file
const foo = 1 // foo is unused, but there's no error
console.log('1')
</script>
```

### Duplicate imports work elsewhere in our codebase, backstory

We added a rule from `@typescript-eslint` to support type-only imports without throwing errors. I added this as a one-off in `launchpad`, but didn't apply it to the rest of the codebase.

Later versions of Vite **require** you to separate import types.

**This PR adds the same rules around the codebase and starts linting \*.vue files with the same standards that *.ts, *.js files get.**

**Additionally, because we're now linting our *.vue files, I found quite a few unused variables, methods, and the like inside of our existing Vue code!** Including one entire mutation.

### After this change

**Duplicate imports don't throw**

```ts
// 😀 no errors
import { createServer as viteCreateServer } from 'vite'
import type { ViteDevServer } from 'vite' 
```

**Unused variables do throw**

```vue
<script>
// an entire file
const foo = 1 // foo is unused, and eslint catches the failure
console.log('1')
</script>
```

title: Typescript error while using Cypress.Command.add(): Property 'selector' does not exist on type 'JQuery<HTMLElement>'
body:
### Current behavior

I am getting a Typescript error for those cases:
- Cypress.Command.add() with { prevSubject: true }
```ts
Cypress.Commands.add("newCommand", { prevSubject: true }, (element) => {});
```
In the above example, `element` is of type `unknown` but instead, it should be `JQuery<HTMLElement>`, this could be handled by passing the generics values like that:
```ts
Cypress.Commands.add<"newCommand","element">("newCommand", { prevSubject: true }, (element) => {});
```
But I think passing `true` to the `prevSubject` option, the element type should be `JQuery<HTMLElement>` by itself. 

- Cypress.Command.add() with {prevSubject: "element" }
```ts
Cypress.Commands.add("newCommand", { prevSubject: "element" }, (element) => {
  element.selector
});
```
I am trying to access the `selector` property, but I got a typescript error that it does not exist on type `JQuery<HTMLElement>`


### Desired behavior

No typescript error should be printed, as the `selector` property does exist in the `element` object.

### Test code to reproduce

https://github.com/atarek12/cypress/blob/fix-prevSubject-types/cli/types/tests/cypress-tests.ts#L87

### Cypress Version

9.5.0

### Other

_No response_

title: chore: percy updates
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist

- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1214

Once this PR is merged, we can enable the "Wait for base build" feature in Percy, because we will ensure `10.0-release` and  `develop` builds always finalize. This will dramatically improve the usability of our Percy diffs.

### Additional details

This PR modifies our circle.yml to:

- Remove Percy target branch and commits, and remove the `required` jobs for percy-finalize. After this PR merges, "wait for base build" will be turned on in our Percy settings, which means each PR will always wait for the ideal build for the target branch to finalize and compare with that, instead of ignoring in-progress or unfinalized builds which often leads to an apparent comparison with `develop` when making a PR into 10.0-release for example.

- Restore the `wait-on-circle-jobs` polling JS process. This polling lets us ensure the that builds on `10.0-release` and `develop` will always finalize, since now PR builds will wait for this before they begin a diff. Without this, builds only finalize when all required jobs pass, which can lead to multiple problems.

- Add new logic to `wait-on-circle-jobs` based on branch names:

Branches `10.0-release` and `develop` will always allow Percy to finalize for a given run.  Even if some jobs that generate snapshots fail in CI, for a given commit on those, we always finalize so that PRs with that commit as the merge base will have something to diff against. The polling allows us to move forward when things are completed, not just when

Other branches - ie, feature branches, will finalize only if all required jobs are passing. If there are flaky tests, PR authors must "rerun from failed" to get a finalized percy build that includes all expected snapshots, or if the flake was introduced on the branch, fixing the flake would be better.

Documentation of how Percy should be used, and where it fits into the PR review process, has been added to the internal Unified Dev Process Google doc, since Percy is only used internally. For the same reason, I've removed the Percy section from the draft Testing Strategy and Styleguide. That guide has been moved into `/guides` at the suggestion of @flotwig, an that seems like the right place for it.

title: before hooks not running in expected order
body:
### What would you like?

when using `Before` and `BeforeEach` within a `describe` block, i expect `before` and `beforeEach` to run before the following Context block. eg.
describe(
describeBeforeContext()
describeBeforeEachContext(
Context(
contextBeforeIt()
contextBeforeEachIt(
it()
contextBeforeEachIt(
it()
describeBeforeEachContext(
Context(
contextBeforeIt()
contextBeforeEachIt(
it()
contextBeforeEachIt(
it()
))))

### Why is this needed?

To add more predictability in the Before hook functionality. To add the ability for more complex test setups with less code. Better readability and ease of implementation

### Other

Currently before hooks seem to jump past the beforeEach in the block eg.

describe(
describeBeforeContext()
Context(
contextBeforeIt()
describeBeforeEachContext(
contextBeforeEachIt(
it()
describeBeforeEachContext
contextBeforeEachIt(
it()
Context(
contextBeforeIt()
describeBeforeEachContext(
contextBeforeEachIt(
it()
describeBeforeEachContext(
contextBeforeEachIt(
it()
))))

- Closes #20147

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

* Disabling `Origin-Agent-Cluster` header for proxied responses to ensure `document.domain` can continue to be set with Chrome v106 and up

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

Chrome is [planning](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/immutable-document-domain/
) to make document.domain immutable by default in a future release, currently targeted at v106. The will do so by interpreting the default value of the `Origin-Agent-Cluster` response header as `true` rather than `false` as it is today.

This PR sets the [`Origin-Agent-Cluster` header explicitly to false](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/immutable-document-domain/#as-a-last-resort-send-the-origin-agent-cluster-0-header) on the top-level runner response, as well as the iframe response and proxied request responses that have a domain setter injected into them. This will allow tests that utilize subdomains to continue to execute appropriately.

Validation is a little tricky given that we're ahead of the game and no existing tests currently fail without this change. Unit tests/comments were added for the appropriate functions to ensure that these additions aren't inadvertently removed prior to the deprecation taking place. You can validate the current changes as well by starting the runner with Chromium 101 and verifying that no [deprecation warnings](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/immutable-document-domain/#how-do-i-know-if-my-site-is-affected) are logged to the console during an e2e test run.

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2022-23647](https://togithub.com/PrismJS/prism/security/advisories/GHSA-3949-f494-cm99)

### Impact
Prism's [Command line plugin](https://prismjs.com/plugins/command-line/) can be used by attackers to achieve an XSS attack. The Command line plugin did not properly escape its output, leading to the input text being inserted into the DOM as HTML code.

Server-side usage of Prism is not impacted. Websites that do not use the Command Line plugin are also not impacted.

### Patches
This bug has been fixed in v1.27.0.

### Workarounds
Do not use the Command line plugin on untrusted inputs, or sanitized all code blocks (remove all HTML code text) from all code blocks that use the Command line plugin.

### References
- https://github.com/PrismJS/prism/pull/3341

title: Enhance Command Group to Expand/Collapse & Pin Log Details
body:
### What would you like?

Currently, there are two types of Command Logs implemented in Reporter today:
- Command Log
- Command Group

Both can display log details, however, the group provides context to commands logged within it and it can be expanded and collapsed. This is visible when using the `cy.sessions` command (referencing Cypress 9.5.4). We need to enhance the command group to support printing log details to the DevTools console and support showing/pinning snapshots if there are snapshots related to the log.

title: fix: avoid nextjs unsafeCache and watchOptions
body:
- Closes UNIFY-1133

In webpack 5 it seems that loaders called with the exact same query are not re-run. 
This creates a situation where the Cypress file watcher is updating the files but the new files are never pushed in the loader. It results in Cypress throwing a (No tests found) error since the spec exists but not in the AUT.

In this PR I disable caching and unsafe caching for the browser.js file.

- Closes #19882

### User facing changelog
n/a

### Additional details
To prevent current users from being impacted by the multi-domain work, `experimentalMultiDomain` config checks have been added in the proxy to prevent any injection/delaying issues for users when they upgrade cypress when multi-domain is released, but aren't actively using it. The goal here is to make sure cross origin behavior with cypress remains the same when multi-domain is not in use.

Most of the code changes are minimal, but tests needed to be updated/added. I added tests for the `SetInjectionLevel` middleware to help better understand what injections are needed in what cases, as well as to test current injection behavior with/without the presence of configuration options. 

While working on multi-domain, we skipped the `captures cross origin failures` test in `navigation_spec` as `fullMultiDomain` was being injected regardless of flag. Since the `experimentalMultiDomain` config option is now set to true for all driver tests, this test was migrated to a system test to test when this option is `false`. There are currently some issues replicating this behavior in firefox under system-test, and the test needs to be updated in the future once a suitable testing method is found.

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3980464/156433624-4d5c54db-a250-4bcd-91d7-9dba60257bbb.png)

title: fix(multi-domain): Handle SameSite cookies
body:
- Closes #19849

### User facing changelog

N/A

### Additional details

For multi-domain authentication workflows, when the secondary domain attempts to set a cookie and the cookie is `SameSite=Strict/Lax`, the browser won't set it since `top` is a different origin. This is also the case when navigating back to the primary domain, even though the origin is the same as `top`, since it's cross-origin and not a top-level navigation.

To resolve this, when a request attempts to set a cookie for a request from the AUT that is cross-origin, we force the cookie to be `SameSite=None; Secure`, so that it gets set by the browser. Firefox won't set `SameSite=None; Secure` cookies for `http://localhost` in an iframe, so we remove the `Secure` flag in that case.

This is a temporary solution for the experimental release of multi-domain support. In the future, this will be replaced with a more robust solution that provides the necessary cookies to cross-origin requests without changing the SameSite attribute of the cookie when a request attempts to set it.

title: fix: wire up scaffolded indexHtml to dev servers
body:
- Closes UNIFY-1004
### User facing changelog
Renames `indexHtml` property for dev-servers to `indexHtmlFile` and wires up project setup to link to generated `component-index.html` file.

### Additional details
This update adds the `indexHtmlFile` option for both webpack and vite dev-servers (and associated plugins). The majority of the changes are system tests added.

These changes will not be breaking as `indexHtml` was only added on `10.0-release`. I added back in the `template` option to the `@cypress/webpack-dev-server` as this might be used by users. Since each dev-server contains a fallback template, the `indexHtmlFile` option is not required but it will be generated for all new projects that are setup via the launchpad.

To be able to system test these changes, I had to change the `@cypress/mount-utils` dependency from `0.0.0-development` to `*` in `@cypress/react`. It's not ideal, but the system-tests node install will fail otherwise since the `0.0.0-development` link doesn't work for system test projects. I explored ways of fixing this similar to how the system-tests node install will replace linked package dependencies with `file:some-path`, but it was adding a lot more complexity so I decided on this route. `*` dependencies will get replaced with the current version when running `npm-release.js` so it will not affect the final dependencies of the published packages.

title: Test runner left panel disappears after the salesforce application is open
body:
### Current behavior

After log in to the application the test runner **left log panel disappears** after salesforce application is open and execution stops without any error report. Application stays open and execution stops
The message "Chrome is being controlled by automated test software" still exists, but there is no Test Runner left pane.

### Desired behavior

Able to automate the salesforce application using Cypress

### Test code to reproduce

```js
cy.visit('https://testsalesforce-as--testsalesforcefc.lightning.force.com/')
cy.get('#username').type('my_username')
cy.get('#password').type('my_password')
cy.get('#Login').click()
```

### Cypress Version

9.4.1

### Other

The following workaround is no longer supported:
```js
    var URL = "https://testsalesforce-as--testsalesforcefc.lightning.force.com/?un=my_username&pw=my_password"
    cy.request(URL)
    .then(() => {
       cy.visit(URL)        
    }) 
```
    
Salesforce has disabled this feature in it's latest release
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000363298&type=1

title: test: update screenshot system-tests flake so that it no longer compares images for uniqueness that represent the same state
body:
### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
