title: [Multi-origin]: Improve error message when attempting to visit different origins at same level
body:
### What would you like?

Improve the [error message](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/8a78b5c127a937df58d96e4b1d1f689416ce387d/packages/driver/src/cypress/error_messages.ts#L2093-L2115) when a user attempts to visit 2 different origins at the same level in a test. 

It should mention that cy.origin can be used to accomplish that.

Examples:

```js
cy.visit('domain1.com')
cy.visit('domain2.com')
// ... more commands on domain2.com ...
```

should instead be:

```js
cy.visit('domain1.com')
cy.origin('domain2.com', () => {
  cy.visit('domain2.com')
  // ... more commands on domain2.com ...
})
```

And this applies within cy.origin as well:

```js
cy.visit('domain1.com')
cy.origin('domain2.com', () => {
  cy.visit('domain2.com')
  cy.visit('domain3.com')
 // ... more commands on domain3.com ...
})
```

should instead be:

```js
cy.visit('domain1.com')
cy.origin('domain2.com', () => {
  cy.visit('domain2.com')
})
cy.origin('domain3.com', () => {
  cy.visit('domain3.com')
 // ... more commands on domain3.com ...
})
```

In the future, we could also recommended nested cy.origins for the second example once they are supported.

title: refactor: change git info handling to happen eagerly / asynchronously
body:
- Part of UNIFY-1206

### User facing changelog
Improves loading of the test runner, by moving git info loading from blocking the GraphQL resolution, to loading when the project loads & refreshing when specs are updated.

### Additional details
Previously, we fetched the git branch & spec list git info as the GraphQL query resolved. This can be a slow operation, particularly on Big Sur, which suffers from an electron bug causing slow child_process execution. Regardless of the bug, we shouldn't block the rendering of the UI on the fetching of git info.

Moves the `GitDataSource` to be more self-contained, keeps a map of resolved spec `gitInfo` which can be used to quickly respond to the `gitInfo` field on the `Spec` type. This info is refreshed when the specs list updates, and we put a watcher on the `.git/HEAD` file to know when the branch has changed. We also refresh the git info every 60 seconds while in open mode otherwise, to make sure the UI stays up to date.

title: fix: add safety check for command.clone when cmd does not have args
body: While pulling in the[ logGroup changes into within in the 10.x branch,](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/20980) I noticed two consistent command failures with the following error: The test flow could be summarized like: ```js cy.get('modal').as('modalAlias').within(() => {}) // within using log group // do something cy.get('@modalAlias') // command replay is triggered which includes replaying the end-logGroup command ``` When a command is replayed, it's cloned and injected into the command queue. When the command is cloned, it pull sanitize the commands args list to pull forward an create a new command. Generally commands have args, but because the injected end-logGroup command did not have args passed, it was undefined and caused this error. title: fix: Fix perf issue with command log
body: - Closes (I tagged a bunch of performance issues that I think this will address) - https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/16130 - https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/8658 - https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/6270 - https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/6388 - https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/15880 - https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/5987 ### User facing changelog Added a new configuration option, `numCommandsToShow`, which can be used to yield performance improvements for long running tests. This will limit the number to commands that show in the Command Log (the left sidebar) of a cypress test, instead of allowing it to grow indefinitely. ### Additional details We already have a parameter, `CYPRESS_NO_COMMAND_LOG`, which hides the Command Log altogether. However, this is not sufficient for both debugging and performance. `numCommandsToShow` seeks to provide a solution that satisfies both performance and debugging concerns. While this does restrict the user from clicking on snapshots past the specified `numCommandsToShow` value (and only if they opted into this), I don't think this is typically needed (when debugging, we only need the last couple of commands around when the test failed) Related docs PR: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-documentation/pull/4431 ### How has the user experience changed? I believe this simple change / configuration can yield huge huge performance gains for users, with little to no risk of regression at all. I ran a cypress test w/o this change, and repeated the same series of steps in a test 1000 times (I just took screenshots because the video was too big, and I also didn't bother waiting to get to 1000). The test was to: * Go to a public todo page * Add a todo item * Delete the todo item * Repeat From the screenshots, we can see that this step started off taking 400ms, and very quickly we found ourselves at the 1200ms mark, a 3x increment from when the test started, and after only 100 iterations. #### Before applying this PR #### After applying this PR (using a `numCommandsToShow` of 25) Next, I applied this PR, and adjusted the new configuration option, numCommandsToShow, to 25. For the duration of the test, the duration of the same sequence of actions did not linearly increase with the number of commands getting run. Also, note that at the 100 iteration mark, this test took /50%/ of the time as the previous test, 42s vs 87s. ### PR Tasks - [x] Have tests been added/updated? - [ ] Has the original issue (or this PR, if no issue exists) been tagged with a release in ZenHub? title: Interrupted `file:preprocessor` child process with disconnected IPC channel during `preprocessor:close` causes unclear plugin error
body:
### Current behavior

When interrupting the Cypress process with `SIGINT` during the execution of a test the following error is displayed:

```bash
We stopped running your tests because a plugin crashed.

Your pluginsFile threw an error from: /home/tom/cypress-test/src/plugin.ts

Error [ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED]: Channel closed
    at new NodeError (node:internal/errors:370:5)
    at ChildProcess.target.send (node:internal/child_process:724:16)
    at Object.send (/home/tom/.cache/Cypress/9.5.3/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/lib/plugins/util.js:32:25)
    at EventEmitter.<anonymous> (/home/tom/.cache/Cypress/9.5.3/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/lib/plugins/preprocessor.js:45:16)
    at EventEmitter.emit (node:events:406:35)
    at Object.removeFile (/home/tom/.cache/Cypress/9.5.3/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/lib/plugins/preprocessor.js:119:17)
    at Object.options.onBrowserClose (/home/tom/.cache/Cypress/9.5.3/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/lib/open_project.js:135:40)
    at EventEmitter.<anonymous> (/home/tom/.cache/Cypress/9.5.3/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/lib/browsers/index.js:212:19)
    at Object.onceWrapper (node:events:513:28)
    at EventEmitter.emit (node:events:394:28)
    at BrowserWindow.<anonymous> (/home/tom/.cache/Cypress/9.5.3/Cypress/resources/app/packages/server/lib/browsers/electron.js:431:25)
    at Object.onceWrapper (node:events:514:26)
    at BrowserWindow.emit (node:events:406:35)
```

Based on the text above the stack trace I would assume I made a mistake in my `plugin.ts` `pluginsFile`, however, that is actually empty. Without a custom `pluginFile`, the error will default to the 'standard' Cypress plugin file (`plugin.js`).

### Desired behavior

I would expect that Cypress checks whether or not the `file:preprocessor` child process is still connected or not terminated before trying to send something on its IPC channel. If disconnected or terminated, Cypress should not try to send something to the child process.

In other words, I would expect that I do not get an error.

### Test code to reproduce

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "cypress-interrupt-test",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "main": "index.ts",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "node --loader ts-node/esm index.ts"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "cypress": "^9.5.3",
    "ts-node": "^10.7.0",
    "typescript": "^4.6.3"
  }
}
```

`index.ts`:

```typescript
import cypress from "cypress";

cypress.run({
    config: {
        baseUrl: "http://localhost:2000",
        supportFile: "src/overwrite.ts",
        pluginsFile: "src/plugin.ts",
        integrationFolder: "cypress/integration",
        testFiles: ["**/*.*"],
    },
    spec: null,
    quiet: true,
});
```

`src/overwrite.ts`:

```typescript
// is empty
```

`src/plugin.ts`:

```typescript
/**
 * @type {Cypress.PluginConfig}
 */
module.exports = (on, config) => {}
```

`cypress/integration/interrupt.spec.ts`:

```typescript
describe('an elaborate test', () => {
    it('can wait', () => {
        cy.wait(10000); // wait to allow us to interrupt the Cypress process
    });
});
```

The SUT is just a simple web server with two pages, `/` containing a link to `/page2.html`

Execute `npm start` or `node --loader ts-node/esm index.ts`.

### Cypress Version

9.5.3

### Other

Tested on Ubuntu 20.04 and 21.10, with node versions v16.5.0, v17.4.0, and v17.9.0. Also tested with Cypress 9.5.0.

The following check is performed before trying to send something, however, it purely checks whether or not the process is killed. The process might already have been disconnected at this point (or even terminated).
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/933e0eb3d427c5e1dac0d6c34d0fb9c01ab30bf7/packages/server/lib/plugins/util.js#L28-L30

`aProcess` looks like this when it passes the `if` above:

```js
{
    ...,
    connected: false,
    signalCode: 'SIGINT',
    exitCode: null,
    killed: false,
    ...,
}
```

To at least make sure that the process is not disconnected this additional check should be added:
```diff
diff --git a/packages/server/lib/plugins/util.js b/packages/server/lib/plugins/util.js
index 8d0e823847..b0b6e19076 100644
--- a/packages/server/lib/plugins/util.js
+++ b/packages/server/lib/plugins/util.js
@@ -25,7 +25,7 @@ module.exports = {
 
     return {
       send (event, ...args) {
-        if (aProcess.killed) {
+        if (aProcess.killed || !aProcess.connected) {
           return
         }
```

You could go even further by checking the termination status through `.exitCode`, but I do not think that would be more helpful in this situation.

fix: aut centering and height calculation
body: - Closes UNIFY-1380, UNIFY-1340 and UNIFY-1446 ### User facing changelog - The AUT will be at the expected scale when the runner launches, as the reporter and specs list width used to calculate the initial scale - The height of the header in the AUT area will be included when calculating scale - items wrapping in the header, message, or opening the reporter will all be correctly accounted for the so AUT remains fully visible. - A 1 pixel vertical border that was appearing on the left hand side of screenshots created with `cy.screenshot()` has been fixed. 👆All of this brings us into parity with 9.x (though screenshots from CT in 9.x have a similar extra pixel on the left, I don't see any issues about this but still seems better to fix than to leave it wrong, especially since the extra border would now impact all screenshots including e2e). ### Additional details We were not initializing the Specs List and Reporter width values from saved preferences correctly when calculating the initial scale of the AUT. This meant we calculated the initial scale based on the default values for the reporter and specs lists sizes, even though the UI showed the correct actual size of the Reporter and Specs List. Setting those values from GQL in the store before initializing the style for the AUT fixes this. Since I was I already in the scale math and was aware of UNIFY-1340, I added the fix for that as well, to get scaling 100% correct. The "extra 1 px border on the left" screenshot issue doesn't have a ticket, but it caught my attention while dialing in the screenshot behavior. The screenshot behavior needed to be rechecked for this PR because changing the transform origin of the AUT and adding the left margin from 9.x would break many screenshot captures if we didn't make those changes go away during screenshotting. Walking through the PR, these are the changes: - add "scales the AUT correctly" tests to cypress-in-cypress - start watching the height of the AUT header so that we can recalculate scale when it changes - clean up some imports in SpecRunnerHeaderOpenMode a bit - only add the 1px left hand boarder to the main-pane to avoid it showing up as an extra pixel on the left of screenshots - fix origin of scaling transforms, and bring over an explicit margin-left that was used in 9.x to keep things centered when scaling. - Reorganize how things happen in the SpecRunnerOpenMode (and run mode) script section, so that the we update the store with the computed values of `specsListWidthPreferences` and `reporterWidthPreferences` _before_ calling `useRunnerStyle()` to give us the initial scale. This was the source of both the "too large for window" and "not taking enough space" category of bugs. - Simplified `useRunnerStyle.ts` a little bit, it exports some values and accepts some params that we just not need any more. - Replaced the old reference screenshots and fixed a typo in the folder name. - Almost got the screenshots into Percy, but created https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1566 for that instead when it seemed to have some nuance. ### How has the user experience changed? #### Old resizing behavior Shows all three bugs - starting out scaled to small, header wrapping causing bottom of AUT to disappear, and starting out scaled too large, cutting off right side of AUT): https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8340719/163070501-d44a3cbd-c135-416a-89ca-a09ccf6149f4.mov #### New resizing behavior Sows that all 3 bugs cannot be recreated in the same ways, full AUT iframe is always visible, and when scaled, the margins and centering are correct. https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8340719/163069583-71bc4749-1bf1-4191-85c0-f17ed9c66f5e.mov #### Old vs new screenshots No longer has that 1px border on the left. 9.x screenshots from its versions of the spec had the same extra pixel, caused by same issue of a border hanging around: ![Screen Shot 2022-04-13 at 8 43 19 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8340719/163183548-d7a79eff-e925-462d-b0a5-8fa48e25ca69.png) ### Testing This PR adds percy snapshots for various sizes of the runner and confirms that we use the value from GQL for the initial scale calculation. These snapshots won't add value until #20604 is merged, since Cy-in-Cy tests do not render in Percy. To manually test, follow the example in the videos. Resize the reporter to much larger or much smaller than the default. And refresh the page. Prior to this PR, scaling should start out wrong, after this PR scaling should start out correct. ### PR Tasks - [x] Have tests been added/updated? - [ ] Has the original issue (or this PR, if no issue exists) been tagged with a release in ZenHub? (user-facing changes only) - [ ] Has a PR for user-facing changes been opened in [`cypress-documentation`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-documentation)? - [ ] Have API changes been updated in the [`type definitions`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/types/cypress.d.ts)? - [ ] Have new configuration options been added to the [`cypress.schema.json`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/schema/cypress.schema.json)?

title: fix: Guard against slow requests in GraphQL Resolution (part 2)
body:
- Closes UNIFY-1206

### User facing changelog

- Improved loading times for App & Launchpad in 10.0, when working on a slow network

### Additional details

Part 2 of the changes related to UNIFY-1206, this addresses requests dealing with fetching remote data. The main change is the addition of a `nexusDeferIfNotLoadedPlugin`, and `graphqlRequestInfo` associated with a DataContext run through a `Proxy`, scoped to each request. 

We assume that any remote (Cloud) fields should return `null` immediately, unless we already have their info in the electron [urql cache](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/cdb4a82fa379062d7f65c19de1014c5ca3ad3e7a/packages/data-context/src/sources/CloudDataSource.ts#L48-L56), we will then trigger the client to refetch. By adding the `graphqlRequestInfo`, we are able to know what the current operation is, and target the client and tell it specifically which operations to refetch, rather than refetching them all. In general, this adds better handling for this specific situation which will be more and more common as we stitch in the remote schema, without needing to define any extra logic via directives client-side, or add additional duplication in subscriptions for each possible case.

- Simplifies the data layer by removing the SSR "prefetching" of GraphQL data. That was mostly added as a band-aid to cover up the slowness of field-resolution, but adds a lot of unnecessary complexity for the value it provides. If the queries are fast by default, there's no real value to having this layer.

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2021-43803](https://togithub.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-25mp-g6fv-mqxx)

Next.js is a React framework. In versions of Next.js prior to 12.0.5 or 11.1.3, invalid or malformed URLs could lead to a server crash. In order to be affected by this issue, the deployment must use Next.js versions above 11.1.0 and below 12.0.5, Node.js above 15.0.0, and next start or a custom server. Deployments on Vercel are not affected, along with similar environments where invalid requests are filtered before reaching Next.js. Versions 12.0.5 and 11.1.3 contain patches for this issue. Note that prior version 0.9.9 package `next` hosted a different utility (0.4.1 being the latest version of that codebase), and this advisory does not apply to those versions.

### [`v11.1.0`](https://togithub.com/vercel/next.js/releases/v11.1.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/vercel/next.js/compare/v11.0.1...v11.1.0)

A security team from one of our partners noticed an issue in Next.js that allowed for an open redirect to occur.

Specially encoded paths could be used when `pages/_error.js` was statically generated allowing an open redirect to occur to an external site.

In general, this redirect does not directly harm users although can allow for phishing attacks by redirecting to an attacker's domain from a trusted domain.

We recommend upgrading to the latest version of Next.js to improve the overall security of your application.

#### How to Upgrade

-   We have released patch versions for both the stable and canary channels of Next.js.
-   To upgrade run `npm install next@latest --save`

#### Impact

-   **Affected:** Users of Next.js between 10.0.5 and 10.2.0
-   **Affected:** Users of Next.js between 11.0.0 and 11.0.1 using `pages/_error.js` without `getInitialProps`
-   **Affected:** Users of Next.js between 11.0.0 and 11.0.1 using `pages/_error.js` and `next export`
-   **Not affected**: Deployments on Vercel ([vercel.com](https://vercel.com)) are not affected
-   **Not affected:** Deployments **with** `pages/404.js`

We recommend everyone to upgrade regardless of whether you can reproduce the issue or not.

##### How to Assess Impact

If you think sensitive code or data could have been exposed, you can filter logs of affected sites by `//` (double slash at the start of the url) followed by a domain.

#### What is Being Done

As Next.js has grown in popularity and usage by enterprises, it has received the attention of security researchers and auditors. We are thankful to Gabriel Benmergui from Robinhood for their investigation and discovery of the original bug and subsequent responsible disclosure.

We've landed a patch that ensures path parsing is handled properly for these paths so that the open redirect can no longer occur.

Regression tests for this attack were added to the [security](https://togithub.com/zeit/next.js/blob/canary/test/integration/production/test/security.js) integration test suite

-   We have notified known Next.js users in advance of this publication.
-   A public CVE was released.
-   We encourage responsible disclosure of future reports. Please email us at `security@vercel.com`. We are actively monitoring this mailbox.

body:

title: node_module caching for binary system tests is flakey
body:
### Current behavior

We generate node_module caches in CircleCI for our binary system tests and share them across multiple jobs. To do this, we hash the contents of all package.json/yarn.lock files within the `system-tests/projects` directory and use that as part of our cache key. However, depending on the executor architecture, the generated hash can differ for the same content, causing a mismatch.

We attempt to correct the mismatch by falling back to a recent cache that matches a subset of our key; however, we do not perform a subsequent install to ensure any missing dependencies are added. This has the potential to create volatility and flake in our build system.

### Desired behavior

We need to make sure that:
* Our cache keys are generated in a deterministic way across architectures
* If we don't have a valid cache, ensure that the node modules are properly installed for a project
* We don't fallback to state keys when we are actually doing partial cache fallbacks

### Test code to reproduce

Here's a recent example showing the mismatch: https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/cypress-io/cypress/36440/workflows/b32ce66c-e33a-478b-9888-e0046b815fa7/jobs/1459760?invite=true#step-112-1

But this occurs for any build at the moment. Whether or not it's a problem will depend on what else has built recently and how recently the package/lock contents have changed.

### Cypress Version

N/A

_No response_

title: feat: Auto-merge config when adding new testing type
body:
- Closes UNIFY-1256

### User facing changelog

When setting up a new testing type, if they already have a project, instead of asking the user to merge the config manually, we can do it automatically in the large majority of cases (basically unless the user is doing something extremely custom, or using non-babel compatible TS syntax). If we encounter an error while attempting to add, we will then show the existing "merge" UI.

### Additional details

- Uses Babel to reliably merge with the config, using ASTs to detect the most common patterns:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress' // or const { defineConfig } = require('cypress')

defineConfig({ ...
```

```ts
import { defineConfig as myDefineConfig } from 'cypress' // or const { defineConfig: myDefineConfig } = require('cypress')

myDefineConfig({ ...
```


```ts
import cy from 'cypress' // (or import * as cy from 'cypress')

cy.defineConfig({ ...
```

```ts
export default { ... // (or module.exports = { ...)
```

- If we don't detect one of the common patterns, but see something like:

```ts
module.exports = callSomeFn() // (or export default callSomeFn())
```

We add via a spread operator:

```ts
module.exports = {
  ...callSomeFn(),
  e2e: {}
}
```

- If there is already an object property matching the given testing type, we do not add to the file:

```ts
export default {
  e2e: {}  // we will not scaffold if we are requested to add "e2e" for some reason
}
```

- If the file is empty for whatever reason, we will recover & scaffold it anyway (this is currently an unhandled edge case)
- Uses [babel-plugin-tester](https://github.com/babel-utils/babel-plugin-tester) to unit test the different situations we want to be able to merge, via the `__babel_fixtures__` directories.
- Removes prettier as a dependency, opting to source the prettier if it's defined in the user's project

- `baseError` state will be surfaced in the app now, as well as the launchpad
- a loading spinner will appear when the config has been saved and is reloading, or the config has been reloaded manually with the "try again" button from the error state.


### Additional details

This PR moves BaseError.vue into `@packages/frontend-shared` and adds a subscription to this state in the App. It also adds some more calls for `toApp()` around the same places we call `toLaunchpad()` to keep state in sync.

One side not is that without a valid config, we were not initially able to serve the application at all, which broke reloading behavior, so there are some changes to avoid serving a 500 with an error payload in that situation. With the 500 avoided, we still hit some problems loading the app with no config resolved, so I added defaults for `namespace` and `socketIoRoute` so that the front end can loaded/

### How has the user experience changed?

Previously the BaseError component was only in Launchpad and the browser App would not show these kinds of errors. Now they appear.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8340719/166287918-502b9add-5a8a-4b88-a6d7-7f737986ee0c.mov

The 2nd half of the bug reported in [UNIFY-1440](https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1440) is also addressed by this PR, config values for project ID are now synced in both config and Dashboard Settings parts of the settings page:


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8340719/166306693-627285fa-13e5-4180-ada5-857dd1a8c60b.mov



### How to test manually

With the App and Launchpad open on a project, break the config file by setting an invalid value, or breaking the syntax of the the file. Errors should appear in both places. Refreshing should work in both places. "Try again" should work in both places. After fixing the config file, "try again" button should clear the error from both places.

When the App is open, it looks like config errors are the only thing that trigger a Base Error state, @tgriesser is this correct? I see some other things but they would only happen during migration. I've added tests related to the config state, if can think of other ways to get a baseError, I'll test them as well.

For UNIFY-1440 testing, change the `projectId` in the config whilst on the settings page and see that the new ID gets populated in both the config section and the Dashboard Settings section.

title: Implicit form submission should work when the submit button is not nested in the form, but is associated
body:
### Current behavior

When there is a submit button outside of the form, but associated to the form by the `form` attribute

```ts
someInput.type('{enter}')
``` 
does not submit the form

I'm assuming this is because Cypress is searching for the buttons with 
```ts
form.find('input, button')
```
Instead of searching for every submit button/input and testing if it's nested or associated by the form attribute

My submit button is not a child of the form, but it looks like
```html
<form id="my-form-id" onSubmit={function(e) { console.log('submitted'); e.preventDefault() }}>
  <input type="text" />
</form>
<button form="my-form-id" type="submit">Save</button>
```

### Desired behavior

Cypress should implicitly submit the form on enter in a text field

```html
<form

</form>

title: fix: Long Cypress verification times
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes UNIFY-1600

In 10.0-release, verifying Cypress can take a long amount of time, ~18s on average on my Mac. This is due to a few factors:

* Recent changes were made to optimize dependency loading during boot, but we seem to have been relying on this require having executed elsewhere during initial load: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/20932/files#diff-fd8260e3de42c8cd3e678bac66b13db87507e88b3b4b3919d7463645bc345b28L16

* Electron v15.4.0 recently fixed a [bug](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/32888) related to process termination and will now wait for the run loop to be idle prior to closing (I think, been a while since my C days).

The combination of these two changes is causing the significant slowdown, likely because loading one of those imports keeps the process active longer than it used to. It’s also the root cause of the binary-system-tests flake we’ve been seeing in 10.0-release builds; one of those tests runs verify and occasionally exceeds its timeout.

Changes made here include:

* Adding a require for 'server/lib/project-base' to `server/lib/cypress`. This replaces the `server/lib/open_project` require that was there prior to #20932. I was able to track down the slowness to the missing project-base import that was previously imported by open_project; however, the imports within project-base seem to be interrelated, as far as the slowness goes. I added a comment here to validate the need for this after we upgrade to Electron 18, which is in progress in develop.

* Removing the openProject function defined in `server/lib/cypress`. It is never called at this point and I don't want its presence to cause confusion. If I'm missing a non-obvious place where this _is_ used, please call it out, I can't find it.

* Adding inline requires for electron within makeDataContext and related files; we don't need to require electron initially.

* Updated the mocha timeout for the module-api binary system tests. These tests are exceptionally flakey without these PR changes, but they were occasionally flakey prior to the electron upgrade and even in develop due to verification being somewhat dependent on system resources. 30s was just a little too tight; bumped to 45s, which in all my testing has been more than adequate.

title: fix: retrying config loading errors that lead to new errors freezes initialization
body:
- Closes UNIFY-1467

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

When the app is in an error state, and the user clicks "Try again" and the result is another error, the new error is now displayed instead of getting stuck in the initialization state.

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

Previously, we were not emitting to the launchpad that we had begun initialization again on refresh. This was causing a race condition where the error state wasn't properly being updated on the client. Going forward, we are going to ensure that we are emitting to the launchpad right after initialization and returning immediately rather than waiting for refreshing to be done. This will allow the client UI to be properly updated. In addition, in situations like migration and project, this will make sure that the user receives some feedback after completing the workflows.

While working through this issue, I noticed a few places that could be cleaned up as well. There was some dead code and some code that seemed to more closely belong in other data sources or actions.

title: chore: Updating system test node modules cache logic to support binary tests
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes #21123 

During an investigation into some test flake, I noticed that the binary system tests were not consuming the generated node module cache for the system test projects. While this did not ending up being the root cause of the flake, I figured we'd get it fixed up to limit future confusion.

Changes made here include:

* Updated the cache keys for the state flags to not not match against our partial cache key fallbacks. We never want to fallback to the state cache when we are looking up the actual cache, and this update prevents it entirely.

* Removed the partial cache fallback for the `restore_cached_system_tests_deps` step. We should always have a cache, and if we don't, we'll just do a full install like normal to limit potential issues from the partial match deps.

* Moved saved cache location of system test node modules from `~/.cache/cy-system-tests-node-modules` to `/tmp/cy-system-tests-node-modules`. CircleCI had permissions issues applying the cache to this location on the plain Linux machine, due to the cache being generated on a Docker image.

* The `cache_key.sh` script was updated to generate a deterministic result when run on different build machines. Previously it was always mismatching on the Linux machine due to the expanded glob results being in a different order. This only appeared recently due to a number of similarly named projects being added to the repo.

Chrome is [planning](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/immutable-document-domain/) to make document.domain immutable by default in a future release, currently targeted at v106. title: fix: restart dev-server on config change
body:
- Closes [UNIFY-1236](https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1236)

### User facing changelog
Restart dev-server when config is refreshed

### Additional details
The component dev-server is killed whenever the Cypress config changes. A new child process is created, but the dev-server requires an explicit `start` for it to actually start since it is a function that is registered on the `dev-server:start` event. This was only being called once during project initialization so any subsequent changes to the config would never restart the server.

This PR moves the `devServer.start` event into the config loading process such that whenever the config is refreshed, the dev-server will be recreated.

### How has the user experience changed?


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25158820/165393639-86e36241-c15c-4d02-b1ff-ab0caa6f033e.mov

- Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1547 (epic, all others are sub tasks)
- Closes [UNIFY-1452](https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1452)

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->
 
- Improve language detection throughout app (JS or TS).
- Remove ability to select JS/TS when configuring a project.

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

Allowing the user to select JS/TS during project setup proved to add a lot of complexity and additional surface area for bugs. For this reason, we decided to **remove this feature** and **automatically** detect JS/TS, defaulting to JS if we are unsure. 

The [full technical brief is here](https://github.com/cypress-io/tech-briefs/pull/22) and explains the how and why behind this decision. You should read it before reviewing this PR.

The detected language (JS or TS) is used for initial scaffolding (`cypress.config.js`, etc), migrating (`cypress.json` -> `cypress.config`) and the type of file we create when scaffolding a new spec from within the runner.

### How has the user experience changed?
<!-- Provide before and after examples of the change.
Screenshots or GIFs are preferred. -->

- No longer show a "select language" screen
- Identify language type based on algorithm (see [technical brief](https://github.com/cypress-io/tech-briefs/pull/22))

* Removed `experimentalSessionSupport` Flag
* Added `experimentalSessionAndOrigin` Flag containing:
  * All features from the experimentalSessionSupportFlag
  * A new Cypress command called `origin` which allows users to run commands within multiple origins from a single test.  
  * Cross-domain requests will no longer fail immediately, but instead, time out based on `pageLoadTimeout`.
  * Tests will no longer wait on page loads before moving on to the next test.

### Additional details
The goal of this PR is to merge `develop` containing the `cy.origin` command and a few other updates, into `10.0`. For original PR into `develop`, please see #18075. To recap important changes in the development environment:

* Driver integration tests in CI now have two jobs per browser:
    * 1 each with `experimentalSessionAndOrigin` off (with the tests restructured to use a visit between tests to be compatible with sessions). The `cy.origin` tests are not run in this job
    * 1 each with  `experimentalSessionAndOrigin` on with `cy.origin` tests run in this job. When this feature becomes GA, the goal is to consolidate back into 1 integration job per browser.


For merging with 10.0, main conflicts/changes from the `develop` branch into `10.0`:

### Driver

* Test file restructuring (from `integration` to `e2e` and following `*.cy.js` paradigm over `*.spec.js`) and various snapshot updates. Also updating tests that look for `cypress.json` to look for new `cypress.config.js` paradigm.
* Renaming `createSpecIframe` to generic `addIframe` as we need to now add multiple iframes to create the spec bridges for `cy.origin`.

### Runner / App

* In `develop`, we were able to reference `Cypress` to remove/create the iframes and inject them into the page. Since it doesn't look to be instantiated yet, the same functionality has been replaced with native DOM methods. 
* Moving all the logic from the old `runner` -> `app` that is AUT/iframe/event driven:
    * `event-manager` (new websocket/communicator methods, screenshot methods (NEEDS TO BE VERIFIED)
    * `aut-iframe`  changes for cross origin snapshotting behavior and removal of snapshot responsibilities (NEEDS TO BE VERIFIED)
    * `iframe-model` changes for cross origin snapshotting behavior

### Server / Data-Context

* Addition of `remoteStates` concept needs to be consumed by the `data-context` package when serving the app. `runner.serve` is no longer used in `10.0` and `makeServeConfig` is the method where `remoteStates` likely needs to be reset. When the config is served, `remote` should otherwise be set to `current`.
* CRI client changes to account for frame tree updates to attach `X-Cypress-Is-AUT-Frame` header to inform the server to inject the cross origin driver, as well as passing the feature flag into the CDP automation static constructor.
* IMPORTANT: Resolving the to `runner` directory in e2e mode and the `runner-ct` directory otherwise to make sure the runner routes can serve the cross origin bundle. (THIS NEEDS TO BE VERIFIED IF THIS CHANGE IS CORRECT)

title: fix: automation disconnected error appearing when switching browsers
body:
- Closes [UNIFY-1638](https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1638)

### User facing changelog
Fixes a bug where switching to another browser that opens quickly can catch the `automation:disconnected` event from the previously closed browser

### Additional details
There was a race condition where switching from one browser to another would surface the `automation:disconnected` event if the new browser can open quickly. I was only able to reproduce this when switching to Electron since Electron can open so quickly, but it could likely happen to any browser if your machine is fast enough.

This PR compares the last browser that was opened to the currently active browser. If we have a new browser, we can safely ignore the disconnect event. What was happening was that the user could switch to Electron and be running a test before the disconnect event from the other browser was fired. It would then emit a message to the frontend that the automation disconnected, and the event manager for the new browser would intercept this message and cause the app to think it's in a broken state.

We reuse the same socket connection when switching browsers, so I couldn't remove the listeners or restart the socket.

title: fix: reporter resizing in small viewports and AUT scaling when specs list is open
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1471

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

This PR fixes three issues:

1. A previously harmless issue with the reactivity of how the `isSpecsListOpen` value was revealed by #21103. It meant when the specs list was closed by default, expanding it didn't add the width of the specs list to the scaling math, so the AUT would get cut off.
2. In some situations, resizing the window could put the reporter and specs list into a "locked" state, which had several negative side effects.
3. The handle for resizing the inline specs list had become harder to "grab" as it was only active on the left hand side, due to some z-indexes changing that placed it below the reporter in the stacking order.

### Additional details

[Loom demo of the changes in this PR](https://www.loom.com/share/255baa2019164dc6b2811127cf8aaf37).

To solve the first issue, we now access the `isSpecsListOpen` via `runnerUIStore.isSpecsListOpen` in the `useRunnerStyle` composable, instead of destructuring it. This maintains its reactivity. 

To solve the second issue, without disrupting the idea that the panels in the runner should have some minimum widths, required some changes. We now check if the window size is too small for the content, and if so, allow some scrolling so that users can always find the AUT and adjust the reporter size if they don't have much room. 

There were some side effects of allowing overflow in the resizable panel system, so there are some CSS class changes to keep the visual appearance of everything correct, and also some general removal of unused code.

Reacting the the window size and updating the minimum allowed widths when the window is small meant adding some new values to the `runner-constants` file.

Some tests have been added that open and close the specs list and reduce the viewport size to test scrolling. In the absence of visual regression testing for this part of the app, I wanted to add a visibility-based check, and did create something that put elements in all corners of the iframe (example screenshot below). But visibility checks appeared to run _in the context of the iframe_ so would pass even if the iframe was outside the parent viewport.

![Screen Shot 2022-04-27 at 6 53 32 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8340719/165876949-f1238f4a-9ab1-4dce-8703-de50283a3a45.png)

That said, doing that exercise and some other testing persuaded me that validating the displayed scale % was failing in all the places I would have wanted the visibility checks to fail, so the % values should be helpful going forward. Tests have been updated to include more opening and closing the specs lists, which would have caught the regression.

### How has the user experience changed?

The user can now recover better in very small windows, or at least figure out what's going on with the help of scrolling. The AUT is scaled correctly in all cases I could find.

### How to test

Open any spec and try any combination of dragging, opening, closing, resizing, refreshing, etc that you can think of that could put the scaling or the UI in to a bad state.

Very open to feedback on the readability of the calculations to somebody with fresh eyes. Is is easy to follow? Would you be comfortable making changes to this?

title: .type() should allow to enter all values that can be typed manually to an input field (valid/invalid)
body:
### What would you like?

I would like .**type()** to support entering invalid values if invalid values can be entered manually to an input field (because of some issue with the field/application)
Using the **cypress real events** plugin (**.realType()**) we can replicate the manual behavior of typing invalid values, but it won't fetch the typed invalid values. 

### Why is this needed?

I want this because as a tester we want to replicate/test from an end-user perspective. Cypress should support entering all values that a user can enter manually.
In our application, there was an issue where an input field of type number was accepting invalid values ex 'e','24--', '--' etc. Using **.type(),** I was not able to enter these values into an input field, even though the field was accepting these values and I was able to enter it manually as well.
In the screenshot below, the input field with the label **TestIntegerYear** is of type **"number"**, and it was accepting invalid values like 'e'. I used the .**type** method and tried entering 'e' to that field to replicate manual behavior. But the .**type()** was not able to enter 'e'. So I used **.realType()** from real events plugin. Using **realType()** I was able to enter the invalid value 'e' but while fetching I was getting an empty string ''. Cypress was not able to fetch that entered invalid value. resulting in assertion getting passed.

**cy.get('locator').clear().focus().realType('e');
cy.get('locator').should('have.value', '');**

![cypress  type()](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/72487913/165949924-eacb53a1-23f1-4617-97c1-3db820be8d51.png)



### Other

cy.get('locator').should('have.value', '');

This assertion was getting passed since the value typed using realType() - 'e' was not returned.

title: fix: moving away from runner and disconnecting websockets stops listening for changes to webpack build
body:
- Closes UNIFY-1651

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

In component testing, when the user moves away from the spec runner (for example to the Runs page) and then goes back to the spec runner, reruns due to webpack dev server recompilations will now properly reset the state of the reporter.

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

The steps to recreate this issue were:

1. Launch the app and run a component test
2. Click the runs tab
3. Go back to the spec list tab
4. Run the component test from step 1 again
5. Put your computer to sleep
6. Wake the computer
7. Modify the test in step 1
8. The test re-runs but the spec totals don't reset

What ends up happening in this flow is we [set up the websocket](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/app/src/runner/index.ts#L38-L44) and [on connection](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/server/lib/socket-base.ts#L315-L325) we set up the server to join the `runner` room. When we [move away](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/app/src/runner/unifiedRunner.ts#L18) from the spec list tab, we [teardown](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/app/src/runner/index.ts#L182) the event manager and [turn off](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/app/src/runner/event-manager.ts#L590) all websocket events. When we return to the spec list tab, we [turn on](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/app/src/runner/event-manager.ts#L67) all websocket events again except for the initial connection event. When the computer goes to sleep, the websocket connection is killed, and when it is reestablished, the connection event doesn't fire again and thus we never join the `runner` room again. Thus, when we modify a test file and recompile the webpack bundle, the `runner` channel is [notified](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/server/lib/socket-ct.ts#L19-L21), but nothing is listening on the client. Thus, the [event manager](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/app/src/runner/event-manager.ts#L146) is not notified and the reporter is not [reset](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/app/src/runner/event-manager.ts#L615).

To fix this, we should ensure that we are setting up the `connect` listener along with the other listeners in `addGlobalListeners`. We only do this if that event is not already set up. This flow is broken only in component testing, but I added a corresponding test in e2e as well to ensure that flow stays stable as well.

In addition on this PR, we clean up some dead code that was discovered.

Screenshots or GIFs are preferred. -->

title: Succeeds finding a button but says it's not visible
body:
### Current behavior

Cypress finds the button I want to click. It is visible on the snapshot and highlighted when hovering the corresponding line of test in the left part.

However, it says "This element is not visible" despite it being really visible and even highlighted by Cypress.

The next step, .click(), times out.

### Desired behavior

Cypress should see a button or any other element which is unquestionably visible

### Test code to reproduce

Unfortunately I can't provide a test URL or the full code to reproduce, because the app is under development and not yet released. But whatever the code is, the button **is** visible and clickable, both in the browser and in the Cypress snapshot.

Basically the two problematic lines of code are : 

```
await cy.get("button[data-test-id=editSearch]").should('exist'); // --> Passes but says the button is not visible
await cy.get("button[data-test-id=editSearch]").click(); // --> Fails

// alternative :
await cy.get("button[data-test-id=editSearch]").trigger("click"); // --> Also fails, same timeout
```
![2022-05-02_144207](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3706912/166237539-5d5e8370-ef56-4a53-bba3-c194946a04b5.png)



### Cypress Version

9.5.0

### Other

I had opened a similar issue abour a year ago, with all the material I could find to troubleshoot it, which was never addressed and apparently diappeared. Back then, Cypress failed to see checkboxes, despite them totally being present and visible on the snapshot. This made me abandon working with Cypress. I'm giving it another go, and again I'm getting the same problem with a button.

title: Cannot check existence on a chained query
body:
### Current behavior

It should be possible to do:
```ts
cy.get('#does-not-exist').contains('alksjdflkasjdflkajsdf').should('not.exist')
```

But it fails with:
> Timed out retrying after 4000ms: Expected to find element: #does-not-exist, but never found it.

### Desired behavior

This test should pass.

### Test code to reproduce

https://github.com/steinybot/cypress/tree/bug/chained-query-existence

### Cypress Version

9.6.0

### Other

Why does `getUpcomingAssertions` break on the first command that is not an assertion or utility? It seems like this ought to check for any assertion.

I feel like the existence check in the query is a mistake. Why not have this in a command which actually needs the element rather than this awkward lookahead thing? For example, in:
```
cy.get('#foo').click()
```
I would expect `click` to make sure it exists not `get`.

title: chore: Distribute tests to desktop-gui containers. Make `desktop-gui` tests faster!
body:
- Related with #21304
- Closes #21318

### User facing changelog

N/A. It's an internal CI change. 

### Additional details

#### Why was this change necessary? 

For some reason, a test in `settings_spec.js` of `desktop-gui` CI failed on all recent PRs of mine (#21286, #21285, #21197, #21283). So, I tested it with #21304 that it happens with an empty commit. 

I investigated this failure and learned that it's a flaky test and run 7 times ([5 passed, 2 failed](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/cypress-io/cypress/37258/workflows/fa6c4589-3ccc-4dc6-9761-56419cd602a5/jobs/1498481/parallel-runs/0?filterBy=FAILED)). Because each container of desktop-gui is running all of the desktop-gui tests. 

It was the reason why `desktop-gui` is always super late to finish.

And it can cause unwanted flakiness.

#### What is affected by this change?

N/A

#### Any implementation details to explain?

* I distributed tests to the containers. Currently, each container runs 3 test suites. 
* I used the code at driver tests.
* It's much faster to run CI. `desktop-gui` finishes before others.

title: Handle Aliases in cy.origin callback
body:
### What would you like?
Handle `cy.intercept` aliases within `cy.origin`.

```
cy.intercept('welcome.html').as('welcome')

cy.origin('http://www.foobar.com:3500', () => {
  cy.visit('/')
  cy.get('button[data-cy="go-to-welcome"]').click()
  cy.wait('@welcome').its('response.url').should('contain', 'welcome.html')
})
```

### Why is this needed? 
Allows user to wait for intercepted requests within `cy.origin`.

title: CI: Builds from external contributors duplicate tests run across mutliple machines
body:
### Current behavior

When a build is created by an external contributor, the tests are not split up across the machines due to them not having access to the record keys. We still parallelize the job (up to 7 machines) which means we are using up CI time and increasing the likelihood that the job fails due to flake.

### Desired behavior

We should not be parallelizing jobs if the tests cannot be split up, or we should use our own logic for splitting the tests across machines

### Test code to reproduce

Check out a build from an external contributor e.g. https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/cypress-io/cypress/37271/workflows/1ad10bf4-86c3-4bff-bad8-044b3952ad4b/jobs/1499238/parallel-runs/5?filterBy=ALL

title: fix: issue with generating cypress.config.js in projects with type of module
body: - Closes UNIFY-1669 ### User facing changelog Projects that don't use typescript and have a type of `module` will now have their `cypress.config.js` file properly scaffolded ### Additional details Previously, projects that don't use typescript and have a type of `module` would generate a `cypress.config.js` using `require` and `module.exports` syntax which is invalid for those types of projects. The following error is generated: ``` [cy:open:dev:10207]: ▲ [WARNING] The CommonJS "module" variable is treated as a global variable in an ECMAScript module and may not work as expected [cy:open:dev:10207]: [cy:open:dev:10207]: cypress/plugins/index.js:19:0: [cy:open:dev:10207]: 19 │ module.exports = (on, config) => { [cy:open:dev:10207]: ╵ ~~~~~~ [cy:open:dev:10207]: [cy:open:dev:10207]: This file is considered to be an ECMAScript module because the enclosing "package.json" file sets the type of this file to "module": [cy:open:dev:10207]: [cy:open:dev:10207]: package.json:19:10: [cy:open:dev:10207]: 19 │ "type": "module" [cy:open:dev:10207]: ╵ ~~~~~~~~ ``` To fix this, we will need to flag projects that are set up with a type of `module`. When a project is flagged that way, we will ensure to use the `import`/`export default` syntax when generating a new `cypress.config` file. In the process of fixing this, I also noticed that migrating a legacy `module` type project with a plugin file runs into a problem since we try to require the plugin file in `run_require_async_child`. To fix this, we will fallback to the import syntax on error which is something we are already doing when loading in the config file itself. ### How has the user experience changed? title: Custom commands not working inside cy.origin callback
body:
### Current behavior

We are testing the new `cy.origin` command to use multiple domains in the same test. But when we want to use a custom command (ie: one that was defined with `Cypress.Commands.add('customCommand', customCommandFunction);`) in the second domain, it throws the error `cy.customDomain` is not a function

### Desired behavior

be able to use custom commands in multi-domain tests

### Test code to reproduce

```
Cypress.Commands.add('customCommand', () => { visit('') });
```

and then in the test:

```
    cy.origin('second_domain.com', () => {
      cy.customCommand();
    });
```

### Cypress Version

9.6.0

### Other

Using `experimentalSessionAndOrigin = true`

title: chore: Following up on mochaEvent test performance on Windows
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md

- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes UNIFY-1579

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

N/A

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

UNIFY-1579 was logged to track down or otherwise determine the need for increased timeouts for the mochaEvent tests on Windows. More raw data can be found on the JIRA, but to summarize:

* Cypress execution times for similar test suites in 9.x and 10.0-release are comparable on Windows, with 10.0-release generally performing (slightly) better. This indicates that there is not a generalized performance regression with 10.0-release in windows.
* Cypress execution times for in 10.0-release for the `app` integration tests (e.g. cypress-in-cypress tests) are much longer in Windows than they are on linux, even with greater resources available on the Windows build box. Increasing the Windows resource size from `medium` to `large` decreases the delta but does not erase it. The mochaEvents specs are a subset of the `app` tests and are similarly impacted.

It’s also important to understand how these mochaEvent tests are structured and execute. Each test in these specs performs the following tasks:

1. The outer Cypress loads the inner Cypress app 
2. The inner Cypress loads the runner and parses the spec under test
3. The inner Cypress executes the spec to completion
4. The inner Cypress emits the appropriate lifecycle events with mocha snapshot data
5. The outer Cypress performs the snapshot diffing and calls `done()` when complete

As they are written, steps 2 through 5 above all must occur within a single command timeout for the test to succeed. Given Window's performance with cypress-in-cypress tests, it's not surprising to me that these tests sometimes exceed the default timeout duration.

I attempted remove the default timeout increase from the suite and target individual tests that were more prone to failure; however, further testing showed that any of these specs can time out. So I left the increases where they were and with the same duration, as it has proven to be adequate.

Changes made in this PR include:
* Updating the comments around the increased timeouts to more definitively state why they are present.
* Updating the mochaEvent tests to directly visit their spec vs. navigating through the UI. This does not have an impact on their timing out, but it does make them complete quite a bit faster across all jobs.

title: Bundled Node 16.5.0 release is out-of-date
body:
### Current behavior

I've mailed the security team and has been told I could open this as an issue.

The Node release embedded inside `Cypress` by default on release 9.6.0 is `Node` version `16.5.0`, the latest release from Node of the v16 had past security release after `16.5.0` and the latest release is currently `16.15.0`, two releases before there was a security release and there were perhaps more before, see : https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/master/doc/changelogs/CHANGELOG_V16.md#16.13.2

### Desired behavior

Cypress should embed the latest Node v16 LTS release in order to not be affected by 4 CVEs in case the host system using Cypress does not come with an up-to-date Node release.

### Test code to reproduce

I haven't tried to exploit the CVEs, but only users that don't have any system `node` up-to-date installed will be vulnerable.

### Cypress Version

9.6.0

### Other

This issue should have the label `security` added to it.

title: Response body sometimes not displayed in console props for xhr request
body: ### Current behavior The response body is not always displayed in the console props for xhr requests. There appears to be a race condition between the xhr request finishing and the proxy sending the `response:received` event. Proxy sends the `response:received` event: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/aa6f3b8039495ac37ced4ac581129a020ba66fa4/packages/proxy/lib/http/request-middleware.ts#L51-L57 Call made to update the console props after receiving the event: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/aa6f3b8039495ac37ced4ac581129a020ba66fa4/packages/driver/src/cypress/proxy-logging.ts#L336 Console props are updated with the xhr values. However, if the xhr isn't fully complete (i.e. readystate === DONE), then these values are not valid. https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/aa6f3b8039495ac37ced4ac581129a020ba66fa4/packages/driver/src/cypress/proxy-logging.ts#L226-L231 This is causing flake in the following test: ### Correct console props: ### Incorrect console props: ### Desired behavior Console props always contains the xhr response body. ### Test code to reproduce Run the following test multiple times until it fails: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/aa6f3b8039495ac37ced4ac581129a020ba66fa4/packages/driver/cypress/integration/cypress/proxy-logging_spec.ts#L153 ### Cypress Version develop ### Other _No response_

title: fix: UNIFY-1625 Runs tab not updating in real time
body:
- Closes UNIFY-1625

### User facing changelog

The runs tab will refresh with the latest runs & updates to any "running" rows in an interval, currently every 15 seconds.

### Additional details

This PR includes improvements to the overall GraphQL layer in the Cypress app, and combines changes made in two other PRs (#21408, #21412) related to changes needed as improvements for UNIFY-1625 (runs tab updates) & the work @MuazOthman is doing around app/cloud integration

- Adds tests for the expected behavior re: fetching updated runs
- Adds some formalization around the caching & invalidation strategy for using the urql client on the server
  - `CloudDataSource` now manages all of this behavior, and adds
  - Adds unit tests for the new API surface area
- Improves our "pushing data to the client" when remote data has resolved into the query
  - Previously, we sent a signal that something on the client has changed, which triggered re-querying
  - Now, we `execute` the part of the query which has been updated and send that down in a `pushFragment` subscription payload, so the client can update the cache directly
  - Adds unit tests for the `pushFragment` behavior
- Simplifies the remote query delegation, via `delegateCloudField`, removes batch resolving, which we will revisit in future PRs
- Adds a `refetchRemote` mutation field, which will act as a signal to the electron process that we want to skip the server-side cache, and update any values we are requesting
- Patches URQL w/ changes merged in https://github.com/FormidableLabs/urql/pull/2431, currently blocked on upgrading to the latest urql graphcache, see https://github.com/FormidableLabs/urql/discussions/2440

- Closes #21361 

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

XHR calls will now properly display the response body in the command log

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

When the proxy gets the close event for the response, we send the `response:received` event to the client. There is a race condition where this might reach the client before the XHR readystate has been updated on the client. If this happens, the xhr that gets attached to the log will not have a response body yet. To fix this, we will listen to the `onload` event of the xhr call if the xhr call hasn't completed and delay updating the proxy logging response until then.

title: Investigate cy.origin being significantly slow in 10.x than in 9.x in electron 94
body:
### Current behavior

when merging the `cy.origin` work into the `10.0-release` branch, there looks to be a performance penalty for the time it takes the cross origin logs to return to the primary Cypress instance, as well as some UI interaction commands, such as checkbox selection and input typing. 

This was causing flake for log assertions, such as `#consoleProps`, within the `cy.origin` tests. To temporarily work on this, [shouldWithTimeout](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/21237/files#diff-1f5fc5ebd02c5cd35a9903e1df25c1041573b158e073a00519a07b6861c9861cR113) was increased from `250ms` to `1000ms` (1 second) to allow for the logs to come back in time for the assertions to work.

#### Slow typing inside `cy.origin`
![slow-typing](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3980464/167480422-1890d9c0-740a-4808-b94e-d3d5af248132.gif)

### Desired behavior

Ideally, there should be no performance penalty accrued, and `shouldWithTimeout` should only need a max timeout of `250` to return the logs back to the test. Investigation into the performance impact that caused this is needed, and based off of those discussions, a solution needs to be derived. 

### Test code to reproduce

run [shouldWithTimeout](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/21237/files#diff-1f5fc5ebd02c5cd35a9903e1df25c1041573b158e073a00519a07b6861c9861cR113) with a default of 250ms and watch many of the `cy.origin` tests fail in CI (and possibly locally)

run the first test inside the `basic_login.cy.ts` spec and notice how slow typing takes in the `cy.origin` command

### Cypress Version

10.0.0

body:

-->

- Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1728

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

This removes a check for the open/closed state of the specs list when deciding whether to account for the specs list width in determining the available space for the AUT.

### Additional details

The ticket shows the Specs List expanded and the AUT not scaled down to correctly to compensate. This indicates that though we were reacting correctly to the saved preference (specs list open) in the UI, there was a situation where we were not reacting to it correctly in the values used to scale the AUT. The bug in the ticket couldn't be reproduced, but this redundant expression seems like the explanation for what could have caused it.

The ternary expression removed by this PR was essentially old code, and had become redundant, because when the panel is closed, we also fire a `panelWidthUpdated` event setting the client side state of the `specsListWidth` to `0`. This achieves exactly the same thing, so there is no need for the two checks, and it's possible that updating both at the same time introduces a race condition where the cached `0` width got used incorrectly in the situation in the ticket.

### How has the user experience changed?

Before, possible to see this:

![Screen Shot 2022-05-09 at 9 55 11 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8340719/167425828-569a3bdb-6169-46f3-983c-b0550323f47d.png)

After, AUT scales correctly:

![Screen Shot 2022-05-09 at 9 56 16 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8340719/167425992-e524f33c-8e35-4859-ab6d-181348666c8e.png)

Jennifer verified on the new branch that the issue was not reproduced.

body: ### Current behavior Running cypress tests through cypress.run in headless mode. title: feat: distinguish app vs launchpad utm_source when using utm params
body:
Closes https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1436

### User facing changelog

No user facing changes, but onlinks that previously had no `utm_source`, now correctly set a source of 'Binary: App' and 'Binary: Launchpad' depending on where they were clicked.

### Additional details

In 9.x the `utm_source` query param of `Test Runner` was added on the server as a part of `openExternal`. This PR removes that functionality completely from the server, and instead applies the same rule on the client side, in our `getUrlWithParams` helper function, to add the `utm_source` automatically to URLs that already include any other utm params.

Among other things, this makes the full length URL testable from the client side, and allows us to continue having well-formed links with accurate `href` attributes.

This PR covers all links in the docs menu and the growth prompt that's part of it, and any future links that use utm params will have the correct source appended automatically.


### How to test manually

Click any links in the docs menu in the launchpad and app and verify that when they take you to the docs pages, the utm params are present in the page URL and include the correct utm_source - `Binary: App` for the app and `Binary: Launchpad` for the browser.

title: fix: ct testing support for node 17+
body:
- Closes [UNIFY-1620](https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1620)

### User facing changelog
Fix ct apps using webpack-dev-server v4 not working for Node >= 17

### Additional details
Node 17+ changed how they resolve DNS names. Changing `localhost` to `127.0.0.1` is the fix for this issue

https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/40537
https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/issues/10917
https://github.com/chimurai/http-proxy-middleware/issues/705

To test this (using Node 17+), I had to make a few changes to the wherever we were building Webpack. Since we are using an older version of Webpack (< 5.6.1), we have to set `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider` for all Webpack build scripts. Without these changes, `yarn` and `yarn dev` will not work as it will fail with [digital envelope routines::unsupported](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/14532)


### How has the user experience changed?
CT works for Node 17+

Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

### Additional details
After merging `cy.origin` into the `10.0-release` branch, it was noticed that certain `cy.origin` tests were performing incredibly slow in electron. It turns out the root cause of this was the spec bridge iframe being beneath the Spec Runner / Reporter / AUT, which for some reason was causing electron to slow down drastically. In `9.x`, the spec bridge overlays the Reporter / AUT due to how the UI layout is structured. That structured changed in `10.x`, which made this problem visible. We were able to reproduce this issue in `9.x` by attaching the spec bridge after the `body` element, instead of within it. To fix this in `10.x`, we need to set the spec bridge to be within the viewport by set `top` and `left` to `0`. This is verified by a new system test added to make sure the spec bridge isn't shifted south of the AUT.

If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

Fix a bug where non-spec files are included in run mode when using `--spec` with a glob.

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

Previously, we allowed to glob by anything - even things outside of the defined `specPattern`. This is incorrect - we only want to let things run that are within the `specPattern`. This is how 9.x functions. It also prevents situations where Cypress hangs, or gives a strange error, when trying to run something invalid, like an `.mp4` or other non-spec file.

After making this change, many system tests failed, since they relied on the previous, incorrect behaviour of running things outside of the `specPattern`, which is now  uses the `cy.js` (some were still using `spec.js` extension). I updated all the spec files and the associated snapshots to use the new `cy.js` pattern.

I also unskipped a test in `system_node_spec.js`, which was skipped for no obvious reason.

title: .select unable to find option when value given is a number
body:
### Current behavior

When trying to select and value given is a number, Cypress fails to find the option value and fails. However, when it's changed to string, it finds and passes.


### Desired behavior

According [docs](https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/select#Arguments) it receives strings and numbers.

### Test code to reproduce

Index.html as documentation
```
<html lang="en">
  <body>
    <form>
      <select>
        <option value="456">apples</option>
        <option value="457">oranges</option>
        <option value="458">bananas</option>
      </select>
    </form>
  </body>
</html>
```

example.js
```/// <reference types="cypress" />
it('it will fail', () => {
  const selection = 457;
  cy.visit('index.html')

_No response_

### Test code to reproduce

Any test project will do. The thing is to run on node.js v16 with OpenSSL 3.

### Cypress Version

9.6.1

### Other

The change merged in #19977 is not a solution for a root cause, but a workaround. Relying on the vulnerable OpenSSL algorithm is not a future-proof solution.

Now that OpenSSL 3 is becoming standard, it is not viable anymore.

```
$ ldd /usr/bin/node | grep ssl
        libssl.so.3 => /lib64/libssl.so.3 (0x00007f588d549000)

node: --openssl-legacy-provider is not allowed in NODE_OPTIONS
```

The real solution is to update to Webpack 6 or use `output.hashFunction: "xxhash64"` option as described in https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/14532#issuecomment-947525539

title: fix: Ensuring spec file presence prior to webpack-dev-server compilation
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! PLEASE...
- Read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Read our Code Review Checklist on coding standards and what needs to be done before a PR can be merged: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#Code-Review-Checklist
- Mark this PR as "Draft" if it is not ready for review.
- Make sure you set the correct base branch based on what packages you're changing: https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#branches
-->

- Closes UNIFY-1697

### User facing changelog
<!-- 
Explain the change(s) for every user to read in our changelog. Examples: https://on.cypress.io/changelog
If the change is not user-facing, write "n/a".
-->

### Additional details
<!-- Examples:
- Why was this change necessary?
- What is affected by this change?
- Any implementation details to explain?
-->

There is a race condition between our webpack compilation and our emission of the `dev-server:specs:changed` event. When a spec file is removed from the file system, we attempt to compile prior to updating our internal `files` property within the plugin, causing the loader to reference files that no longer exist.

I updated the `CypressCTWebpackPlugin` to filter out files in state that no longer exist on the file system during the beforeCompile phase. This prevents both the initial error from being presented at file removal time and allows the file to be immediately executed when re-created.

title: the experimentalSessionAndOrigin feature should not be available in component testing
body:
### What would you like?

`experimentalSessionAndOrigin` should be an e2e-only configuration option. Later we must evaluate if using session in CT would be valuable as well was what test isolation in CT looks like, if it is available at all.

There also needs to be an update to the migration algorithm to prevent adding this config to CT?

The change may be similar to this:
https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/packages/data-context/src/sources/migration/codegen.ts#L436-L440

### Why is this needed? 

`cy.session` and `cy.origin` are both experimental and need further evaluation on their relevance to Component testing.

### Other

* Only allow `experimentalSessionAndOrigin` within the E2E object of the configuration file.
* Migrate anyone using `experimentalSessionAndOrigin` at the global config to move it into the E2E object during 10.0 migration.
* Throw error if `experimentalSessionAndOrigin` exists within the global config object for the CT config object.
* Document `experimentalSessionAndOrigin` as an E2E config only property in the unification docs.
* Add this change to the 10.0 Release changelog.

title: fix: support loading config files for projects with type module, without esbuild
body:
- Closes [UNIFY-1779](https://cypress-io.atlassian.net/browse/UNIFY-1779)

@flotwig or @lmiller1990 I could use a hand in figuring out why the existing test suite [here](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/10.0-release/system-tests/test/config_modules_spec.ts#L40-L51) does not fail.
